events.name: Sunset Guided Tour
events.venue: Stonehenge Aotearoa, 51 Ahiaruhe Rd, Carterton
events.long_description:
Experience Stonehenge Aotearoa at its most breathtaking — as the sun dips below the Wairarapa horizon.
Our Sunset Guided Tour blends astronomy, storytelling, and the natural beauty of twilight for an evening you will never forget.

Led by one of our knowledgeable guides, this 90-minute experience explores how ancient cultures used the Sun to track time and mark the turning of the seasons. You’ll discover the scientific and cultural thinking behind the Henge’s unique Southern Hemisphere design before watching the sunset alignment from inside the stone circle.

Weather permitting, you’ll witness how the setting Sun interacts with the structure — a striking moment that links ancient knowledge with the rhythms of the natural world.

Duration and Schedule
• Allow: Approximately 90 minutes
• Start Time: Begins one hour before sunset
• Availability: Offered any day with advance booking

events.id: Cornelia Parker-City Gallery Wellington-Wellington NZ
events.name: Cornelia Parker
events.venue: City Gallery Wellington
events.long_description:
After three years of closure, the newly renovated and strengthened City Gallery Wellington Te Whare Toi will host the art of Cornelia Parker. The British visual artist is best known for her innovative and contemporary sculpture and installation art. Her large-scale, immersive installations explore themes of destruction and reconstruction, transformation and metamorphosis. Objects are exploded, crushed, and suspended in a world upended and remade anew.
Curated by independent UK-based curator Andrea Schlieker and City Gallery Wellington’s Senior Curator Aaron Lister, City Gallery Wellington’s exhibition will encompass Parker’s long career as an artist. This includes an immersive sound-and-light installation, ‘Stolen Thunder’. The work gathers the sounds of approaching storms from around the globe and across time. The exhibition will also showcase her paintings, photos, films, and sculptures.
“I have always said this is the one exhibition I want to do before I die,” said Charlotte Davy, Ringatohu Toi Director, Art and City Gallery Wellington. “I have been following Cornelia Parker’s work for the last twenty years. Bringing her mischievous, dark, and literally explosive work to Wellington is incredible.” 
Parker’s work often fills entire rooms and invites the viewer to move through and around the art. Given its physical scale, the blank canvas of the reopened gallery offers the perfect opportunity to host the exhibition. The exhibition will kick off in October 2026 and run through March 2027. 
Charlotte notes the exhibition’s themes are also of particular relevance to Wellington. “I hope that the exhibition and our return to Te Ngākau Civic Square will reflect our city and also help remake it. We are looking forward to opening with a bang.”

events.name: Jesus Christ Superstar
events.venue: St James Theatre, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
It’s a 70s rock musical of biblical proportions, and it’s back. Jesus Christ Superstar is heading to St James Theatre, and Wellington audiences are in for a treat. This production won the 2017 Olivier Award for Best Musical Revival and came fresh off an acclaimed 2023/24 tour of the United Kingdom. 
Jesus Christ Superstar explores the biblical events leading to the death and resurrection of Jesus Christ as seen through the eyes of his betrayer, Judas Iscariot. The story, told entirely through song, explores the personal relationships and struggles among Jesus, Judas, Mary Magdalene, Jesus’ disciples, his followers and the Roman Empire.
The 1970s rock score features lyrics and music by Emmy, GRAMMY, Oscar, and Tony winners Tim Rice and Andrew Lloyd Webber. Well-known numbers include I Don’t Know How to Love Him, Gethsemane, and Superstar.

events.name: New Zealand Cricket: Summer Season
events.venue: Hnry Stadium and Cello Basin Reserve, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
It looks like New Zealand Cricket (NZC) has smashed it for six. The 2026-27 international home season of cricket promises an exciting few months of action across the country. Wellington has scored six major opportunities to see the BLACKCAPS and WHITE FERNS in action. Three formidable opponents are travelling to New Zealand’s shores. The Indian, Bangladeshi, and Sri Lankan teams have booked their tickets for Aotearoa and will play tests, ODIs, and T20 matches against the Kiwi women’s and men’s teams. 
The Indian men’s team will be particularly busy during their visit. With twelve matches booked against the BLACKCAPS, it will be the most internationals scheduled for an Indian men’s tour in NZC history. Fans will get their chance to see them duke it out in all three formats across the capital, beginning with a T20 at Hnry Stadium on 27 October. 
Make sure you don’t miss the WHITE FERNS. They host Bangladesh in Wellington in a T20 and ODI, during their only home tour of the summer. The Wellington schedule finishes with a visit from Sri Lanka for an ODI against the BLACKCAPS on 19 January at the Cello Basin Reserve.   
With games split across Hnry Stadium and Cello Basin Reserve, the city will be bouncing with life. The 2025/26 season saw bumper crowds, and our men's and women's sides are set to build on this exciting momentum.

events.name: Circa Theatre Season 2026
events.venue: Circa Theatre, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Inside Circa Theatre’s waterfront venue, you’ll find two performance spaces. Both offer a smorgasbord of professional theatre throughout the year. Playwrights from international heavy hitters to brilliant Kiwi voices are represented. It also includes programming from comedies and cabarets to contemporary dance and pantomime. 
Before or after your show, visit the on-site café, brasserie and restaurant, Chouchou. It opens out onto a deck, where you can take in views across the harbour. Look up to admire the art installation above. Called ‘Velarium’, it undulates in the wind, mirroring the water in the harbour. 
Circa Theatre began its life in 1976. A breakaway group of actors and theatre practitioners decided that Aotearoa needed a new and innovative approach to theatre. Five decades later, it is still pushing boundaries, making people laugh and cry, and creating theatrical memories. 
If you don’t have your own Circa memory yet, there’s an opportunity to create one nearly every night of the week.

events.long_description:
Overview

Our Leadership & Management Part 3 workshop is a practical skills training course designed for people in a leadership/management position.

Leaders today are expected to be the driving force of their teams. They are constantly under pressure to lead effectively in a business environment that is characterised by constant change. Our leadership and management courses offer participants the opportunity to develop the necessary skills to embrace this challenge and lead their teams through these times with confidence and pride.

Our Leadership & Management - Part 3 workshop is a practical skills training course designed for people already in a leadership/management position, or those about to take up a new role, who want to explore the latest thinking and models for effective management and leadership and build on the techniques acquired in our Part 1 and 2 workshops.

In today’s world, emotional Intelligence is a critical and powerful component of effective leadership. This 2-day course will equip leaders with the skills to become more ‘people smart’ by developing ways to lead with emotional intelligence. Participants will also learn how to inspire their people with a shared vision and align teams to company goals, along with the tools to lead and manage change, ways to become a more influential and persuasive leader and the tools to raise awareness and manage unconscious bias in the workplace.

Course Outcomes

Assess your leadership strengths and identify opportunities for growth
Learn how to become a more inspirational and influential leader
Understand the importance of emotional intelligence as a key leadership skill
Learn how to lead with emotional intelligence, develop leadership self-awareness and become more ‘people smart’
Communicate your goals, vision and purpose with greater clarity, confidence and inspiration
Inspire and align your team to your shared vision and goals
Understanding change and learn how to lead change and growth in your organisation
Apply strategies to motivate and inspire your people to embrace change and strive for positive outcomes
Understand what unconscious bias is and recognise its effects on your people and your organisation
Explain how you can manage your own unconscious bias and implement steps to raise awareness and manage unconscious bias in the workplace

Course Prerequisite: Participants must have a good understanding of leadership and management fundamentals and/or have previously attended the Business Training New Zealand - Leadership & Management Part 1 & 2 course.

For more information or to book: email info@biztrainers.co.nz or call 04 974 8790

events.venue: AREA Meetings and Events, 1 O'Reily Ave, Wellington
events.long_description:
Leaders today are expected to be the driving force of their teams. They are constantly under pressure to lead effectively in a business environment that is characterised by constant change. Our leadership and management courses offer participants the opportunity to develop the necessary skills to embrace this challenge and lead their teams through these times with confidence and pride.

Our Leadership & Management - Part 3 workshop is a practical skills training course designed for people already in a leadership/management position, or those about to take up a new role, who want to explore the latest thinking and models for effective management and leadership and build on the techniques acquired in our Part 1 and 2 workshops.

In today’s world, emotional Intelligence is a critical and powerful component of effective leadership. This 2-day course will equip leaders with the skills to become more ‘people smart’ by developing ways to lead with emotional intelligence. Participants will also learn how to inspire their people with a shared vision and align teams to company goals, along with the tools to lead and manage change, ways to become a more influential and persuasive leader and the tools to raise awareness and manage unconscious bias in the workplace.

To book: email - info@biztrainers.co.nz or call 04 974 8790

events.long_description:
1 or 2 Day Presentation Skills Workshop

Limited tickets available. Get in now so you don't miss out!

When effective presenters speak, they do more than inform - they influence, persuade, and inspire. That isn’t down to magic or your personality; it’s method. With the right tools, anyone can build genuine connection and move a room.

This workshop is for leaders, emerging leaders, technical specialists, and professionals who want practical tools and techniques for speaking in both formal and informal settings.

Short on time? Attend 1 Day (Foundations) for all the core skills. Ready for a bigger shift? Choose 2 Days (Advanced) for one on one coaching and deeper transformation. Pick what’s right for you.

You’ll leave with the tools to present more clearly, confidently, and with the influence your role demands. This is not just for the stage. You will use these skills everyday.

The workshop format

Small group format for maximum practice and feedback (no massive groups).

Learning is adapted and personalised for maximum value (no cookie-cutter approach).

Hands on, practical learning, with easy to apply tools and techniques (no sitting around listening to theory).

The Effective Speaker - One Day Workshop (Foundations):

Tuesday 24th November

A hands-on day where you’ll learn our step-by-step SpeakerMap™ system to plan valuable presentations quickly and with ease.

You’ll learn the principles behind useful visuals, how to manage nerves, and three delivery techniques you can use immediately.

Foundations is best for technical experts who know their stuff but struggle to get it across, and nervous presenters who want a safe, practical reset.

What you’ll learn

Plan engaging content (fast)

Use the SpeakerMap™ to develop a clear Key Message and structure that keeps audiences attentive without overload.

Plan faster, make better decisions about what to include (and what to ditch).

 

Design useful slides (not wallpaper)

A simple but revolutionary way to design slides that support - not sabotage - your message.

Practical guidance on using AI to fast-track draft slides and create supporting documents (and how to avoid creating AI slop!)

How to use PowerPoint to keep you on track without putting your audience to sleep.

 

Keep nerves under control

A proven psychological approach to calm the mental chatter that causes waffling, speed talking, and blank moments.

Build a personal plan to shift focus from “me” to the audience and the outcome you want.

 

Deliver in a natural, engaging way

Three delivery techniques that help you look credible, be engaging and feel confident.

(For more intensive delivery coaching, check out Day Two)

 

Plenty of practice

You’ll practise each technique in pairs or threes - supportive, safe, and highly practical.

Includes

A full day of training

All food and drinks during the workshop

The Effective Speaker workbook

30minute one on one follow up session

Investment: $1,200 + GST

The Effective Speaker - Two Day Workshop (Advanced)

Tuesday 24th November & Wednesday 25th November

Gain all the skills from Day One - and then take them further. If presenting is central to your career growth, this is the coaching workshop you need.

Over two full days, you’ll create a significant shift in your communication skills.

Day One gives you the foundations to make presenting easier and more effective.

Day Two consolidates and extends these skills. You’ll go deeper into content planning, adapt the tools to your real work presentations, and get personalised coaching to develop your own authentic style.

You’ll also learn strategies for handling even the toughest audiences. The workshop is practical, hands-on, and focused on learning by doing - presenting, receiving coaching, and observing your peers.

If you’re ready for lasting, transformative change in your communication skills, the two-day option is the best choice.

What you’ll learn

Everything from Day 1 (Foundations) PLUS

Go deeper with planning

Apply the SpeakerMap to plan an actual presentation that you can give. 

Dive deeper into crafting valuable messages that you can use in the future. 

Rehearse in a way that actually works

A practical way to prepare when time is tight — so you own your words.

Shift from competent to compelling

One-on-one coaching targeted to your specific needs.

Video feedback plus our inside-out coaching methodology to reconnect you with the techniques you use naturally in conversation.

How to use silence, pace, notes, and the remote without looking stiff or artificial.

How to speak with energy and authenticity, not speed and panic.

Eliminate “ums” and “ahs”, look confident (even when you’re not), and create a sense of commitment that audiences feel.

An understanding of your personal communication strengths and the areas you need to focus on for growth.


Handle audiences like a pro

Strategies for side chats, interruptions, distractions, disagreement, and the odd angry voice - while staying calm and in control.




Includes

Everything in Day 1, plus:

A second full day of training

All food and drinks during the workshop

Videos of your presenting and coaching sessions

events.long_description:
Overview

Join us for the return of the PENZ Big Day Out series – our annual opportunity to connect, learn, reflect, and be inspired!

Big Day Out 2026 – Phase 4 PE Curriculum

Every November, we hit the road and bring kaiako together from across Aotearoa for a day of connection, learning and practical PLD.

This year, we're getting you ready for the new Year 9–10 (Phase 4) PE curriculum, rolling out in 2027. You'll leave with a clear understanding of what's changing, hands-on strategies to try in your classroom, and a plan to put it into action.

How the day works

1. Understand the curriculum
A quick look across Phases 1 to 4, then a closer focus on Phase 4: the key changes, structure, progressions and capabilities.

2. Explore it through the strands
Three hands-on workshop rounds, one for each strand:

Workshop A – Movement
Workshop B – Active Participation
Workshop C – OED

Each workshop previews Phase 3, then digs into the knowledge and practices in Phase 4. You'll take home a printed resource from every session (also available after the day).

3. Apply it to planning
Map your current programme onto the new curriculum using a large-format planning canvas, with a focus on flexible planning and a knowledge-rich framing.

Please bring a copy of your current year plan.




Key details

Check-in: 8.45am | Finish: 4.30pm
Includes morning tea, lunch and afternoon tea
Limited tickets – first in, best dressed




Tickets

General: $150 per person
PENZ Members: $80 per person

Ticket price includes Morning & afternoon tea, Lunch and a full day of PLD




Note to Members: Apply your promo code at checkout to activate the discount.

School Members – your MOE school number
Personal Members – your name without spaces
Organisations and Tertiary Members – your organisation name without spaces




Teaching Years 7–10 PE in 2027? This is the one to be at!




Who should attend?
Classroom teachers, specialists, curriculum leaders and beginning teachers. If you'll be teaching Years 7–10 Physical Education in 2027, this day is for you.

Spaces are limited, so reserve your spot now.

Read less

events.id: Ngā Mokopuna Tour-Te Herenga Waka Marae, 46 Kelburn Parade, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Ngā Mokopuna Tour
events.venue: Te Herenga Waka Marae, 46 Kelburn Parade, Wellington
events.long_description:
Ngā Mokopuna: A Living Building Story Tour

Join us for an introductory guided tour of Ngā Mokopuna, Te Herenga Waka Victoria University of Wellington's pioneering regenerative building project.

This experience explores the vision, values, and aspirations behind a building designed to tread lightly on the environment while creating lasting benefits for people and place. Grounded in principles of kaitiakitanga and inspired by mātauranga Māori, Ngā Mokopuna reflects a commitment to caring for our natural world and future generations.

During the tour, you'll learn about the Living Building Challenge, one of the world's most ambitious sustainability frameworks, and discover how Ngā Mokopuna has been designed to meet its rigorous standards. The project represents a significant step towards becoming one of Aotearoa New Zealand's next recognised Living Buildings.

From outside the building and surrounding precinct, you'll hear the stories behind its design, sustainability features, and cultural foundations. You'll also meet staff and student ambassadors who work and study within Ngā Mokopuna and learn firsthand how the building supports teaching, learning, wellbeing, and community.

The tour also provides an opportunity to view Te Tumu Herenga Waka Marae and hear how the marae and Ngā Mokopuna together express values of sustainability, kaitiakitanga, belonging, and connection.

Whether you're interested in sustainable design, Māori worldviews, education, architecture, or the future of the built environment, this tour offers a unique insight into a project that seeks to demonstrate what regenerative design can achieve.

Come and discover how sustainability and kaitiakitanga are being brought to life at Ngā Mokopuna.

events.long_description:
French Pastry for Beginners
A 4-Week Hands-On Series

Step into the world of French pâtisserie with our beginner-friendly four-week course designed to teach you the essential techniques behind some of France's most iconic pastries. Guided by Le Ciel's experienced pastry chef and owner, Shuchi, you'll build your confidence week by week as you learn the foundations of classic French baking.

This progression-based course is perfect for anyone who loves baking, wants to develop professional techniques, or is looking to begin their pastry journey. Each class focuses on a new skill while building on what you've learned in previous weeks, making it easy to continue growing as a baker.

Week 1 – French Macarons

Take on one of France's most famous pastries with confidence. Learn how to create smooth macaron shells, perfect feet, balanced fillings, and troubleshoot common problems so you can recreate them successfully at home.

Week 2 – Choux Pastry

Master the fundamentals of pâte à choux as you learn to mix, pipe, bake, fill, and finish classic French favourites including profiteroles and éclairs. You'll also learn how to make silky pastry cream and achieve perfectly crisp shells.

Week 3 – French Tarts

Discover the secrets to beautiful French tarts by learning sweet pastry dough, blind baking, creamy fillings, fruit finishing, and professional presentation techniques.

Week 4 – Mille-Feuille

Complete the course by creating the elegant Mille-Feuille. Learn how to work with puff pastry, prepare rich vanilla crème pâtissière, assemble delicate layers, and finish with a professional glaze.

What's Included
Four hands-on classes
Step-by-step instructions from professional pastry chefs
All ingredients and equipment are provided
Recipe booklet to take home
Your creations to enjoy and share
Small class sizes for personalised guidance

Who is this course for?

This course is ideal for complete beginners and enthusiastic home bakers. No previous baking experience is required—just bring your enthusiasm and a love of French pastries.

By the end of the four weeks, you'll have mastered a range of foundational pastry techniques and be ready to continue into our future intermediate pastry workshops.

Spaces are limited to ensure every participant receives plenty of individual guidance. Early booking is recommended.

events.venue: 3 Market Lane, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
events.long_description:
EXPLORE THE LARVAL MASK IN A SERIES OF PHYSICAL THEATRE WORKSHOPS

What can your body communicate when your face disappears?

Larval masks are oversized, simplified shapes that transform the actor into something not quite human.

Across four practical workshops, we’ll explore how larval masks can be used to develop physical character, stage presence, movement quality and non-verbal storytelling, while making space for play, curiosity and discovery.

BOOK ONE, SOME, OR ALL FOUR CLASSES

Participants can attend individual workshops or book the complete four-class series.

The full four classes are recommended, as each session builds your familiarity with the mask and gives you more opportunity to develop your physical vocabulary and apply what you've discovered to both masked and non-masked performance.

THE FOUR CLASSES

WEEK 1-TUESDAY 3rd Nov 4:30-6pm, Toi Aro

An introduction to the larval mask. Explore the relationship between mask, body and space. Begin to discover the physical language of the mask.

WEEK 2-TUESDAY 10th Nov 4:30-6pm, Toi Aro

Developing movement vocabulary through movement, rhythm, gesture and stillness. Explore a set of tools that help you communicate with your audience.

WEEK 3-TUESDAY 17th Nov 4:30-6pm, Toi Aro

The larval mask in situations. From embodying a larval character through to creating the start of simple scenes.

WEEK 4-24th Nov 4:30-6pm, Toi Aro

Putting the mask into performance. Develop short physical sequences and explore how the skills from the series can be used in performance.

WHAT YOU'LL TRAIN

Working with the larval mask will help you develop:

Physical clarity — making movement and intention readable to an audience

Presence — learning how stillness, focus and rhythm can hold attention

Economy of movement — discovering how less can communicate more

Physical character — creating a figure through the body rather than starting with psychology

Non-verbal storytelling — communicating without relying on dialogue

Play and imagination — approaching performance through curiosity rather than predetermined choices

FEE

$20 waged · $15 unwaged per workshop

Full four-class series: $70 waged · $50 unwaged

If cost is a barrier to attending, please get in touch. We may be able to help

ABOUT THE TUTOR

John Armstrong is a Wellington-based theatre-maker and educator whose practice centres on physical theatre, mask and academia.

John's physical theatre training includes residencies with Frantic Assembly in London, as well as a year of specialist mask training at Hagley Theatre School in Christchurch with Pedro Ilgenfritz. He has continually worked as an actor in professional companies, theatre-in-education programmes and as a teacher in tertiary settings. As a writer and researcher, he runs Theatre Research NZ

events.long_description:
Overview

Explore anxiety as a signal for growth through timeless yoga wisdom and psychology.

Inspire Me!
Lessons from Anxiety: Using Difficult Situations for Growth




“A crisis is a terrible thing to waste” said famously by economist Paul Romer

Anxiety gets a bad reputation, but it's not actually the enemy. Anxiety is an internal alarm system, letting us know something in our life needs attention. We tend to respond by chasing the next fix that will soothe uncomfortable emotions, hoping the feeling will just go away. But if the underlying thing never gets addressed, the anxiety doesn't either. It just bubbles up in different ways and different situations.

This workshop isn't about adding another technique to your list. Instead, we'll look at how yoga lifestyle and yoga psychology approached this exact feeling long before self-care was a trend, and why that ancient framework still holds up today. Sometimes the answer isn't something new, it's remembering what already worked before and was simply overlooked.

End the session on a high note with a delicious plant-based dinner, dessert, and good conversation.
Meet your host Rasesvari

Rasesvari is an events co-ordinator who loves to bring people together and create a warm and memorable experience. She thrives on connection with others and has a deep desire for a lifestyle of yoga, meditation and holistic healing.

events.long_description:
Forty Years Below - Antartica Show - Fundraiser for Coastguard Mana
The rugged beauty of the Old Man Range in Central Otago is a long way from the expanse of Antarctica, but for a young boy Roger Lusby, the two worlds were connected by the sight of American orange tailed aircraft soaring over his parents apricot Orchard and Roxburgh, Central Otago.

These childhood moments sparked a curiosity that lead Roger to spend a year at Scott base in 1969.

Now almost 60 years later he is touring his show called “40 Years Below” to communities who will have the unique opportunity to hear his stories first hand.

Roger offers a glimpse into what it was like to live and work as a base mechanic for a year and Sir Edmund Hillary's original base.

The evening also features are moving trip tribute to Sir Ernest Shackleton's legendary 1914 endurance expedition, celebrating one of histories's greatest stories of survival.

A seasoned balladeer Roger’s audiovisual show includes pictures, stories, songs, poems and humour to share his experience.

All funds collected from Rogers show go to help fund your local community needs.

Feedback from earlier shows.

Enthralling, inspiring, superb. Informative and enlightening.
I felt like I had been to Antarctica.
I have been to many presentations of time spent in Antarctica over the years, but none have evoked such a feeling for the unique place of peace and solitude, yet mixed with extremely tumultuous and unimaginably harsh conditions.

There will be a $15 charge for this show that will be collected in cash at the door.

“an excellently executed, hilarious and side-splitting bit of nonsense to create tears of joy, all much-needed. Pure entertainment has real worth.” Otago Daily Times 2023

Before Penny Ashton’s Sense & Sensibility and Promise & Promiscuity there was Austen Found. Born in Wellington’s NZ Improv Festival in 2008, this best-selling completely improvised Austenian musical started it all. And in 2026 she is beyond excited to be bringing her original partner in bonnets; founder of the Improvisers, star of LOTR and M3GAN; Lori Dungey along for the carriage ride. Addicted to Darcy? Easily Persuaded? Bonkers for Big Balls? Aren’t we all! Join Ashton (Olive Copperbottom, The Tempestuous), Dungey (The Dinner) and Burgess, as they swoon, romp, and pianoforte their way through Austen’s world. Charming suitors, meddlesome mothers and surprisingly well-educated girls will all paint a vivid picture in song, dance and passionate handholding.

Complete sell out Wellington Improv Fest, Adelaide Fringe and NZ International Comedy Fest.

events.name: Jesus Christ Superstar
events.venue: St James Theatre, 77-87 Courtenay Place, Wellington
events.long_description:
Following acclaimed and sold-out runs in London as well as an extensive tour of North America, the UK, and Australia, the Olivier Award-winning reimagined production of Tim Rice and Andrew Lloyd Webber celebrated musical JESUS CHRIST SUPERSTAR will play in Auckland, Wellington and Christchurch this October through to December, as part of a major international tour.

Featuring lyrics and music by Emmy, GRAMMY, Oscar, and Tony winners Tim Rice and Andrew Lloyd Webber, this production was reimagined by London’s Regent’s Park Open Air Theatre, where it originated, and is helmed by director Timothy Sheader and choreographer Drew McOnie. Completing the creative team is design by Tom Scutt, lighting design by Lee Curran, sound design by Nick Lidster, and music supervision by Tom Deering.

A global phenomenon that has wowed audiences for decades, JESUS CHRIST SUPERSTAR is a timeless work that explores the biblical portrayal of the extraordinary events that led to the death and resurrection of Jesus Christ as seen through the eyes of his betrayer, Judas Iscariot. The story, told entirely through song, explores the personal relationships and struggles among Jesus, Judas, Mary Magdalene, Jesus’ disciples, his followers and the Roman Empire. Originally released as a concept album, the iconic 1970s rock score contains such well-known numbers as ‘Superstar’, ‘I Don’t Know How to Love Him’, and ‘Gethsemane’.

events.long_description:
One of the top singer-songwriters to come out of the United States’ 60s music scene was none other than Neil Diamond. With a career spanning five decades, Neil is behind many hits that have stood the test of time and still woo listeners around the globe. Now you get to hear a tribute to him at The Opera House this November. 
Imbuing long-loved hits with new energy, The Sweet Caroline Tour recreates the feel of the famous man with careful attention to detail. It focuses on recapturing the sound, look and charisma of one of the world’s greatest entertainers. 
At the concert, you’ll hear songs that made numerous top ten lists, won Grammy awards and earned an induction into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame. Zac Coombs steps into the shoes of the original performer and brings his own musicality and showmanship to the stage. Don’t worry, you’ll hear all the timeless hits like Sweet Caroline, Song Sung Blue, Red Red Wine, Cracklin’ Rosie, Cherry Cherry, Crunchy Granola Suite, Shilo, Solitary Man, Kentucky Woman, I Am… I Said, and more. 
Relive an era when songs were written with heart, soul and honesty, and melodies stayed with you for a lifetime.

events.long_description:
NZ Photographers of Cultural Collections is a group of photographers and imaging professionals working across Galleries, Libraries, Archives, and Museums across Aotearoa. We photograph cultural collections from paintings through to scientific specimens, and from intangible culture, through flat copy digitisation to 3D scanning. 

The forum is a chance to share knowledge and build professional networks. It provides valuable professional development that is otherwise hard to come by for this specialised field. We specifically aim to help smaller institutions by democratising specialist knowledge and building a network of support across the country. This year we have hybrid capability, and welcome physical event (paid) online-only (free) registrations.

This event relies on volunteers and institutional support. Thanks to Te Papa Tongarewa for donating the venue and kaimahi time, and National Services Te Paerangi for funding and administrative support and additional travel support for eligible attendees. Kaimahi from NZ maritime Museum, Auckland University of Technology, Auckland City Libraries, Puke Ariki and Archives NZ/National Library have collaborated to organise the event this year.

These contributions help keep costs down, the physical registration fee will help to cover a venue set up fee and a catered morning tea and lunch for in-person attendees.

Online attendees will receive an email with the zoom link closer to the date.

We intend to record the event via zoom. If we decide to distribute recordings in any form, we will seek the permission of speakers before doing so.

We'll be closing registrations for in-person attendees at 4pm Friday 6th Nov.

We have an online network here: https://groups.io/g/NZPCC
For any pātai please email us at: nzpcccommittee@gmail.com

Join us for the return of the PENZ Big Day Out series – our annual opportunity to connect, learn, reflect, and be inspired!

Big Day Out 2026 – Phase 4 PE Curriculum

Every November, we hit the road and bring kaiako together from across Aotearoa for a day of connection, learning and practical PLD.

This year, we're getting you ready for the new Year 9–10 (Phase 4) PE curriculum, rolling out in 2027. You'll leave with a clear understanding of what's changing, hands-on strategies to try in your classroom, and a plan to put it into action.

How the day works

1. Understand the curriculum
A quick look across Phases 1 to 4, then a closer focus on Phase 4: the key changes, structure, progressions and capabilities.

2. Explore it through the strands
Three hands-on workshop rounds, one for each strand:

Workshop A – Movement
Workshop B – Active Participation
Workshop C – OED

Each workshop previews Phase 3, then digs into the knowledge and practices in Phase 4. You'll take home a printed resource from every session (also available after the day).

3. Apply it to planning
Map your current programme onto the new curriculum using a large-format planning canvas, with a focus on flexible planning and a knowledge-rich framing.

Please bring a copy of your current year plan.

events.venue: Te Rauparaha Arena, 17 Parumoana St, Porirua - Mana
events.long_description:
Tū Rangatahi is a free suicide prevention day for rangatahi, run by Te Waka Whaiora at Te Rauparaha Arena in Porirua.

It’s run for rangatahi and led by rangatahi. The day is about looking out for your mates, your loved ones and yourself, and knowing where to go if you or someone close to you needs help.

The speakers are people who started at the bottom and got somewhere. Between the talks there are rap battles, singing and a school choir. The MCs are Porirua community leader Daniel Filemoni and his nephew, comedian Laban Miller.

Local services will have stalls on the day, and Te Waka Whaiora’s rangatahi team will run a quiet space for anyone who needs a break.

There’s a free sausage sizzle and prize draws. It’s open to all ages, so bring the whānau, and you don’t need to register.

Schools and groups can contact Tyla at tyla@tww.org.nz.

If this raises anything for you, free help is available any time. Call or text 1737, or call Lifeline on 0800 543 354 or Youthline on 0800 376 633 (free text 234).

events.name: Beyond the BIM
events.venue: 65 Victoria Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Election periods can be strange times in the public sector.

Uncertainty, relief, frustration, hope, grief, curiosity, exhaustion, or a mix of all of them before the second cup of coffee. Most of us keep moving because the work still needs doing. That doesn't leave much room to notice what's happening beneath the surface.

Are you a public servant navigating change, uncertainty, and the twelfth rewrite of the BIM?

Beyond the BIM is a chance to step away from your desk for 45 minutes. Get some of what you’re carrying out of your head and onto paper, so you walk back with a bit more room than you left with.

You'll receive a small sketchbook to keep, along with a handful of reflective prompts and access to a table full of stickers, pens, pencils and washi tape.

Whether you've been wrestling with 3am ruminations, gone cross-eyed from staring at your screen, or simply need to trade the office air-con for a different flavour of recycled air, you're welcome here. Bring a colleague if you’d rather not walk in alone.

This is a space totally unconcerned with politics and fully concerned with people.

We'll spend a little time noticing, creating and exploring. There will be an opportunity to share at the end if you'd like to, but you're equally welcome to keep your reflections entirely to yourself.

This session is offered on a koha basis. Contributions towards venue hire and materials are welcome, but not expected.

Come as you are.

events.name: What's one financial question you've wanted to ask?
events.venue:
22 Ballance Street
Wellington, Wellington Region
events.long_description:
Overview

Many of us have financial questions we've been meaning to ask for years but never get around to. This is your chance to ask them.

We're surrounded by financial information. Social media, podcasts, news articles, online calculators, investment commentary, and endless opinions from friends and family.

With so much information available, it's easy to feel overwhelmed or unsure about what's actually relevant to your situation.

That's why I'm hosting a small group discussion for people who have questions about their financial future, whatever stage of life they're at, but aren't sure where to start.

We'll explore some of the questions that keep many people awake at night:

Am I making the right financial decisions?
What happens if life doesn't go to plan?
How do I balance enjoying life now with preparing for the future?
What financial risks am I not seeing?
Will I have enough to retire comfortably?
I'm earning an income, so why does it feel so hard to get ahead?

And perhaps most importantly:

What's one financial question you've always wanted answered but never asked?

Join us for an open, relaxed conversation where no question is too simple, and the discussion is driven by what matters most to the people in the room.

events.long_description:
For one night only DUB HUB’s Quiz Night Wednesday is becoming a fundraiser for Tim Cox.

Tim is a dad, husband, brother and friend from Island Bay who is living with incurable pancreatic cancer. Your support has already helped him get to the USA for life-extending treatment. The costs were well over what was raised so we’re keeping the support going to help cover the remaining expenses and look after his family.

Tim, along with a bunch of other Dads, has been on a quiz team at the Island Bay pub most weeks for about 12 years. It started as a playdate set up by the Mums when the kids were all at playcentre together, and the 'Dads team' has ebbed and flowed ever since.

So on 25 November, grab your friends, form a team (or come solo and we’ll place you on one) join alongside the 'Dad's team' and test your general knowledge. Every $10 ticket goes to Tim and his family.

Buy tickets for your whole team in one go, or have each person buy their own.

When purchasing your ticket you’ll be asked to supply a team captain name, This will assist us to allocate tables. If you don’t have a team yet, just let us know when booking and we’ll sort you out.

$10 a ticket,
8 people maximum per team.
Quit starts at 7pm, but please arrive earlier to get settled.

Can’t make it? You can still donate at givealittle.co.nz/cause/help-tim-get-life-extending-treatment

Thank you to the DUB HUB team for their support and for allowing us to takeover Quiz Night Wednesday.

events.id: Shaun Kirk - Live @ Undercurrent, Wellington, NZ-118 Tory Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
events.name: Shaun Kirk - Live @ Undercurrent, Wellington, NZ
events.venue: 118 Tory Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Hailing from the music-filled streets of Melbourne, Australia, Shaun Kirk is an award-winning blues and soul troubadour recognised for his exceptional talent as a born entertainer. His unique talent has not only earned him many accolades but also much praise from fellow artists, such as three-time Grammy Award Winner Fantastic Negrito, who has declared his show as "One of the best one-man shows he’s ever seen!"

Kirk's vocals exude a gritty, soulful depth that seems to transcend far beyond his years, with critics continually acclaiming him as "one of the finest blues voices Australia has ever heard" (Buzz Mag). Complementing his vocal artistry, Kirk's vintage guitar tones and raw grooves pay tribute to the timeless influences that have shaped his musical journey, resulting in a distinctive sound fast becoming his own.

Shaun’s musical journey has taken him to stages all over the world, where he's not only performed but consistently sold out shows, leaving audiences enthralled by his magnetic presence. From iconic festival stages like Bluesfest Byron Bay, where he's become a familiar name, to sharing the billing with legends like Robert Plant of Led Zeppelin, John Mayer, Paolo Nutini, John Butler Trio, and The Teskey Brothers; Kirk's artistic prowess is in esteemed company. Moreover, he's also had the honour of opening for household names such as blues maestro Joe Bonamassa, soul sensation Allen Stone, and the indomitable Beth Hart; further solidifying his place in the landscape of contemporary music. This remarkable journey is a testament to Kirk's unmatched talent and ability to connect with audiences across genres and generations.

events.name: Wheeler's Luck
events.venue: Studio 73, 73 Main Street, Greytown
events.long_description:
‘Wheeler’s Luck’
by Nigel Collins, Toby Leach and Damon Andrews

Wheeler’s Luck is a rural NZ comedy set in the Wairarapa and will run for nine performances from 18th November at Studio 73, Greytown.
Auckland developer, Richard Lush, plans to build a seven-storey gaming and entertainment facility, swimming pool, hotel, health spa, and 18-hole golf course in a local town near you, all at the invitation of the Mayor (a keen golfer). The aim is to inject millions into the local economy and create 51.5 new jobs.

The trouble is, the land has been left to the people of the town according to the will of Nora Cox, not the council - a fact that Mayor Duncan Sanderson has tried to keep under wraps. But there’s no chance of secret machinations in this small town, with eccentric local postie Murray Dickie on the case.

To add to his woes, the Mayor is also having trouble with freak weather and regurgitating sewerage, an experience that will resonate with some Wairarapa residents. There’s a brawl in a local pub that conforms only loosely to legal opening hours, and an annual horse race held on the beach.
So the plot unfolds in this Greytown Little Theatre comedy production Wheeler’s Luck, set in Bell End (a small coastal community to be found in Wairarapa) and coming to Greytown’s Studio 73 in November this year.

The play was written by Nigel Collins, Toby Leach and Damon Andrews, each of whom have significant careers in film, television and theatre as actors and playwrights. Nigel and Toby first performed Wheeler’s Luck in 2004, playing all 52 of the characters of the hilarious and complex plot moving between 1882 and the present day.

Five characters will play all the parts, sometimes conversing with themselves, including the roles of animals and faxes and bells, and swiftly moving between genders. The actors are Egan Tearle, Josh Cameron, and three Kuranui College teachers of music, drama, and dance - Lisa McLeod, Juanita McLellan and Alena-Rose Burt.

events.name: Te Ara Tupua Discovery Rides
events.venue: Switched on Bikes, Wellington Waterfront 15/22 Herd Street, Te Aro, Wellington, Wellington
events.long_description:
Sunday, 15 November 2026 – 2:00pm-5:00pm
Thursday, 26 November 2026 – 5:30pm-8:30pm
Sunday, 29 November 2026 – 2:00pm-5:00pm
Thursday, 10 November 2026 – 5:30pm-8:30pm

$10 Booking Fee- This is refunded in store when you arrive!

Join us for a new and immersive cultural experience exploring the deep rooted history of Te Whanganui a Tara and its surrounding area, uniquely delivered by knowledgeable story tellers on a guided eBike ride on the state of the art Te Ara Tupua cycle way, skirting around Wellington’s harbour. Mana whenua are your guides on this experience, sharing tales of their own whakapapa and lending insight to how indigenous history shaped the area. You’ll explore Te Ara Tupua cycle way offering up stunning views of Wellington and its harbour and stop at the ūranga (landscaped rest areas) along the way to hear stories and observe the wildlife who make their home along this coast. This is a truly unique chance to kōrero with mana whenua connected to the area while riding along Te Ara Tupua cycle way on an electric bike in a safe and supported guided ride.

On this ride you will:

Learn the history of the settlement of Te Whanganui A Tara (Wellington’s Harbour) through knowledgeable local guides from Te Wharewaka o Pōneke, and other important stories of the area.
View and learn of the stunning art at each end of the cycle way, depicting the stern and bow of a waka taua which represent rangatira still protecting the area.
Check out this unique section of cycling infrastructure on a quality electric bike with experienced cycle guides from Switched on Bikes.
Gain confidence cycling a new route

Additional Information:

There is a booking fee of $10 which includes eBike hire which is refunded in store when you arrive for the ride.
Each booking comes with an electric bike, helmet and instructions on how to use an eBike
Each ride will be fully guided by staff from Switched on Bikes at the front and rear of the group
All rides begin and finish at Switched on Bikes on the Wellington waterfront near Waitangi Park. Please arrive approx. 15 minutes prior to the start of the ride for bike fitting and a safety briefing.
Open to riders aged 18+ (or 13+ if accompanied by an adult). Families are also welcome to bring younger children on cargo bikes or bike seats from Switched on Bikes or their own

We have regular bikes, eBikes with kids seats and cargo bikes for those who want to ride with children and an electric trike. When booking, please let us know your height so we can allocate you the correct bike and of any accessibility requirements you may have.

Please contact us at info@switchedonbikes.co.nz for more information

Note: This event may be postponed or cancelled at short notice in the event of bad weather. If this occurs, Switched on Bikes will notify you as soon as possible using the contact phone number you provide during registration.

events.id: Women of Pōneke November 2026 Event-70 Molesworth Street, Thorndon, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
events.name: Women of Pōneke November 2026 Event
events.venue: 70 Molesworth Street, Thorndon, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Women of Pōneke : Together by Design - The Next Chapter

26 November |5pm -7.30pm | Te Ahumairangi Foyer

National Library 70 Molesworth St

Women of Pōneke exists to elevate women in our city, and it starts with connection. We are ambitious about where that can go, and we are here to serve the women who make it what it is.

On Thursday 26 November, we are bringing everyone together for an evening that is Together by Design.

First and foremost, this is a night out: lively, warm and relaxed. Come with a crowd, or come on your own and leave having met someone new. Expect laughter, easy conversation and time to unwind in a welcoming space, the Te Ahumairangi Foyer at the National Library on Molesworth Street in Thorndon.

The food will be amazing and you will leave well nourished. Everybody Eats, the social enterprise that looked after us in September, is providing the platters, and Luna Estate will be pouring the wine. We are paying Everybody Eats the full value of the catering, so every ticket helps a social enterprise thrive and puts our community’s support to work close to home.

The evening also opens a conversation about what comes next. We have some big ideas, and we reckon you will too. Women of Pōneke is working with Kathryn Robinson and Celine Yockney from Verian, who have generously contributed their research and engagement expertise to help us design the event and make sense of what we hear from you.

We will talk it through over a glass of bubbles or juice. We will share a little of our thinking, we want to hear yours, and your answers will shape what we build.

A ticket gets you good food, warm company and a seat at the table for what comes next. All are welcome, so bring a colleague, invite someone whose company you enjoy and come ready to have fun. We cannot wait to see you there.

We know things are busy in the run to the end of the year, so here are four reasons to come:

Nourishing kai and wine: platters from Everybody Eats, with Luna Estate pouring.

Warm company: familiar faces and new ones, in an evening built for connecting and unwinding.

Your ticket makes a difference: the full catering value supports a social enterprise.

A seat at the table: big ideas for what comes next, shaped by you.

So grab your ticket now and share with at least one amazing woman (and/or ally) in your life.

To cover our costs, we are charging for this event. We know that things are tough at the moment for many, so if this is a barrier for you to attend, please contact us and we will do everything to support you to attend. 

Help a woman in need

If you wish to support someone else who may have a financial barrier, please buy one of the "Buy-One, Give-One" tickets, so we can support more of the amazing women of Pōneke to attend.

Get in quick!

Tickets for previous events have sold out fast. For this event we are capped at 250 people attending and we will be updating our social media channels on the progress of the ticket sales, so get your tickets quick.  

Accessibility
The Te Ahumairangi Foyer, National Library is fully accessible. If you are not able to use the steps on Molesworth Street, you will be able to access the venue via the lift off Aitken Street. There will be staff at the door to be able to support and guide you to the venue space.

A bit about us 

Me.We.Pōneke is our signature quarterly event designed to inspire, connect and raise the voices of our wonderful community of Wellington women, and people who identify as women. 

We believe that magic happens when women come together. We’ve seen it. We’ve felt it. And we want to create more of it with regular events that are open, welcoming, supportive and empowering for the women of Wellington.

Come along, bring a friend and join us as we continue to raise the voices of Wellington women and invite you all to be part of Me We Pōneke.

We are so grateful to all of our supporters, especially Steph and the team at Inside Recruitment.

You can join our mailing list from website, thanks to our amazing partner Springload. Check it out here and make sure you sign up to our mailing list: https://www.womenofponeke.org....

We are also on Insta! Follow us here: https://www.instagram.com/wome…

events.name: Butch Auction
events.venue: level 1/60 Cambridge Terrace, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Haere mai for the cheekiest fundraiser known to femmes/thems - Butch Auction 2026 🔥

A handful of butches are donating their services to fundraise for InsideOUT Kōaro and Gender Minorities Aotearoa. The services range from chefs, barbers, writing workshop facilitator, waiata performer, cocktail bartender etc,

Here's what you need to know before you come along, during the auction, and what happens afterwards.

Before the Auction -

Butch profiles will be uploaded on this event page and 04BC instagram page so you know who you'd want to bid for. The profiles will show terms and conditions such as

if the service is available for a group setting,

how long is the offer valid for,

additional costs may apply to certain services;
For example, you bid on a chef and win (congrats!). You have your first sit down and plan out a 3-course meal for a special event for you and 4 other friends. The chef may only offer to cover the first $100 of the groceries so you will need to reimburse them for the rest of the grocery bill.

how much notice to give your butch before redeeming the service,

any other conditions or boundaries attached to the offer.

Make yourself a paddle to use on the night for bidding purposes only, if you don't have a ready-to-go one. Please do not use the paddle on anything or anyone at the event, even if it was consented! This is not the space for it.

Please consider what you are comfortable paying for a butch. You can also consider financially teaming up with friends to bid on a particular service.

Due to limited venue capacity, please let us know if you're no longer able to attend so we can offer your spot to someone else.

During the Auction -

Our MCs will introduce each butch, what they're offering, and a reminder of the butch's terms and conditions before opening the floor to bids. 

At the end of the bidding, the contact details of the top two bidders will be collected.
The full terms and conditions will be shown to the top bidder on the night. They will have 24 hours to decide to accept the T&Cs.

If T&Cs are agreed to -- a group chat between 04BC, bid winner, and the butch will be set up.

If not -- the second top bidder will be notified and be given a chance to review the same T&Cs.

If the second top bidder agrees to the T&Cs -- a group chat between 04BC, bidder and the butch will be set up.

If not -- the offer will not proceed.

After the Auction -

The successful bidder will have a 7-day window to finalise the payment to 04BC.

04BC will facilitate an initial meet and greet between the successful bidder and the butch. This is an opportunity to connect, clarify expectations, and make sure everyone is comfortable with the arrangement before moving forward.

If a disagreement or concern arises, 04BC can help facilitate communication.

If an issue cannot be resolved, or either the butch or successful bidder feels unsafe or uncomfortable proceeding, the offer may be withdrawn. Any refund considerations will be assessed in line with the circumstances, but please be aware that a full refund may not be possible as this is a fundraising event.

A VERY IMPORTANT REMINDER


You're bidding on a specific service not purchasing a person.

Winning a bid does not entitle you to anything beyond what the butch has explicitly offered and agreed to. There are no implied romantic, physical or sexual expectations attached to any winning bid.

Every butch has their own boundaries and conditions, and these must be respected throughout the process. Consent is ongoing, and either party can choose not to proceed.

No SWERFs, No TERFs.

Let's keep it cheeky, respectful and safe for everyone ❤️

Venue is wheelchair accessible with lift access and accessible bathrooms.

events.long_description:
Overview

Explore your creativity through intuitive Neurographic Art and a soothing sound bath, blending mindful expression with deep relaxation.

Meditate & Create
Neurographic Art & Sound Bath experience

 

Please try to arrive by 5:45pm so we can get everyone into the event and start on time at 6pm.

 

Neurographic Art is a simple, intuitive art practice that invites you to slow down, soften the mind, and turn your thoughts and feelings into lines, shapes, and patterns. There’s no right or wrong way to create, and no artistic experience is needed.

Alongside the art practice, you’ll be guided through a deeply relaxing sound bath featuring singing bowls, chimes and flutes. Let the sounds create space to settle, listen inward and connect with your creative flow.

Come as you are, explore without expectation, and leave with your own unique piece of art.

Please stay for a delicious plant-based dinner and dessert afterwards, included in your ticket!
Meet your Artist Rowena

Kia ora, I’m Rowena and I’ve been teaching art to kids, adults, retirees, and folks on the margins for 15 years. I aim to make art and creativity as inclusive as possible, especially for the people who say, ‘I can’t do art.’

Meet your Sound Healer Alexandra

Alexandra is a sound healing practitioner devoted to nurturing healing in both mind and body. She believes that sound vibration holds the power to expand consciousness and restore harmony and balance in our lives. Her journey into sound healing began with the realization of how deeply sound vibration was affecting her psyche, making her more mindful of the music she listens to and the intention it carries. Along the way, she has drawn inspiration from the Bhakti Lounge Kirtan. Their music has profoundly influenced her own sound healing practice, inspiring her to explore sound as a tool for transformation, connection, and inner peace.

Read less

events.venue:
Bhakti Lounge Wellington
Wellington, Wellington
events.long_description:
Overview

Pause, soften and turn inward with Yoga Nidra, a gentle journey of deep rest, reflection and trusting the quiet process of becoming.

Yoga Nidra: The Art of Becoming




Please try to arrive by 5:45pm so we can get everyone into the event and start on time at 6pm.




As late spring unfolds around us, nature offers a gentle reminder that growth does not need to be rushed.

The buds open when they are ready.
The light returns in its own rhythm.
And beneath the surface, so much is quietly becoming.

This Yoga Nidra is an invitation to pause, soften and listen inwardly.

To honour where you have been.
To rest in where you are.
And to gently welcome all that is beginning to unfold.

You do not have to know exactly where you are going. Perhaps, for now, it is enough to trust the becoming.




After the event is over, enjoy an amazing plant-based dinner and dessert, all included in your ticket!
Meet your host Nicola

Nicola of Namaste Nicola is a dedicated yoga teacher with over 20 years of experience teaching across Australia and New Zealand. With more than 300 hours of training with international teachers, her approach is gentle, soulful, and deeply grounded in yoga philosophy. Nicola creates a calm and nurturing space where students can slow down, rest deeply, and reconnect with themselves through practices such as Yoga Nidra, Hatha, and Yin Yoga.

Read less

Since forming in 2021, SONOROUS has quickly become one of Aotearoa's most exciting young rock acts. Blending blues, soul, classic rock and contemporary influences, the trio delivers energetic live shows built on powerful vocals, expressive guitar work, and memorable songs.

Fronted by guitarist and vocalist Lucian McDermott, recognised by Blues Festival Guide USA as one of the world's top eight emerging blues guitarists, alongside bassist Khani Te Mete and drummer Cooper Paalvast, the trio has performed throughout New Zealand and Australia.

Don't miss the chance to catch them now as they bring their unique blend of rock, blues, and soul to the Capital Blues stage.

events.long_description:
Following a breakout run of releases, international touring, and millions of streams across Spotify and social media, PRINS returns for her biggest headline shows to date.
Now based between Los Angeles and New Zealand, the Auckland-born pop artist has spent the past two years building momentum across New Zealand, Australia, Europe, and the United States, developing a reputation for emotionally charged alternative pop, razor-sharp visuals, and a live show that punches far above its weight. With influences spanning RAYE, Tate McRae, Doja Cat, and Don Toliver, PRINS blends vulnerability, confidence, chaos, and high-energy performance into a sound that feels both intimate and larger than life.
Fresh off performances across Germany, Australia, and the US, PRINS now brings her new era MESSY, YOUNG & ABLE to the stage for the very first time. Built around themes of ambition, imperfection, self-expression, and growing up in the social media era, the show combines full choreography, live performance, and the raw energy that has made PRINS one of New Zealand’s most exciting emerging pop artists.
With multiple chart placements, national radio support, and over 8 million Spotify streams to date, this marks the beginning of PRINS’ boldest chapter yet.

events.name: Reel Rock 20 Film Tour - Wellington
events.venue:

Wellington, Wellington Region
events.long_description:
Overview

Reel Rock 20 brings a new collection of films celebrating ambition, resilience and the relentless pursuit of the impossible.

Reel Rock 20 brings the world’s greatest climbing stories back to the big screen with a thrilling new collection of films celebrating ambition, resilience and the relentless pursuit of the impossible.

This year’s program follows four extraordinary climbing journeys: Olympic champion Janja Garnbret sets her sights on Bibiliographie; Michaela Kiersch’s historic quest to achieve the ultimate climbing double of 5.15 and V15; Colin Haley’s legendary winter solo push on Cerro Torre; and Ben Mayforth’s determined pursuit of 5.13 as he continues to redefine what is possible in adaptive climbing.

JANJA GARNBRET
Olympic champion Janja Garnbret sets her sights on the legendary climb Bibiographie
Featuring: Janja Garnbret

MICHAELA KIERSCH
Michaela Kiersch sets out to make climbing history by becoming the first woman to complete the ultimate climbing double: sending both 5.15 and V15.

Her pursuit demands extraordinary strength, precision and perseverance as she pushes the limits of performance across two of climbing’s most difficult disciplines.
Featuring: Michaela Kiersch

COLIN HALEY
Elite alpinist Colin Haley lays everything on the line in a legendary winter solo push on Cerro Torre - one of Patagonia’s most iconic and unforgiving peaks.
Alone in extreme conditions, Haley takes on a bold alpine challenge where speed, commitment and survival are inseparable.
Featuring: Colin Haley

BEN MAYFORTH
Ben Mayforth redefines adaptive climbing through an intense and resolute pursuit of 5.13.
Driven by determination and an uncompromising approach to progression, Mayforth challenges expectations and expands the possibilities of adaptive climbing.
Featuring: Ben Mayforth

Tickets are on sale now at reelrockfilmtour.com.
NO REFUNDS OUTSIDE OF ADVENTURE ENTERTAINMENT'S CONTROL

The band will play original music from his various projects, reinterpreting songs that have until now only been been heard acoustically. Inspired by folk music from around the world and infused with jazz performance practice, these tunes create an open and inviting sound that changes depending on the musicians on stage. Featuring the mercurial sounds of electric bass and Rhodes piano contrasted with the warmth of the saxophone. Hiding amongst these tunes will be some swing compositions and arrangements of favourite melodies.

events.id: Cat Power: The Greatest on Tour-The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
events.name: Cat Power: The Greatest on Tour
events.venue: The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
20 years on from its release, Cat Power’s album, The Greatest, still retains its mesmeric pull. A late-night classic, it still feels as intimate and raw as it did in 2014. Now you get the chance to hear the album in its entirety live at The Opera House in Wellington.   
The concert won’t just showcase this seminal album — it’ll sit alongside favourite songs from Cat’s catalogue over the past three decades. The concert will drift through heartbreak, survival, longing, and grace with the kind of restraint that only makes the emotional weight hit harder. From the slow-burn sway of Living Proof to the bruised beauty of The Greatest, these songs endure because they tell the truth softly.   
The support act for the Wellington concert is Lawrence Arabia. He is known for his sophisticated songwriting and distinctive blend of indie-pop, chamber-pop and psychedelic influences. Lawrence has toured extensively across New Zealand, Europe and North America.

events.name: The Great Southern BioBlitz 2026
events.venue: ZEALANDIA Eco-Sanctuary, Waiapu Road, Karori, Wellington
events.long_description:
From Friday the 27th to Monday the 30th of November, the tracks of Zealandia will be teeming with citizen scientists (that’s you!) taking part in the Great Southern BioBlitz.

A bioblitz is a great way for communities to get involved in the natural world, learning more about the fauna, flora, and fungi living right under our noses. Spend the weekend taking photos of as many different species as you can to upload to iNaturalist, and watch as experts come along behind you and identify what you have found!

And how can we make that even more exciting? By making a friendly competition out of the event with neighbouring cities by having the most observations recorded! Look out Christchurch!

Anyone can participate and contribute to the wider data base of species in Aotearoa New Zealand. We can’t wait to see your observations from all across the Wellington region, whether that’s here at Zealandia or in your own backyard.

Learn more about the Great Southern BioBlitz.

Regular entry fees to the sanctuary apply. Members go free!

Photo: Lynn Freeman x Fujifilm

events.name: Blackout Poetry workshop at 'Oneiric Reality: The architecture of a dream' exhibition
events.venue: 41-47 Dixon Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Join us for an intimate blackout poetry workshop at Blue Door Studios Gallery, held just before the opening of 'Oneiric Reality: The Architecture of a Dream', an exhibition celebrating Latin American women artists and artists of Latin heritage from across Aotearoa.

Blackout poetry is the mindful act of removing, reshaping and reimagining words. During this 1-hour workshop, you will take a page, choose the words that speak to you, and cross out the rest, until an ordinary text becomes something that’s entirely yours. No writing experience is needed.

What’s included

All workshop materials.

A glass (or two, we won’t tell!) of wine.

A first look at 'Oneiric Reality' before the official opening.

The chance to exhibit: If you'd like, your finished poem can stay up and be displayed as part of the gallery exhibition all weekend!

Usually La Esquina workshops are just for Latina women in Wellington, but this one’s open to everyone! We’re exhibiting, we can’t help ourselves, and we wanted to make something before the gallery opens to the world. You don’t need Spanish or any writing skills, just bring your curiosity and some thirst for wine and art.

Please note: The main exhibition opening night begins separately at 7:30 PM.

events.long_description:
Learn to create gorgeous leadlight designs with our experienced jewellers!

This course starts om Fri 27 November and runs for 4 weeks until Fri 18 December, 5.30pm-8.30pm.

Your 4-week block will give you time to learn the basics and then create one or more stained glass projects.

This class is ideal for creating sun-catchers or small decorative projects for beginners, or working on slightly more complex pieces for those with some experience.

Beginners will start by planning their design, then learning to cut the glass, and prepare it before foiling and soldering each piece, creating a simple elegant clear glass starter project.

Beautiful coloured glass, copper foil and leadlight solder are then available to purchase as required for your other projects.

This is a warm and friendly class with excellent support and learning for complete beginners and more advanced students. All tools are supplied, though you are welcome to bring your own tools and glass if you have them.

All materials (glass, foil, and solder) are extra and can be purchased at the studio at a very reasonable cost.

events.name: Cluedunnit | MURDER AT THE MANOR - Murder Mystery Dinner - The InterContinental Hotel -Wellington-NZ
events.venue: 2 Grey Street, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
events.long_description:
CLUEDUNNIT

DINNER WITH 'MURDER ON THE MENU'

Step into a world of intrigue, suspense, and unforgettable entertainment as InterContinental Wellington partners with Cluedunnit to present an immersive murder mystery dining experience. Guests will be transported into a captivating story where secrets unfold, clues emerge, and every guest becomes part of the investigation.

Combining exceptional hospitality with live theatrical entertainment, Cluedunnit invites guests to enjoy a delicious dining experience while questioning suspects, following leads, and working together to solve a thrilling mystery. From the moment you arrive, you'll be immersed in a world of drama, laughter, and unexpected twists.

Whether you're planning a unique night out with friends, celebrating a special occasion, or enjoying an unforgettable evening with colleagues, Cluedunnit at InterContinental Wellington promises the perfect blend of fine dining, mystery, and entertainment.

Guests will interact with a live cast of characters, uncover clues, and work together to crack the case, all while enjoying a delicious three-course dinner.

But beware, all is not as it seems. As secrets unravel and tensions rise, you'll need to decipher the clues, question the suspects, and piece together the evidence before it's too late. After all, where there's a will, there's a murder.

Where there's a mystery, there's a motive. Where there's a motive, there's a murder. The question is: whodunnit?

MURDER AT THE MANOR - The Story So Far...

It is 1929 and this English Cotswold beauty spot is celebrating the life of elderly heiress Rose Stimper, who, in an act of philanthropy, has bequeathed the village a large sum of money and left instructions that the villagers must decide how best to spend it. 

This will be a party like no other. Everyone has ideas on how to spend the money, and the entire village turns out to attend Pokeingham Hall, which has been thrown open for the first time in many years to host the event.

But beware, all is not as it seems. There are dark forces at work.

Enjoy a delicious three course dinner as you question the suspects, decipher the clues and work to crack the case. And please remember - where there’s a will, there’s a murder!


DINNER MENU:

STARTER: gf/v

Sashimi cut Akaroa salmon and yellow fin tuna, preserved lemon, harissa, coriander

MAIN COURSE: gf/v

Corn fed Chicken supreme, truffled portobello plin ravioli, ajo blanco, spring asparagus, chardonnay jus

VEGETARIAN MAIN COURSE: gf/df

Risotto prima vera Aged Acquerello rice, asparagus, green beans, peas, parmesan fondue

DESSERT: gf/v

Dark blood chocolate mousse, with raspberry and dark chocolate crumble.

We cater for all dietary requirements - please select the relevant option at checkout. 

BOOKING YOUR PLACE AT A TABLE: 

You will be seated around tables of 10. If it is likely that friends will be coming along too, it is best to book all your places at the same time to ensure you are all on the same table.

Please note, ticket sales will end 72 hours before the event. 

FOR FURTHER INFORMATION, CONTACT:

Cluedunnit Murder Mysteries: 

www.cluedunnit.com.au

info@cluedunnit.com.au

cluedunnitwellington@ihg.com 




0450 511 945


Where there's a will...there's a murder!

Gather your friends, fire up your brain cells and crack the case!

Dress in the stylish Art Deco period...

...and immerse yourself in the mystery.

The Cluedunnit murder mystery team.

CAT POWER
THE GREATEST. ON TOUR.
Brought to you by Banished Music, Strange News, and Love Police.

This November, Cat Power returns to Aotearoa, New Zealand for the first time since 2014 for three special shows: Thursday 26th November at Auckland’s Bruce Mason Centre, Friday 27th November at Wellington’s Opera House and now Saturday 28th November at Christchurch's James Hay Theatre. Cat Power will be performing her seminal album The Greatest in full, alongside songs spanning one of the most singular songbooks of the last three decades.

Twenty years on, Cat Power’s Memphis soul stirrer The Greatest is still one of the most astounding records ever to be heard, a late-night classic that still feels as intimate two decades after it first blew our minds and broke our hearts.

Support for these three shows will be Canterbury’s finest, Lawrence Arabia, performing an intimate solo set. Expect to hear some old favourites and new treats from his forthcoming album.

events.name: Cat Power. The Greatest. On Tour.
events.venue: The Opera House, 111 - 113 Manners Street, Wellington
events.long_description:
Twenty years on, The Greatest still sounds like midnight.

This summer, Cat Power returns to New Zealand for a run of special shows performing her seminal 2006 album The Greatest in full, alongside songs spanning one of the most singular catalogues in contemporary music.

Recorded in Memphis with members of the legendary Hi Rhythm section, The Greatest remains a defining statement from Marshall: smoky, soulful and heartbreakingly intimate. Featuring enduring tracks including “The Greatest”, “Living Proof” and “Lived in Bars”, the album cemented Cat Power as one of the most influential voices of her generation.

To mark the album’s 20th anniversary, these rare performances will revisit the record front to back, a chance to experience its quiet power, emotional depth and timeless beauty in the live setting it deserves.

Support for these shows will be Lawrence Arabia - the acclaimed musical project of Christchurch-born singer-songwriter James Milne, one of New Zealand’s most celebrated and influential contemporary artists. Across a career spanning nearly two decades, Milne has released a string of critically acclaimed albums, earning an APRA Silver Scroll for his song Apple Pie Bed, the inaugural Taite Music Prize, and multiple Aotearoa Music Awards.

There are few artists who can hold a room the way Cat Power can. Experience the magic of The Greatest and re-enter the orbit of the early millennium in these raw, hypnotic shows in November.

events.name: Oneiric Reality: The architecture of a dream | Art exhibition
events.venue: 41-47 Dixon Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
events.long_description:
‘Oneiric Reality | The architecture of a dream’ is what it feels like to live between two worlds: the one you come from and the one you’ve built. Some of it feels like a dream, some of it feels like home, and some of it feels like both at once. For three days, both live in the same room.


A kind of lucid dream: knowing you’re inside it, and discovering you can choose what comes next.

Work by Latin American artists and artists of Latin heritage from across Aotearoa: paint, ink, photographs, collage, poems. Not all of it is dreamlike. All of it was made from somewhere in between.

Fri 27 Nov: opening night, 7:30 pm

Sat 28 Nov: 11 am to 2 pm and 5 pm to 8 pm

Sun 29 Nov: 12 pm to 3 pm

Come as you are. Wander in any direction.

Photo Mark Coote

events.id: DECEITS AOTEAROA TOUR 2026 - AUCKLAND-Valhalla, Wellington-Valhalla
events.name: DECEITS AOTEAROA TOUR 2026 - AUCKLAND
events.venue: Valhalla, Wellington
events.long_description:
Los Angeles post-punk band DECEITS has been building something real from the ground up. Since forming in 2021, longtime friends Kevin Moreno (Vocals/Instruments) and Francisco Saenz (Drums/Percussions) have self-released their entire catalog, quietly amassing millions of streams, selling out tours, and pressing vinyl that disappears just as quickly as it arrives. Their momentum has carried them from the underground to stages like Cruel World 2025 and across their first European tour, all while earning coverage from Post-Punk.com and the Los Angeles Times. DECEITS aren’t interested in playing it safe. Their take on post-punk rejects the genre’s colder edges in favor of something more alive, pulling in the color, rhythm, and emotional intensity of the Spanish-language music they grew up with. The result is a sound that feels both nostalgic and distinctly their own: moody, melodic, and impossible to stand still to.

This show is at Whammy Bar in Auckland

Tickets here

events.name: Dermot Kennedy
events.venue: TSB Arena, Queens Wharf, Wellington
events.long_description:
Live Nation has announced the return of multi-platinum recording artist Dermot Kennedy, the much-loved singer/songwriter, confirming a string of shows across Australia and New Zealand this November, following his powerful appearance at last year’s MISNEACH Festival in Sydney. This tour announcement follows the release of his new album, The Weight of the Woods, Kennedy creating UK chart history as the first Irish solo artist ever to reach Number 1 with their first three studio albums.

Known for his passionate and powerful live performances, Kennedy is set to kick off a massive international tour, with the UK and Europe starting on May 11, marking his largest run across that region to date, including a return to London’s O2 on June 5. He will also perform at iconic venues across the U.S. and Canada, including Red Rocks Amphitheatre in Colorado, Los Angeles’ Greek Theatre and Forest Hills Stadium in New York, among others.

A Movement extravaganza featuring quick fire 30 minute sets from 7 DJs spinning hot wax all night!
Expect synth-pop, post punk funk, classic early dance, old school rap, goth classics, non stop raging dancefloor bangers!!!

Your host is DJ Matai, known for sets spanning vintage goth, new wave and post-punk. Expect to hear the classic and the obscure. Known for running DIY Punk label Razored Raw and drumming in bands such as No Sector and Maced.

with guests:

DJ Boss Dude- It's your ol' mate, thee space vampire of Newtown, thee headhoncho of Creeps record parlour, thee master of many genres, 80s electronique, synthesizer, Italo-disco, and New Wave.
