events.long_description:
Dutch groove-explorers YĪN YĪN are bringing disco, funk, psychedelia and dance to Wellington’s San Fran Friday 27 November and Auckland’s Tuning Fork on Saturday 28 November. 
Made up of Erik Bandt on guitar, Kees Berkers on drums, Jerôme Schere on keyboards and Remy Scheren on bass, YĪN YĪN are the kaleidoscopic instrumental quartet from Maastricht, Netherlands, renowned for their genre-bending records and transportive live experience. 
Emerging out of an experimental jam session in a remote ballet school village in 2017 that resulted in the making of their debut album The Rabbit That Hunts Tigers, the band have since created another three critically acclaimed albums and spent the better part of the last decade chasing rhythm across continents. 
With relentless international touring and performing everywhere from Fuji Rock Festival and Lowlands to North Sea Jazz Festival and Clockenflap they have been collecting sounds, textures and musical flavours like souvenirs, drawing from a multitude of influences such as ‘70s Thai Funk, Japanese City Pop and crate-dug global disco. Each project has evolved alongside the eager exploration to immerse their worldly experience into a sonic universe of their own.
Their latest of which,Yatta!, arrived in January 2026. A defining influence on Yatta! Is the cosmic allure of Italo Disco - the psychedelic futuristic dance music that emerged in Italy during the late 1970s and flourished throughout the 80s. “It has something of a mystique,” the band explains. 
“Because all the producers were using new recording techniques and effects and stuff like that, but there are not many pictures or videos of how they were creating things in the studio.You have to use your own fantasy and create your own story about how that music is created.”
This one sees the band into their most realised selves yet, translating into an unmissable live experience. “We tried to make a mix of songs that are very energetic and danceable and are party starters, but also have songs that take you on trips and are more easy. People can also just chill and relax and listen to the music and enjoy it.” - YĪN YĪN 

Aotearoa, get ready to move. YĪN YĪN are set to take on Aotearoa for the first time for two shows this November.


San Fran holds a Supervised License. Minors are welcome to attend events at San Fran so long as they are accompanied by a legal guardian at all times whilst at the venue.

events.venue: Meow Nui, 92 Vivian Street, Te Aro, Wellington, 6011, Wellington
events.long_description:
Few DJs understand a dancefloor quite like Marcellus Pittman. A cornerstone of contemporary Detroit dance music, Pittman brings decades of experience, deep musical knowledge and an unmistakable sense of groove to Meow Nui on Friday 27 November.

A true master behind the decks, Pittman is known for sets that move effortlessly between rolling, low-slung house, high-tempo disco, raw techno, funk, post-punk and deeper late-night selections. His approach is instinctive and unpredictable, built around meticulous mixing and an ability to read a room and take it exactly where it needs to go.
Pittman first came to prominence alongside Theo Parrish on Essential Selections Volume 1 before becoming one quarter of the legendary Three Chairs, alongside Parrish, Kenny Dixon Jr. (Moodymann) and Rick Wilhite. He later founded his own Unirhythm imprint and released music through labels including Omar-S’ FXHE, while also collaborating as part of the T.O.M. Project and Rotating Assembly.

His productions carry the same raw, spacious and deeply human quality as his DJ sets, pairing tough drum programming with subtle, unexpected detail. It is a sound rooted firmly in Detroit while remaining completely his own.

From intimate basements to major clubs and festivals across the world, Marcellus Pittman has built a reputation as one of dance music’s most respected selectors. This is a rare chance to experience a true Detroit heavyweight on the Meow Nui system.

Support from Benny Salvador, one of Aotearoa’s most exciting young selectors, blending house, techno, electro, disco-funk, dub, boogie and beyond.

Don’t miss your chance to be in the room.

events.long_description:
After a sold-out tour in early 2026, Sir Tony Robinson brings his talk show back to Wellington. Catch ‘An Audience with Sir Tony Robinson’ at The Opera House. The television presenter, actor, and award-winning writer has an impressive decades-long career. Tony will divulge behind-the-scenes stories from his life on and off screen. He’ll then read from his fiction debut ‘The House of Wolf’, an epic tale of Alfred the Great and the bloody birth of England. He won’t hog the microphone the whole time — you’ll also get the chance to ask him questions. Expect masterful storytelling from Tony and lots of laughs from the audience. 

You might have seen Tony play Baldrick in Rowan Atkinson’s cult 80s sitcom ‘Blackadder’. In the show, his “I have a cunning plan” catchphrase and comedic timing made him a household name. He’s also celebrated for his work in historical broadcasting, which includes presenting 20 seasons of ‘Time Team’. His infectious enthusiasm for history continued, as he wrote his first novel aged 78. The book delves into the (often grim) realities of life for ordinary people caught between Saxon kings and Viking raiders.

events.id: Bike Maintenance for Beginners-Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington-Wellington High School
events.name: Bike Maintenance for Beginners
events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
Bicycle Maintenance for Beginners
Have you recently started riding a bicycle and want to make sure you can take care of it properly? Or have you been riding for ages, but have always been scared to fix anything yourself?
Are you unsure of how to pump your tyres, or how much oil your chain needs? Find yourself fumbling for words when trying to describe that clunking sound to the guy in the bike shop?
This one day course lays bare the nuts and bolts of bicycle mechanics for absolute beginners, as well as those with a little experience. Through practical experience working with your own bicycle, you will find out what needs to be done to keep it running smoothly. We’ll cover what to look out for when things start to wear out, and how to check for problems, so you can be confident your bicycle is safe to ride. You will also learn how to fix some of the most common mechanical problems, and learn about the correct terminology and tools to use.
Those who feel intimidated in bike shops are especially welcome in this course. No question is a stupid question!
Bringing a bike to work on is essential, preferably one that you are riding regularly, because the best way to learn is by building familiarity with your own ride. E-bikes are welcome, although the extra weight can mean they are more challenging to work on. Regardless of whether your bike is in pristine condition, or desperately in need of TLC, it is welcome on the course – bikes showing a bit more wear can be useful for the learning of the whole group.
Bring your pushbike along on the day.  If you have the following, please bring them as well:  A multi-tool and pump; chain oil and rag; lightweight close-fitting gardening or rubber gloves.
Note: A condition of enrolment is that you must provide photo ID when you attend.
(Please note this course is not exhaustive and is not a professional training course).
By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:
- Name most parts of a bicycle correctly
- Perform a quick safety check on any bicycle
- Fix a flat tyre
- Adjust your bike to fit your body
- Oil and clean your chain
- Identify and fix some common brake problems
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

events.name: Eco Dye Workshop
events.venue: Waikanae Arts and Crafts Society Inc,27A Elizabeth St, Waikanae 5036, New Zealand, Waikanae
events.long_description:
Eco Dye Workshop
Impressions of Nature on Silk

Eco dyeing, also known as leaf or eco print, is a gentle, alchemical process where the natural pigments of leaves are transferred directly onto fabric, creating one-of-a-kind botanical imprints.

Join me for a full day of slow making and discovery as we explore this beautiful dialogue between nature and cloth. In the morning, we’ll forage around the hall, gathering leaves and foliage that speak to us. You’ll learn how to prepare and bundle silk with plant materials, drawing out colours and patterns from the landscape itself.

In the afternoon, you’ll design and dye your own silk scarf — a wearable memory of place and season, marked by the delicate traces of nature’s touch.

You will learn

• which plants and fibres work best for this method
• how to use an iron mordant to enhance colour and detail
• different bundling techniques and approaches

All materials and tools will be provided for use during the workshop.

Your workshop fee includes silk fabrics to explore and experiment with, one silk scarf to design and dye, and a detailed handout with information on mordants, dye plants, tips, and useful resources.

A ‘what to bring’ list (including suggestions for clothing and optional items) will be sent out closer to the workshop date.

Booking through my website (see link above)

Location

27A Elizabeth Street (Art and Craft Society)
Waikane
Kāpiti

events.name: Liminal Adult ADHD Workshop (Wellington)
events.venue: 311 The Parade, Island Bay, Wellington 6023, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Living with ADHD can be tiring. Constantly trying harder.

Wondering why things that seem simple for other people can feel so difficult.

Liminal is a workshop designed to help make sense of that experience — and to help you discover practical ways forward.

This isn’t about fixing yourself. It’s about working with how you’re wired.

You’ll leave with:

a clearer understanding of why your ADHD works the way it does

practical strategies you can begin using immediately

hope that life can become easier

Rather than leaving with another list of things you "should" do, you'll leave with one or two small experiments that fit your own life.

What we'll explore

ADHD: why it works the way it does, and why life can feel so much harder than it should.

Emotional regulation: sometimes one of the most overlooked parts of ADHD.

Executive functioning: why starting, planning, remembering, and following through can be so difficult.

Dopamine: motivation, energy, and why "just try harder" rarely works.

Tiny Habits®: a simple, practical way to begin making lasting changes.

Liminal offers education and practical support; it doesn’t replace professional care, provide diagnosis or offer advice about medication.

Who is this for?

This workshop is best suited to adults (16+) who already have some understanding of ADHD — whether diagnosed, self-identified, exploring or supporting someone in your whanau.

However, anyone is welcome.

Come as you are.
You don't need to have everything sorted.
Just bring your curiosity.

Details at a glance

Date: Saturday 28th November 2026

Venue: St Hilda's Church, 11 The Parade, Island Bay, Wellington

Time:

10.00am - Registration, coffee, snacks

10.15am - Workshop begins

12.30ish. Light lunch (included)

2.30pm - Finish

What’s included

Coffee and snacks, light lunch

Workbook materials (new and revamped; including an experiment guide)

A chance to reflect, connect, and further develop your own individual plan

Cost

Individual: $70

Couple: $110

Multiple: Two from one family/whanau: $110

For unwaged tickets ($40) or larger family groups please contact Derek on 021 511 303. You can get an access code to for a group discount.

Some sponsored (free) places are available.

Register by

Please register by the Thursday prior (26th November).

If are signing up . . .

If you have any questions, any information it may be helpful for me to know or requests, please call,

Presenter: Derek Chirnside

Over the past twenty years I've listened to many of adults describe what ADHD feels like from the inside. Again and again I hear similar themes: feeling exhausted, overwhelmed, shamed, huge creativity, humour, resilience, and the longing to simply make life work a little better. Also, timeblindness and hyperfocus!

This workshop grew out of those conversations.

I'm based in Christchurch. I've worked as a classroom teacher, teacher educator (including training teachers to support students with ADHD), university chaplain, and business owner. I'm a long-time ADHD educator with a particular focus on practical, sustainable strategies that help adults live well with ADHD. More information on website

Overview

Come along to this final Think Well Corner session for 2026 and learn how to think clearly, respond wisely and protect your peace of mind.

We've all met them. The colleague who pushes our buttons, the person who always has something negative to say, or someone who somehow manages to turn an ordinary interaction into a difficult one.

And while we can't always change how other people behave, we can become much smarter about how we think about them, how we respond and how much energy we give them.

Join us for a practical, down-to-earth session exploring three simple ways to deal with difficult people more effectively:

1. Question your thinking

Are you seeing the situation clearly, or making assumptions about someone's intentions and behaviour?

2. Choose your response

Learn how to step back, avoid reacting on autopilot and respond in ways that are more constructive.

3. Protect your energy

Understand when to address difficult behaviour, establish boundaries or simply let things go.

And we'll turn the question around too: What if I'm the difficult person? A little self-awareness can go a long way!

There'll be practical examples, useful ideas and plenty of opportunity for discussion.

The aim? To leave with a few simple thinking tools you can put to use in everyday life.

Because you can't always choose the people you meet along the way, but you can choose how you respond to them.

THINK WELL CORNER

Practical thinking skills for real life.

The Aotearoa Jazz Orchestra is pleased to present the next instalment of its jazz improvisation workshop series.

Hosted by cross-genre performer Oscar Lavën, alongside a professional jazz rhythm section, these highly accessible workshops are designed to help musicians build confidence in improvisation through listening, playing, and creative exploration. Particularly suited to musicians from a classical background, the workshops are open to players of all instruments, ages, and musical backgrounds.

Participants in previous workshops praised the supportive atmosphere, practical learning, and encouragement they received while exploring new musical ideas. This workshop will offer participants an entry point into jazz styles, group listening, and the foundational elements of ensemble playing, with the goal of learning to play and improvise on a jazz standard.

You'll have the opportunity to play alongside a professional rhythm section in a safe, comfortable, and supportive learning environment, where experimentation and curiosity are encouraged.

Workshop places are limited, allowing plenty of opportunity for individual participation, discussion, and playing time with the rhythm section.

Suitable for students, amateurs, and anyone wanting to begin their jazz journey.

🤖 AI, MARK MY WORDS!

Write it. Test the AI. Trust your judgement.

Can AI really improve your writing? Or does it sometimes get things wrong?

Join Viet Hub NZ for a FREE, fun and interactive writing workshop where YOU get to challenge AI, spot its mistakes and discover how to become a more confident writer.

Whether you're writing an email to your teacher, applying for a job, preparing an essay or studying for IELTS, this workshop is for you!

🌟 Meet your workshop leader – Kai.

We're excited to have Kai (Anh Khoa Dang), one of Viet Hub NZ's passionate young volunteers, leading this workshop.

At Viet Hub NZ, we believe young people have incredible ideas and deserve opportunities to bring them to life.

Kai has already been supporting learners through our IELTS Writing sessions. Now he's taking the next step – designing and leading his own workshop to help others develop practical writing skills.

Young minds. Bold ideas. The courage to try something new!

Come along, learn something useful and support a young community leader!

✍️ What will you do?

This isn't a workshop where you just sit and listen. You'll be writing, experimenting, discussing and putting AI to the test!

Hey → Dear! Turn a casual text message into a professional email. Can you write a better version than AI?

Spot the 8 writing traps! Discover common mistakes in tone, vocabulary and structure.

Choose your writing challenge! Write an email, job application paragraph or short essay.

Let AI mark your words! Ask AI to review your writing and see what it notices.

Human vs AI! Compare AI's feedback with another participant's. Who catches more mistakes?

You'll also receive practical take-home resources to continue improving your writing.

🎯 Who should join?

This workshop is particularly useful for:

School and university students

IELTS and English-language learners

Jobseekers preparing applications

Anyone who wants to write clearer, more professional emails

Curious minds who want to learn how to use AI responsibly

No advanced writing or AI experience required!

The workshop is delivered in English, with Vietnamese-language support available where needed.

A fully charged smartphone with internet access

Your curiosity and willingness to try something new!

At Viet Hub NZ, we want to create more opportunities for young people to lead, share their knowledge and contribute to their communities.

This workshop is about more than writing. It's about encouraging independent thinking, building confidence and showing that technology works best when we remain curious and critical.

AI can suggest the words. But you decide what they mean.

events.long_description:
Mini mosaics are really quick and simple to make - but can create a really popping design with beautiful coloured glass and fun shapes to decorate.

We will use gorgeous coloured glass pieces to create our designs on small flat backings - this is a very beginner-friendly method, and allows for several pieces to be made within the class time.

This class runs over two sessions; this means you have time to do all the parts of a mosaic. The planning, the glueing, and then your pieces have time to dry so you can then do the grouting and finishing off. A fantastic course that's super fun as a one-off experience - or to dip your toe into working with glass mosaics.

You can have the finished items as either:
A set ready to hang on a wall as singles
On a large sturdy jumpring ready to hang as a cute pendant set (or earrings).
On a cord for an heirloom Christmas ornament.

The class covers:
Preparing your bases and materials
Planning and choosing simple designs to make your mosaics really pop
How to snip your glass down into tiny pieces if needed (most pieces are already cut for you)
Working with adhesives, tips and tricks with tools.

In the second session we will continue finishing off your mosaics, selecting the grout you like, and learning how to apply and clean up this essential part of a mosaic.

Finally we will look at what mounting options and special additions you might want to add to your piece that will complete the design.

You are welcome to continue creating more mosaics and can purchase additional materials to do so. Any that require grouting after the class is completed can either:
Be completed by our team (for a small fee)
Be grouted by you later, we can supply the grout and some sealant for you to take home.

This is a warm, friendly class with excellent support and learning for complete beginners and those who want to start working with hand-cut glass terraria.

All tools are supplied, though you are welcome to bring your own tools and glass if you have them.
Your materials for the class projects are supplied as part of your course fee.

Young makers aged 12 and up are welcome to join the class, as long as they are able to work safely with sharp glass and tools.

Anyone under the age of 16 must attend with an enrolled parent or caregiver who is there to support them and participate alongside them.

events.name: Mozart Requiem (Duncan Druce Completion)
events.venue: Te Raukura ki Kapiti, Coastlands Theatre, 34a Raumati Rd, Paraparaumu
events.long_description:
Mozart Requiem (Duncan Druce Completion)

Kāpiti Chorale and Capital Choir join forces with orchestra and soloists for a powerful performance of Mozart's final masterpiece.

When Mozart died in 1791 at the age of 35, he left the Requiem unfinished. Within months, his student Franz Xaver Süssmayr completed the work on behalf of Mozart's widow Constanze. His version became one of the most famous and beloved works in the choral repertoire and remains the version most often performed today.

Yet Mozart's surviving sketches continued to raise questions. For more than 200 years, composers and scholars have revisited them, searching for clues to how Mozart himself intended to complete the work.

This concert presents one of the most fascinating answers to that question: the Duncan Druce completion. Created in 1984 by the English composer, performer and musicologist Duncan Druce, it draws on Mozart's surviving manuscript while revisiting parts of the traditional completion. The result offers a fresh perspective on one of the defining works of the classical repertoire.

This special collaboration brings together the combined forces of Kāpiti Chorale and Capital Choir, four outstanding soloists and orchestra for two performances: Saturday 28 November at Te Raukura ki Kapiti, Paraparaumu, and Saturday 5 December at the Riley Centre, Wellington High School.

The programme opens with a diverse selection of choral music, including works by Mozart, Salieri, Haydn, Princess Te Rangi Pai and William Dawson, before culminating in Mozart's Requiem.

Soloists

Barbara Paterson, soprano
Ruth Armishaw, alto
Richard Taylor, tenor
Joseph Haddow, bass

events.description:
Mozart Requiem (Duncan Druce Completion) Kāpiti Chorale and Capital Choir join forces with orchestra and soloists for a powerful performance of Mozart's final masterpiece.
When Mozart died in 1791 at the age of 35, he left the Requiem unfinished.
His version became one of the most famous and beloved works in the choral repertoire and remains the version most often performed today.
This concert presents one of the most fascinating answers to that question: the Duncan Druce completion.
This special collaboration brings together the combined forces of Kāpiti Chorale and Capital Choir, four outstanding soloists and orchestra for two performances: Saturday 28 November at Te Raukura ki Kapiti, Paraparaumu, and Saturday 5 December at the Riley Centre, Wellington High School.

events.name: MATRESCENCE Development Showing
events.venue: 12 Cambridge Terrace, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, Nueva Zelanda
events.long_description:
MATRESCENCE

A development showing at Hannah Playhouse

A solo show about the collision of early motherhood, migration and art making.

A mother tries to care for her baby. An artist tries to make a show.

MATRESCENCE follows Ella (“she” in Spanish), a migrant theatremaker and new mother trying to remain creatively alive while navigating the demands, exhaustion and disorientation of early motherhood.

Part testimonial, part creative crisis and part documentary, MATRESCENCE is an anti-biography that moves between Ella’s intimate experience of postpartum life and her attempt to make theatre from inside it. She reaches out to other migrant mothers and theatremakers, searching for answers about care, identity, creativity and belonging. But the more stories she gathers, the less this seems to be a story about one woman.

Join us for a special development showing of MATRESCENCE at Hannah Playhouse, a glimpse into the making of this new documentary theatre work. This is an opportunity to experience the work in progress and be part of its creative journey.

Following the showing, we invite you to stay for an informal Q&A - audience conversation. We would love to hear your thoughts, reflections and responses to the work, while opening up a wider conversation about postpartum, care work, and the complexities of motherhood, particularly when home, family and support networks are far away.

The work is informed by research into matrescence, migration and caregiving, interviews, as well as anonymous testimonies from migrant mothers living in Aotearoa.

Please note: This is a work in development showing, not a finished production. Your presence, thoughts and feedback are warmly welcomed and will contribute to the ongoing development of MATRESCENCE.

CREATIVE TEAM

Created and performed by Romina Meneses

Directed by Mel Dodge

Production Managment: Jessie Rochford-Barber

Lights and AV design: Janis Cheng

Sound Design: Alex Quinn

Set and Costume Design: Miho Aragane

Photo by Charlie Jewell

MATRESCENCE is a new documentary theatre work, set to premiere at BATS Theatre as part of NZ Fringe 2027.

events.name: The Lone Prairie Brothers Play The Shed
events.venue: 46a Victoria Street, Alicetown, Lower Hutt 5010, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Originally from the wilds of the south west of the UK, Phil Lively-Masters is an experienced, dynamic and well travelled singer songwriter, who specialises in writing the sort of Sun Kissed West Coast Laurel Canyon Americana and Roots Rock that made Neil Young, Stephen Stills, the Byrds and 'Wildflowers' era Tom Petty famous. With a powerful, honey soaked voice that has won praise and support slots from the likes of legendary American country rock pioneers The Jayhawks, Lemonheads frontman Evan Dando, original outlaw cosmic cowboy Steve Young (writer of Seven Bridges Road), Neil Halstead (Slowdive, Mojave 3) and received critical praise for acoustic slots at festivals such as Glastonbury and Maverick in the UK. 

Now based in Napier, Hawke's Bay, Phil has 20 years worth of road worn original songs to pull on, covering all the Roots/ Americana elements, with a skilful blend of Country, Rock, Blues and Folk. Having recently been inspired by a sonmgwriting stint in East Nashville, Phil came back to NZ and teamed up with local Lead guitar Telecaster Master Neil Matcheson as a new Americana duo 'The Lone Prairie Brothers', they are currently in the process of short listing songs for a new self titled debut album and racking up live gigs and great reviews in 2026, weaving Phil's trusty Guild 12 and 6 string guitars with Neil's versatile and exciting Telecaster licks; airing brand new songs and including some choice tracks from Phil's previous critically acclaimed UK band CANYON RYDE, (and their album 'Free To Be'), ready to weave a sun kissed, melodic americana spell on any listener.

Reviews for the Canyon Ryde album...

UNCUT MAGAZINE: ‘A prime platter...perfect for those attuned to the soft driftwood sounds of Buffalo Springfield and Gram Parsons'

MOJO MAGAZINE: ‘An excellent and very mature sounding debut in ‘Free to Be’. Another fine example of a talented ‘under the radar’ outfit producing American inspired music as good as, if not better, than a lot of Americans on the same trip. Highly Recommended!’

Sony/Universal Music Historian Richard Havers: ‘Big Names in The Making’…The MAVERICK AMERICANA FESTIVAL... the opening act on the main stage was the intriguingly named Canyon Ryde, featuring the exquisite songs of Phil Lively-Masters. Imagine you’ve been stranded on a California hill farm circa 1969 and you get the vibe. Their music is just so damned catchy!’

MAVERICK MAGAZINE: ‘CANYON RYDE is the vehicle for singer-songwriter Phil Lively-Masters and his superb songs that are evocative of America’s West Coast countryish pop-rock of the late 1960s and early 1970s… with acclaimed players such as singer songwriter Peter Bruntnell and Gary Louris… It is a gorgeous listening experience, especially on the captivating ‘Marine Drive’.

AMERICANA UK: ‘’Subtle and dreamy country boasting a host of Americana luminaries... ‘Free to Be’ is a great country record that is subtle in its approach, gentle in its intentions"

MOJO MAGAZINE: ‘An excellent and very mature sounding debut in ‘Free to Be’. Another fine example of a talented ‘under the radar’ outfit producing American inspired music as good as, if not better, than a lot of Americans on the same trip. Highly Recommended!’
Sony/Universal Music Historian Richard Havers: ‘Big Names in The Making’…The MAVERICK AMERICANA FESTIVAL... the opening act on the main stage was the intriguingly named Canyon Ryde, featuring the exquisite songs of Phil Lively-Masters. Imagine you’ve been stranded on a California hill farm circa 1969 and you get the vibe. Their music is just so damned catchy!’
MAVERICK MAGAZINE: ‘CANYON RYDE is the vehicle for singer-songwriter Phil Lively-Masters and his superb songs that are evocative of America’s West Coast countryish pop-rock of the late 1960s and early 1970s… with acclaimed players such as singer songwriter Peter Bruntnell and Gary Louris… It is a gorgeous listening experience, especially on the captivating ‘Marine Drive’.
AMERICANA UK: ‘’Subtle and dreamy country boasting a host of Americana luminaries... ‘Free to Be’ is a great country record that is subtle in its approach, gentle in its intentions"
events.description:
The Lone Prairie Brothers Play The Shed Tickets on sale Monday 2nd November 6pm via Humanitix.
Doors Open 7pm for a 7.30pm start.
Originally from the wilds of the south west of the UK, Phil Lively-Masters is an experienced, dynamic and well travelled singer songwriter, who specialises in writing the sort of Sun Kissed West Coast Laurel Canyon Americana and Roots Rock that made Neil Young, Stephen Stills, the Byrds and 'Wildflowers' era Tom Petty famous.
With a powerful, honey soaked voice that has won praise and support slots from the likes of legendary American country rock pioneers The Jayhawks, Lemonheads frontman Evan Dando, original outlaw cosmic cowboy Steve Young (writer of Seven Bridges Road), Neil Halstead (Slowdive, Mojave 3) and received critical praise for acoustic slots at festivals such as Glastonbury and Maverick in the UK.
Now based in Napier, Hawke's Bay, Phil has 20 years worth of road worn original songs to pull on, covering all the Roots/ Americana elements, with a skilful blend of Country, Rock, Blues and Folk.

The Undercurrent presents Unsung Heroes!

Cameron Bennett and Chris Priestley -with special guest Angela Fox- share songs, stories and a slideshow from NZ's distant past. Together, they bring to life the characters and stories of our past - the quirky and macabre - that shaped who we are today.

Chris Priestley is a singer, songwriter & NZ historian. He has recorded eight albums and his musical spans over 40 years. As a hospitality entrepreneur he was co-founder of Real Groovy Records & café/music venues Java Jive, Kerouacs, Atomic and Café One2One in Ponsonby.

Los Angeles post-punk band DECEITS has been building something real from the ground up. Since forming in 2021, longtime friends Kevin Moreno (Vocals/Instruments) and Francisco Saenz (Drums/Percussions) have self-released their entire catalog, quietly amassing millions of streams, selling out tours, and pressing vinyl that disappears just as quickly as it arrives. Their momentum has carried them from the underground to stages like Cruel World 2025 and across their first European tour, all while earning coverage from Post-Punk.com and the Los Angeles Times. DECEITS aren’t interested in playing it safe. Their take on post-punk rejects the genre’s colder edges in favor of something more alive, pulling in the color, rhythm, and emotional intensity of the Spanish-language music they grew up with. The result is a sound that feels both nostalgic and distinctly their own: moody, melodic, and impossible to stand still to.

This show is at Space Academy in Christchurch

Whether you're a longtime follower or discovering Dónal for the first time, these shows are a chance to catch an Irish musician making his mark in the southern hemisphere.

events.long_description:
Relive the highs and bitter lows of one of the most beloved comedians and writers of all time. Eric Idle sits down to tell his incredible life story, live on stage at the St James Theatre in Wellington. From the giddy heights of Monty Python success to the trauma of childhood — this is unscripted and candid. The audience will also get the chance to put their own questions to him live on stage.

An Evening of Idle Conversation covers sixty years of show business. Eric will recall memories of the friends he has loved and lost including Graham Chapman, George Harrison, and Robin Williams. He’ll also cover fortunes made and squandered, feuds, reunions, a brush with cancer, and why, at 83, he is still looking on the bright side of life.

Along with five other comics Eric formed Month Python in 1969. The troupe’s absurdist sketches continue to influence comedy more fifty years later. Eric is perhaps most famous for writing the song Always Look on the Bright Side of Life, The Rutles (the world’s first mockumentary), and the musical Spamalot.

events.name: Porirua Parkrun
events.venue: Bothamley Park, Champion Street, Porirua - Mana
events.long_description:
What is Porirua parkrun? It is a free 5km walk or run event - It’s not about coming first or winning. You can go at your own pace and just enjoy being with other people. It is inclusive and the perfect way to start your weekend in the outdoors chatting to people.

The start occurs just upstream of the Bothamley Park carpark. This car park is off Champion street, opposite the intersection with Windley Street. Head to end of carpark where the concrete ends and there is a gate. For location see https://goo.gl/maps/wEohfp9bRu82.

The course is following the old coach road (circa 1870's) established for the early farms in the area. Today this historic track is located within a park, away from cars and now used by walkers, runners and cyclists.

The track is generally 3 metres wide with a gentle gradient and a compacted gravel surface beside the Kenepuru Stream through a picturesque wooded wild valley. (Note there is a pinch point for a short section after the 2km marker where participants need to go single file each direction for approx 30 metres)

The valley runs east-west with mature trees which means this has to be one of the most sheltered places, out of the wind to exercise in Wellington.

What does it cost to join in? Nothing - it's free! but please register before your first run or walk, so you can get your timing results. You only need to register with parkrun once, to participate at any of the parkrun events around the world. Don't forget to bring a copy of your barcode. If you forget it, you won't get a time.

How fast do I have to be? Walking is fine as long as you can finish the 5km. Please come along and join in whatever your pace!

One dog per adult is welcome, as long as it is on a short hand held lead.

Children welcome but those 10 years and under need to be kept within arms reach of a supervising adult.

Note there is no toilets in the park, so go before you go.

We're friendly! Every week we grab a post park run/walk coffee/tea at Get Fixed within Kai Tahi at 20 Parumoana Street, to mix exercise with socialising.

There are volunteering opportunities even week. So those doing Duke of Edinburgh or similar challenges can get volunteer credits. Ensure you contact us well in advance at "porirua@parkrun.co.nz"

events.venue: Charles Plimmer House, Innermost Gardens, Mt Victoria, Wellington
events.long_description:
There's more to you than you think.

Sometimes we get so caught up in the stories we tell about ourselves that we lose touch with what we're actually experiencing.

*Beyond the Story* is an invitation to step out of our heads and into a different kind of exploration.

Through movement, breathwork, music, conversation and shared experiences, we'll explore what becomes possible when we spend less time analysing and more time experiencing.

This is an experiential workshop rather than an introductory programme. It is particularly suited to men who have some experience of men's work or personal development, or who feel ready to explore themselves and their connections with others in a more embodied way.

You don't need to have all the answers. Curiosity and a willingness to participate are enough.

Workshop details

Arrive from 9:00 am. Workshop runs from 9:15 am to 4:30 pm.

BYO lunch. Tea, coffee and light snacks provided.

Fees and applications

Early bird: $70, provided your application is accepted and payment received by Saturday 14 November.

Standard fee: $100.

Applications close Sunday 22 November.

Places are limited. Applications are reviewed before places are offered, so please don't make payment until requested.

Apply using the Workshop Information & Application link above.

Presented by Wellington Men's Trust.
Supported by Matariki Services Ltd.

events.name: Glass Bead-Making Taster - Taster Session!
events.venue: Workspace Studios Ōtaki, 2 Arthur Street, Ōtaki, Ōtaki
events.long_description:
Join us for this fabulous introduction to working with colourful molten glass!

This class is a great way for absolute beginners to get a taste of working with glass to produce beautiful beads that can be used in a myriad of ways, including making a unique gift for your loved one (or yourself!).

As one of the earliest forms of human adornment, beads have long functioned as a way to express individuality, and what better way to do that than to learn to make your own unique beads?

Students are shown correct lampworking techniques to produce several decorative beads in just 3 hours! How many beads you make is up to you; some students make up to 10 while others make fewer using trickier techniques.

Kids over 12 (or so) are welcome to take the class, but anyone under 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

events.long_description:
AJO Jazz Improvisation Workshops

The Aotearoa Jazz Orchestra is pleased to present the next instalment of its jazz improvisation workshop series.

Hosted by cross-genre performer Oscar Lavën, alongside a professional jazz rhythm section, these highly accessible workshops are designed to help musicians build confidence in improvisation through listening, playing, and creative exploration. events.long_description:
Natural Textured Rings - Taster - Wellington!
Make your own personalised ring - a gift for yourself or someone special! :-)

Learn the basic technique first in copper or brass, and then craft your final piece in silver!

Over this taster class, you’ll be guided through the process of heating and texturing metal, cutting and shaping with traditional jewellery tools. Use feathers, leaves, or fabrics to create a unique texture for a beautiful ring!

Learn to measure your finger, cut metal to length and texture it without rolling mill, hammers and punches. Then use a jewellers torch, sandpaper and polishing, and your beautiful new ring will be ready to wear.

This 3-hour class is ideal for beginners, groups of friends and visitors to the city.

Included in the class fee are copper and brass for practising on, a sterling silver ring strip and all consumables such as sandpaper, solder and chemicals. Extra metals are available for purchase in the studio.

Kids aged 12 (or so) are welcome to attend the class, but any person under the age of 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

Workshop fee is $165, Early bird pricing $148 (ends 2 November).

events.id: Unsung Heroes at Greytown Upclose & Personal-Cobblestones Heritage Village, 169 Main Street, Greytown-Event Finder
events.name: Unsung Heroes at Greytown Upclose & Personal
events.venue: Cobblestones Heritage Village, 169 Main Street, Greytown
events.long_description:
Unsung Heroes, Cameron Bennett and Chris Priestley, with special guests Kate Marshall and Angela Fox.
They sing, they play, they recount stories based on actual people and real events that occurred in our colonial history.
You'll enjoy their eclectic brand of folk heritage to in the very appropriate setting of Cobblestones Heritage Village.
You can expect to hear stories from Aotearoa New Zealand’s distant past in song, with newspaper clippings and poems as an introduction and a slideshow of historic images to accompany each tale.
The duo brings alive the incredible stories of our rogues, rebels and folk heroes in an entertaining history lesson through what music critic Marty Duda has called Priestley’s beautiful melodies and “a wonderful, simple, direct singing style.”
They are stories about us, this place and people we hadn’t heard of, wrote another reviewer, Mike Mizrahi.
“Helping to create the wonderful tapestry, unique in the world, of Aotearoa and the brave folk that came and settled here. It was driven by immediate, moving and wonderfully fashioned songs that told these great tales, accompanied by incredible slide imagery that transported audiences to these times.”
The duo are accomplished musicians, whether individually or appearing in a multitude of different groups or collaborative ventures. For this concert they will be joined by local multi-instrumentalist Kate Marshall and will be bringing a few local stories.
Unsung Heroes have performed as part of the Auckland Heritage Festival, and in Christchurch, Wellington and Dunedin but also taken their brand of folk history through folk music to the likes of Gore, Katikati, Inglewood, Okarito, St Bathans and other small locales – and now they are excited to bring this performance to Cobblestones.
Seating is limited and tickets are $25 cash on the door with bookings by text to 02102361951 or buy through Eventfinda

events.name: Catherine Chidgey: The Starving Bride
events.venue: 12 Cambridge Terrace, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Described by the 2026 Arts Foundation Te Tumu Toi Laureate panel as "without a doubt one of New Zealand's most important living writers", internationally bestselling author Catherine Chidgey returns to Verb to discuss her tenth enthralling novel. The Starving Bride is an urgent and searing story set in near-future England.


Dumped by her boyfriend, fired from her job and estranged from her parents, Hazel Whitlock signs up for a sideshow act in Blackpool. The seaside resort has revived all the cancelled old favourites and she will be the Starving Bride. On display in the iconic Blackpool Tower, with a ravenous lion prowling the enclosure, Hazel must lie in silence while strangers view her body.

Join Catherine and Kate Camp for a special one-night event as they discuss the many layers of The Starving Bride, writing female experiences and the questions the book raises about spectacle, desire, survival and society's obsession with beauty.

Unity Books will be at the event bookselling and Catherine will be book signing.

Cover artwork by Max Thompson. Cover design by Todd Atticus. Author photo by Ebony Lamb.

Catherine Chidgey’s novels have been published to international acclaim. Her first, In a Fishbone Church, won Best First Book at the New Zealand Book Awards and at the Commonwealth Writers’ Prize (South East Asia and South Pacific). In the UK it won the Betty Trask Award and was longlisted for the Orange Prize.

Her second, Golden Deeds, was a Notable Book of the Year in the New York Times Book Review and a Best Book in the LA Times. Catherine has won the Prize in Modern Letters, the Katherine Mansfield Award, the Katherine Mansfield Fellowship, the Janet Frame Fiction Prize, and, for her 2016 novel The Wish Child, the Acorn Foundation Fiction Prize.

Her 2020 novel, Remote Sympathy, was shortlisted for the DUBLIN Literary Award and the Jann Medlicott Acorn Prize for Fiction, and was longlisted for the Women’s Prize for Fiction. The Axeman’s Carnival (2022) won the Jann Medlicott Acorn Prize for Fiction. Catherine's two most recent novels are the critically acclaimed Pet (2023) and The Book of Guilt (2025), also published by John Murray.

Catherine lectures in Creative Writing at the University of Waikato.

Kate Camp is the author of many collections of poems, including The Mirror of Simple Annihilated Souls (winner of the 2011 NZ Post Book Award for Poetry) and How to Be Happy Though Human: New and Selected Poems (2020), and a collection of essays, You Probably Think This Song Is About You (2022). Her most recent book is Makeshift Seasons (2025), a new collection of poetry. Kate was born in 1972 and lives in Wellington.

Leaving Dublin, Ireland where he was born and raised until the age of 22, David got drunk on travel and never quite hit sobriety of it. He has lived and worked in twelve countries and visited over eighty. His shows draw on his wide travels, cultural observations, attempts at language study, (occasional) international drinking session(s) and being a mildly confused immigrant. 
David is the winner of the prestigious annual San Francisco Comedy Competition, (previous finalists include Robin Williams, Ellen DeGeneres and Dana Carvey) and runner-up in the Moth’s largest US Grandslam storytelling competition. Also a bestselling writer, David recorded his debut special Documented for Dry Bar Comedy in 2019, his follow up Cultural Appreciation in 202, and his award winning show Shelf Help in 2025. He has been featured on TED.com, Sirius XM, Just For Laughs, Netflix is a Joke Festival, RTE’s Late Late Show, The Irish Independent, Inc, NPR, and the Huffington Post among others. A festival favorite, David's videos have also gone viral many times over with over 800 million views and a social following of over 2 million people. More info: davidnihill.com

events.long_description:
Los Angeles post-punk band DECEITS has been building something real from the ground up. Since forming in 2021, longtime friends Kevin Moreno (Vocals/Instruments) and Francisco Saenz (Drums/Percussions) have self-released their entire catalog, quietly amassing millions of streams, selling out tours, and pressing vinyl that disappears just as quickly as it arrives. Their momentum has carried them from the underground to stages like Cruel World 2025 and across their first European tour, all while earning coverage from Post-Punk.com and the Los Angeles Times. DECEITS aren’t interested in playing it safe. Their take on post-punk rejects the genre’s colder edges in favor of something more alive, pulling in the color, rhythm, and emotional intensity of the Spanish-language music they grew up with. The result is a sound that feels both nostalgic and distinctly their own: moody, melodic, and impossible to stand still to.

events.long_description:
Join us for Professor Tristram Ingham's Inaugural Professorial Lecture, titled "Ōritetanga | Equity. One principle. One journey among many." If you'd like to attend, either in person or via the livestream, please register via the link above. This lecture will be followed by light refreshments.

About Professor Tristram Ingham's research:

Tristram (Ngāti Kahungunu ki Heretaunga, Ngāti Porou) is a clinical epidemiologist with decades of experience in healthcare research. His work advances equity across respiratory health, tāngata whaikaha Māori (Māori disability) and health services’ governance. He uses kaupapa Māori and mixed-methods research to translate evidence into policy and system change in Aotearoa.

Tristram led the development of Whāia Te Ao Mārama, the Māori Disability Action Plan 2018-2022 and is Chair of the Te Ao Mārama Aotearoa Trust, a nationwide organisation representing Tāngata Whaikaha Māori. He was made a Companion of the King’s Service Order (KSO) in the 2025 New Year Honours for services to survivors of abuse in care. In 2024, he received the ONZM for services to the disability community.

Tristram is an honorary fellow of the New Zealand College of Public Health Medicine, a member of the Institute of Directors New Zealand and a member of the Royal Society Te Apārangi.

NZFSS Conference 2026
Registrations open soon!

2026 NZFSS Conference
📍1 - 4 December 2026
📍Takina | Wellington

Register here https://www.nzfssconference.co.nz/

Conference Theme:
At the Confluence: Communities, Catchments, and our Freshwater Futures - Ngā Rerenga E Tūtaki Ana

Our 2026 conference explores the confluence: the place where flows meet, merge, and reshape one another. In freshwater science, confluences are dynamic hydrological junctions which create unique habitats and environments. For this conference it represents the meeting of people, knowledge systems, innovations, and aspirations that shape the future of wai in Aotearoa.

Hosting the conference in Te Whanganui‑a‑Tara/Wellington, where urban streams like Waimapihi and Kumutoto meet the great harbour Te Whanganui‑a‑Tara provides a powerful metaphor for integration across urban waters, catchments, and communities. As Aotearoa navigates changing climate pressures, evolving policy landscapes, disruptive technologies, and growing community involvement, this confluence becomes a space for meaningful collaboration and forward‑thinking action.

We look forward to welcoming you to WLG!

events.long_description:
Overview

Our Leadership & Management Part 3 workshop is a practical skills training course designed for people in a leadership/management position.

Leaders today are expected to be the driving force of their teams. They are constantly under pressure to lead effectively in a business environment that is characterised by constant change. Our leadership and management courses offer participants the opportunity to develop the necessary skills to embrace this challenge and lead their teams through these times with confidence and pride.

Our Leadership & Management - Part 3 workshop is a practical skills training course designed for people already in a leadership/management position, or those about to take up a new role, who want to explore the latest thinking and models for effective management and leadership and build on the techniques acquired in our Part 1 and 2 workshops.

In today’s world, emotional Intelligence is a critical and powerful component of effective leadership. This 2-day course will equip leaders with the skills to become more ‘people smart’ by developing ways to lead with emotional intelligence. Participants will also learn how to inspire their people with a shared vision and align teams to company goals, along with the tools to lead and manage change, ways to become a more influential and persuasive leader and the tools to raise awareness and manage unconscious bias in the workplace.

Course Outcomes

Assess your leadership strengths and identify opportunities for growth
Learn how to become a more inspirational and influential leader
Understand the importance of emotional intelligence as a key leadership skill
Learn how to lead with emotional intelligence, develop leadership self-awareness and become more ‘people smart’
Communicate your goals, vision and purpose with greater clarity, confidence and inspiration
Inspire and align your team to your shared vision and goals
Understanding change and learn how to lead change and growth in your organisation
Apply strategies to motivate and inspire your people to embrace change and strive for positive outcomes
Understand what unconscious bias is and recognise its effects on your people and your organisation
Explain how you can manage your own unconscious bias and implement steps to raise awareness and manage unconscious bias in the workplace

Course Prerequisite: Participants must have a good understanding of leadership and management fundamentals and/or have previously attended the Business Training New Zealand - Leadership & Management Part 1 & 2 course.

For more information or to book: email info@biztrainers.co.nz or call 06 354 5555

events.long_description:
Overview

Discover how leading organisations uncover hidden risks, prioritise investment and make better decisions with confidence.

Executive Briefing for CIOs, Strategy, Digital and Transformation Leaders



AI, transformation, cyber resilience and cost optimisation continue to dominate executive agendas, yet many organisations still lack a connected view of how these priorities impact the broader enterprise.

Join Kapish and Ardoq for an executive briefing exploring how leading organisations are making better decisions through greater visibility across strategy, business capabilities, technology, risk and investment.

Using a fictional organisation facing familiar business challenges, our consultants will walk through a series of executive scenarios involving transformation, AI adoption, technology risk, application rationalisation and operational resilience. We'll demonstrate how leaders can better understand impacts, dependencies and risk through a connected enterprise view enabled by Ardoq.

You'll gain practical insights into how organisations are:

Understanding the impact of strategic and technology decisions
Identifying hidden dependencies and risks
Reducing complexity and unnecessary duplication
Prioritising transformation and technology investments
Strengthening governance for AI and business change

The session includes practical use cases, a live demonstration of the scenarios within Ardoq, and opportunities for questions with our consultants and enterprise architecture specialists.

Lunch and refreshments provided. Places are limited.

events.name: AIPA Wellington | The Changing Landscape of Commercial Photography
events.venue: 2/8 Kent Terrace, Mount Victoria, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
events.long_description:
The Changing Landscape of Commercial Photography

Expanding the frame to fit the evolving world of image making.

Commercial photography has always evolved alongside technology, creativity and client needs. Today, changes happen faster than ever, the lines between photography, video, motion, stop motion and content creation are increasingly blurred. Agencies and clients are after new ways to tell stories and the expectations and skills in image-making shifts with them.

But what does that actually mean for photographers?

Whether you've spent decades behind the camera, are just finding your feet, or you’re somewhere in between, change always brings questions, sometimes challenges and of course, plenty of opportunities.


So do we need to adapt? What skills are becoming more valuable? How are agencies approaching creative production? And how can we evolve our businesses and creative practice without losing sight of what makes our work distinctive?

On Tuesday 1 December, we’ll unpack these questions and more with our guest speakers: 

Ashley Alexander | Photographer, Videographer & Creative

Ashley will share his perspective from behind the camera, how his practice has evolved and the opportunities he's found working across different forms of image-making.

Josh Rollo | Senior Producer, VML

Josh brings the agency perspective, sharing insights into how creative production is changing, what clients are looking for and how agencies are navigating an ever-evolving landscape.

This isn't about having all the answers or trying to be everything to everyone. It's about understanding what's happening around us, learning from each other and recognising the opportunities.

Tuesday 1 December | 6pm

VML, 2/8 Kent Terrace, Mt Victoria, Wellington

Free for AIPA and NZIPP members | $10 for non-members.

Come along and bring your questions, share your experiences and meet other photographers in the industry. Whether you're established, emerging or just curious about what's next, there's a place for you in this conversation.

Good conversations. New perspectives. A chance to think about what's possible. And yes, there'll be pizza!

events.id: Book Group: Chess Story by Stefan Zweig-The Library, 1/53 Courtenay Place, Te Aro, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Book Group: Chess Story by Stefan Zweig
events.venue: The Library, 1/53 Courtenay Place, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
Chess Story (also published as Chess or, more poetically, as The Royal Game) is a novella by the Austrian author Stefan Zweig published in 1942. Written in exile in Brazil, Zweig examines Nazism, and he does so with (Penguin Books tells us) "his signature psychological insight". The story is set on a ship from New York to Buenos Aires and features a gripping chess match. This novella would be Zweig's final work. In exile in Brazil and despairing of the future for Europe, he and his wife committed suicide. He had sent the manuscript of Chess Story to his American publisher just days before.

There's a link to a translation on a website dedicated to the author -
http://www.stefanzweig.de/assets/pdfs/schachnovelle_english_complete.pdf - or, if you prefer to listen and because the novella's under 100 pages, there are audiobooks on YouTube etc that run a couple of hours.

At this Christmas session, we'll also choose what we're reading in the first half of next year. See you there!

Do you keep meaning to read more of the great classics? At Wellington Classic Literature Club, we read works that have stood the test of time, whether they were written in 1780, 1880 or even 1980. We meet on the first Tuesday of the month.

RSVP
Bookings essential. Get your free ticket by clicking 'Register' above. Limited places.

If you've signed up, but things change and you're not going to be able to make it along, please email classiclitwgtn@gmail.com as we may be able to make more spaces available for others.

VENUE
We meet in the ‘Games Room’, The Library bar's private area overlooking Courtenay Place. After you enter the bar, head to your right (up the step) and through a smaller space with booths to the large carpeted space beyond (behind the big wooden sliding door).

ABOUT US
Wellington Classic Literature Club has been running for more than a decade - since the start of 2013 - and we have a great bunch of regulars as well as readers who join us for particular books or simply when it suits.

events.long_description:
Overview

Find calm amid uncertainty with ancient wisdom, modern psychology and practical tools to build resilience and clarity.

Tuesday Wellbeing Seminars:




Finding Ground in an Uncertain World: Ancient Wisdom for Modern Turbulence

Inspire Me!
The world feels increasingly chaotic—from economic pressure to global political shifts and an unpredictable future. When external conditions are completely out of our hands, how do we keep from feeling overwhelmed?
This interactive workshop bridges contemporary psychology with timeless philosophy to help us build unshakeable internal resilience and stay anchored in times of uncertainty. We’ll look at the big picture, unpack what it means to live with the unknown, and share practical tools to maintain clarity amidst the noise.




Please note our events now start at 6pm. Please try to arrive by 5:45pm so we can get everyone into the event and start on time at 6pm.

End the session on a high note with a delicious plant-based dinner, dessert, and good conversation.
Meet your host, Sivananda:

Sivananda’s background is in both science and music, holding a Master's Degree in Data Science, a Bachelor of Science in Physics and a long history of playing and performing on the double bass. His passion for philosophy, music, good food and community attracted him to the bhakti lifestyle. Having studied and practiced the science of the ‘self’ for six years now, he thrives on drawing insights from contemporary science and combining it with yoga wisdom to encourage others to explore new perspectives.

Streets are the largest network of public space in our cities, yet for decades we’ve designed them mainly to move and store cars. Around the world, that’s changing fast. From Bogotá to Paris, cities are reimagining their streets as places to walk, play, meet, shop and breathe.

Drawing on lessons from the Global Street Design Guide and Designing Streets for Kids, this talk shares inspiring stories and striking before-and-after transformations from cities across the globe. It’s a celebration of what’s possible when we design streets for people, and an invitation to imagine what our own streets could become.

events.name: Michal Cihelka – A Most Beautiful Piano Recital
events.venue: Johnsonville Uniting Church, 18 Doctor Taylor Terrace, Johnsonville, Wellington
events.long_description:
Join Wellington pianist Michal Cihelka for an inviting and varied musical journey, bringing together some of the most beautiful and exciting music from the classical repertoire, alongside favourites from the world of musical theatre and popular music.

A particular highlight of the programme is Michal's performance of the first two movements of Shostakovich's beloved Piano Concerto No. 2, uniquely accompanied by his own Unreal Orchestra – a hand-crafted backing track that brings the sound and scale of a full orchestra to the experience.

Also featuring is Chopin's dramatic and deeply expressive Ballade No. 1, Debussy's ethereal Clair de Lune, and a selection of brilliant Preludes by Rachmaninoff.

And, for lovers of musical theatre and popular music, Michal brings together a selection of beautiful and familiar favourites, reimagined through his own distinctive arrangements.

Come along and enjoy a memorable and most beautiful piano recital. Pay-what-you-can tickets start at just $5. Tickets are available online, or at the door on the day (subject to seating availability).

Recital duration is approximately 75 minutes.

events.long_description:
Celebrate, connect and be inspired as we bring the Wellington Women in HealthTech community together to close out 2026.

Join us for an evening of conversation, connection and festive celebration, featuring a panel discussion with Kelsey Schwynn and Eileen Duddy from Health New Zealand | Te Whatu Ora Digital Services. They will share insights into their roles, the different pathways that brought them into digital health, and their experiences working at the intersection of strategy, design and delivery.

Date: Wednesday, 2 December 2026
Time: 5.00 pm–7.30 pm
Venue: Fujifilm, Level 9, 20 Ballance Street, Wellington

Evening programme

5.00 pm–5.30 pm: Arrival and networking

5.30 pm–6.30 pm: Panel conversation with Kelsey Schwynn and Eileen Duddy

6.30 pm–7.30 pm: Festive networking and end-of-year celebration

Meet our speakers

Kelsey Schwynn is a Digital Health Partner at Health New Zealand, with experience spanning health strategy, product leadership, service design and digital transformation. Before joining Health New Zealand, she was Chief Product Officer at Optimal Workshop and held senior strategic design roles in Australia and the United States. Her career has included supporting government agencies, not-for-profits and Fortune 500 companies through human-centred design, product strategy and large-scale digital change.

Eileen Duddy is a strategic digital health leader with more than 20 years’ experience in the health sector, including over a decade working across complex, cross-government initiatives. As a Digital Health Partner at Health New Zealand | Te Whatu Ora, she connects Digital Services with health sector stakeholders, translating clinical, operational and strategic priorities into aligned digital roadmaps and investment pathways. Eileen brings a pragmatic, forward-thinking approach to defining problems, aligning priorities and progressing initiatives that deliver meaningful outcomes for people, whānau and the wider health system.

Come along to hear two compelling career stories, exchange ideas with others across the HealthTech community, and celebrate the people and progress that have shaped another year for WiHT in Wellington.

events.name: Young Photographer Awards 2026
events.venue: 2 Queens Drive, Hutt Central, Lower Hutt 5010, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Join us for a special evening celebrating the creativity, achievements and unique perspectives of young photographers from across the Wellington region and beyond.

Following the success of our inaugural awards in 2025, which brought together nearly 200 children, families, photographers and supporters, the Young Photographer Awards are returning for another inspiring celebration!

Organised by The Art of Seeing Academy, the awards recognise young people aged 7–18 who have participated in our photography workshops throughout the year.

For many of these young photographers, this may be the first time their work has been publicly celebrated. Every photograph tells a story, and every young photographer brings a different way of seeing the world.

What to expect on the night

This year's ceremony will bring together young photographers, their families, professional photographers and our wider creative community.

The evening will feature:

Young Photographer Awards presentation: Celebrating selected young photographers and recognising their creativity, effort and achievements.

Five inspiring guest speakers: Professional photographers sharing their experiences, creative journeys and stories from behind the lens.

Young photographers' work: A celebration of the images, ideas and perspectives developed through our workshops.

A community celebration: An opportunity to come together, support young talent and recognise the importance of creativity in young people's lives.

Meet our guest speakers

We are delighted to welcome five professional photographers who will share their experiences, insights and stories with our young creatives

Fairlie Atkinson
Photography in service of our community


Fairlie is a photography teacher at Kāpiti College who has helped students achieve national recognition through awards and exhibitions. Passionate about creativity and community, she encourages young photographers to use their images to tell meaningful stories, advocate for causes they care about and make a positive difference.

Tara Swan
Wildlife photography and conservation


Tara is a wildlife photographer and ecologist with over a decade of experience working with rare birds. Her photography focuses on Aotearoa's native wildlife and Kaimanawa horses. She'll share how photography can tell the stories of our natural world and inspire greater care for wildlife and conservation.

Dave Allen
Overcoming self-doubt in photography

With over 30 years of experience in photography and videography, Dave will explore how to build confidence as a photographer. He'll share insights into managing self-doubt, stepping outside your comfort zone and recognising the creative strengths that come with being yourself.

Stephen Garner
Projects, corgis, and people: How I get unstuck when I don't know what to photograph

Stephen has been taking photographs since receiving his first camera at age six. He loves street, travel and documentary photography, often accompanied by his two wind-up corgis, Dante and Virgil. He'll share his playful approach to finding inspiration and overcoming creative blocks.

Emmeline Plachecki
Beyond the lens: The stories, feelings and connections behind equine photography

Emmeline is a New Zealand photographer specialising in equine photography. Combining her understanding of horses with a creative eye, she captures the emotions, personalities and connections that make each horse unique. She'll explore how photography can tell stories that go beyond what we see.

Every young photographer deserves to be seen

Throughout 2026, The Art of Seeing Academy has continued to introduce children and teenagers to photography through hands-on workshops across the Lower North Island region.

Some participants pick up a camera for the first time. Others return to develop their skills, explore new ideas and discover their own photographic style.

Our workshops encourage young people to slow down, observe their surroundings, express themselves and build confidence through creativity. We welcome young people of all abilities, backgrounds and learning needs.

The Young Photographer Awards are an opportunity to recognise their progress and celebrate what they have achieved.

Come and celebrate with us!

Whether you are a parent, a young photographer, a photography enthusiast or simply someone who believes in supporting young creative talent, we would love to see you there.

Join us for an evening of inspiring stories, wonderful photographs and well-deserved recognition for our next generation of photographers.

events.long_description:
Overview

A concert in three circles moving between installation, sound and performance.

Curated by composer-artists Elliot Vaughan and Noel Meek, STROMA transforms Massey’s Great Hall into a space for listening, wandering and encountering music from different perspectives.

The evening unfolds in three circles.

From 7:00pm, arrive at your own pace for an open, self-guided installation in the Great Hall. Wander through a collection of intimate works, sounds and performances, taking time to explore the space before gathering at 7:30pm.

At 7:30pm, the space transforms for Gordon Monahan’s Speaker Swinging, as performers set speakers into motion, sending sound and circles of light through the Great Hall.

Then, at approximately 8:00pm, the audience gathers in the round for a seated concert of chamber music, bringing together works by composers from Aotearoa and beyond, including a new commission by Eve de Castro-Robinson.

From open exploration, through sound and movement, to a concert in the round, the evening moves between different ways of listening, experiencing and inhabiting the space.

events.long_description:
Overview

Keeping Ahead of Change, Managing Risk & Building Confidence

9:00 Welcome and Industry Update

Industry update
Key issues to keep on the radar

9:30 Around the Table: What Are You Dealing With?

Share the key compliance issues and challenges you're currently facing
Identify common themes across organisations, buildings and roles
Share solutions, experiences and lessons learned

10:30 Morning Tea

10:45 Compliance Schedules: Keeping Pace with Changing Guidance & Interpretations

Strategies for updating and amending schedules
Responding to changes in legislation, regulations and guidance
Identifying when a Compliance Schedule needs to change
Practical review of real examples

12:00 Lunch

12:45 Building Compliance in Practice: Case Study Workshop

Work through a real building compliance scenario
Identify compliance obligations and risks
Determine what information, documentation and evidence is required

1:45 Using Discretionary Exemptions for Specified Systems and Minor Works

When exemptions can be used
Applying Schedule 1 (2) to alterations, fit-outs and minor works
Specified systems and other compliance considerations
Work through practical examples and common pitfalls

2:45 Afternoon Tea

3:00pm Action Planning

Translate today's learning into practical actions
Identify priorities for your role, clients or portfolio

3:30 Looking Ahead

Key takeaways
What’s coming up
Final discussion

4:00 Close

Your host: Rosemary (Rosie) Killip

If you’ve been around building compliance for a while, you probably already know Rosie.

Rosie has been translating, untangling and occasionally questioning building rules since the 1990s - and founded Building Networks in 2000 to help make sense of it all.

She loves nothing more than taking a complicated compliance issue, pulling it apart and asking the question: “But what does this actually mean in practice?”

Expect a practical day, plenty of discussion, a few challenges to the status quo - and probably a laugh or two along the way.

Read less

events.venue: level 6/44 Bowen Street, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Ever wondered what it really takes to make it to the top? Join us for an evening of speed networking with some of Wellington’s most inspiring executives.

At Get to Know a CxO, you’ll have the chance to move around the room and chat one-on-one with a range of senior leaders. Expect candid conversations about their career journeys, lessons learned, and the moments that shaped their leadership.


This isn’t your typical panel event. It’s relaxed, interactive, and designed to help you connect directly with the people behind the titles. Whether you’re curious about leadership, thinking about your next move, or just love hearing great career stories, this event’s for you.

Come for the insights, stay for the connections ✨

📅 Thursday 3rd December, 5:00PM for a 5:30pm start

📍 Venue: KPMG - Level 6, 44 Bowen Street, Wellington

🎙️ Speakers: 

Philip Whitmore, Partner - Cyber at KPMG

Camy Bhandari, Co-Founder & Director at NZ Tech Rally

Tristan Leist Bessler, Public Sector Account Manager at Databricks

Additional speakers TBC.

Spots are limited, with FLINT members taking priority over non-members so register now to secure your spot!

FLINT is free to join, please register here: https://tuanz.org.nz/flint-signup/

We look forward to seeing you there.

_______________________

About FLINT

If you’re in the early stages of your career and you’re interested in digital technologies, come join the FLINT programme in your local city. We host events, webinars, podcasts and social catch ups that offer valuable networking, learning and growth opportunities. 

Find out more about the Wellington FLINT team here.

	

	




 

	

Philip Whitmore, Partner, Cyber and Digital at KPMG

	

Philip is a Partner within KPMG Cyber with over 30 years’ experience across a broad range of cyber security disciplines. He has worked extensively in New Zealand, as well as throughout the wider Asia Pacific region.  His cyber security knowledge and experience is supported by his wider business consulting background, giving him the ability to readily translate cyber security risks into a business context. Philip’s experience saw him win the New Zealand Cyber Security Person of the Year award in 2023.




	

Tristana Leist Bessler, Public Sector Account Manager at Data Bricks

	

Tristana Leist hails from Databricks, working with Aotearoa organisations to explore how data and AI can support better services and decision-making. Joining us from Seattle, WA, her work has spanned government, defence, education, and aerospace. She leads digital transformation with joy... and the occasional tap dance routine.

Tristana also just scooped up the TUANZ Member awards for 'Outstanding Future Leader'.




	

Camy Bhandari, Co Founder & Director at NZ Tech Rally

	

Camy Bhandari is the Co-Founder and Director at NZ Tech Rally, a community platform for tech practitioners in Aotearoa New Zealand. NZ Tech Rally brings tech professionals from across the country together to build a more diverse, equitable and inclusive tech industry through conferences, meetups and workshops.

She brings over 16 years of software development experience across banking, fintech, consultancies, startups and government. As a first-generation migrant, woman of colour and neurodiverse person, Camy draws on her own experiences to shape NZ Tech Rally into an inclusive and accessible space for everyone.

Please come along and celebrate the end of another great year with NAWIC Wellington!

We're heading to WellyPutt for a fun, relaxed evening of quirky Wellington-themed indoor, non-competitive mini golf, good company, and a chance to catch up with some familiar faces (and meet a few new ones!).

This is a relaxed evening, with plenty of opportunity to mingle, chat and enjoy the company of other women in construction. Whether you're keen to have a go at the mini golf or would rather just come along for a catch-up, we'd love to see you there.

What's included:

• A round of Wellington-themed mini golf at WellyPutt

• Plenty of nibbles and non-alcoholic drinks

• A few spot prizes throughout the evening

Tickets: $15 for NAWIC Members and $20 for Non-Members.

Arrive: anytime from 5:00 pm onwards. Come straight from work, grab a bite, have a putt and enjoy the evening.

Please note: WellyPutt is located upstairs and there is no lift access, so unfortunately the venue is not wheelchair accessible.

It's been a busy year for everyone, so this is a chance to wind down, have a laugh and celebrate another year of connections, collaboration and supporting women in construction. We hope to see you there.

NAWIC Wellington has been a long-time supporter of Wellington Women’s House, and this year we’ll again be collecting a few everyday essentials to pass on, on behalf of our generous NAWIC Wellington members.

If you’re able to bring something along, any of the following would be much appreciated.

Period products

Toothbrushes and toothpaste

Deodorant

Cutlery

Soap, shampoo or conditioner

Night Shift brings short talks, exhibition tours, and hands-on activities inspired by the world of Cornelia Parker to three Thursday evenings.

Come with friends or on your own, explore at your own pace, and linger over a drink at āta.

Join two Aotearoa writers whose fiction ventures into the unknown: Pip Adam, winner of the 2026 Ursula K. Le Guin Prize for Fiction, and Terri Te Tau, author of The Valley of Unlikely Acquaintances and member of the artist collective Mataaho.

With titles like The Future (Sixes & Sevens) and Through a Glass Darkly, Cornelia Parker’s artworks swirl with the sense that nothing is quite settled. Crawl inside that feeling with us.

--

Programme

5.30pm & 7.30pm: Exhibition Tours
Take a closer look at Cornelia Parker on a 45-minute guided tour. First come, first served.

5.30pm, 6.15pm, 7pm, 7.45pm: Step Inside the Darkroom
The Handmade Darkroom Collective is taking over our classroom and turning it into a working photographic darkroom. Inspired by Cornelia Parker, you are invited to make your own A5-sized photogram, playing with directional light and objects of significance or visual interest. Feel free to bring along some small trinkets you may wish to print with. 

Each time slot has a 16-person capacity, on a first-in-first-served basis. Please queue at the classroom door (upstairs) before the session you wish to attend. 

6.15pm & 6.45pm: Feeling Our Way Towards the Future
Two short talks with writers Pip Adam and Terri Te Tau, inspired by Cornelia Parker.

7.00–8.00pm: Behind the Scenes: Cornelia Parker
How do you hang an explosion? Meet some of the people who installed the exhibition and care for its artworks. Drop in, ask questions and find out what it takes to bring this exhibition to life.

--
