events.name: Allegra Krieger
events.venue: San Fran, Wellington
events.long_description:
New York based songwriter and composer Allegra Krieger brings her singular blend of folk, rock and indie pop to San Fran on 3 December, joined by special guest Elly Mae.

Known for songwriting that is intimate, understated and deeply observant, Krieger pairs soulful vocals with raw, vulnerable lyricism, moving through themes of love, loss and self-discovery with a striking sense of emotional clarity. Her work has earned praise from the New York Times, who described her as a “deceptively understated songwriter,” while Paste has celebrated the distinctive poetry running through her music. 

Having shared stages with artists including Jana Horn, Fust, Johanna Samuels, Shalom and Charlotte Cornfield, Krieger has steadily carved out a space of her own within contemporary indie songwriting, creating music that feels equally at home in moments of quiet reflection and full-band intensity. 

Opening the evening is Pōneke songwriter Elly Mae, whose dreamy guitar-led folk-noir draws from the textures of The Brian Jonestown Massacre, PJ Harvey and Mazzy Star. Since first appearing on Wellington stages in early 2025, she has gone on to perform at Newtown Festival, CubaDupa and Flying Nun’s A Month of Saturdays live series, with RNZ describing her sound as a “woozy ethereal slice of dreampop.” 

Together, the two artists make for an evening of evocative songwriting, atmospheric guitars and music built around the power of close listening.







San Fran holds a Supervised License, meaning minors are welcome to attend events at San Fran so long as they are accompanied by a legal guardian at all times whilst at the venue. Minors are of course not allowed to purchase alcohol under any circumstance.

Overview

Stoned-Em Sounds Summer Slam 2026 spearfishing and ocean cleanup competition

The Stoned-Em crew, in collaboration with Henderson’s, proudly presents the Stoned-Em Sounds Summer Slam 2026 Spearfishing & Ocean Clean-Up Competition!

4th–6th December 2026

New Zealand’s biggest spearfishing and ocean clean-up competition is back! This year we’ve mixed things up with a new format and new venues, while keeping the three-day competition across the Marlborough Sounds.

The competition boundaries cover a massive 4,000 km², and competitors can shore dive, kayak or use a boat.

NEW REGISTRATION & BRIEFING FORMAT

Register anytime between 9:00am–7:00pm on Friday 4th December at Henderson’s, 38 Grove Road, Mayfield, Blenheim.

At registration, you’ll sign in and watch the compulsory briefing video, covering the rules, safety information and the big reveal – the seven target species for 2026.

You’ll also collect a $15 Henderson’s voucher and 1.5 kg Fish Magnet burley, which are included with your entry.

THREE DAYS – SEVEN SPECIES

Our scoring system means the number of different species entered is more important than weight, encouraging competitors to target different species rather than simply up-sizing their catch.

It’s two divers per team and $75 per diver.

OCEAN CLEAN-UP – LET’S BREAK 10 TONNES!

Looking after the marine environment we all enjoy is a huge part of the Summer Slam.

Since the competition began, our competitors have removed approximately 7.8 tonnes of rubbish from the Marlborough Sounds. In 2026, we want your help to push that total beyond 10 tonnes!

We’re introducing new ocean rubbish categories this year, alongside some awesome prizes. Details will be revealed at the briefing.

NEW WEIGH-IN VENUE – BOOMTOWN BEER GARDEN

events.long_description:
Pre-Christmas camp at Catchpool Valley, Remutaka Forest Park
Join us for a pre-Christmas camp in the Catchpool Valley. All campers welcome including tents, $10 per night for adults; $5 per night for children and young people aged 5-17 years; 0-4 years free.

This Department of Conservation campsite is part of the Remutaka Forest Park and situated on the road from Wainuiomata to the coast.

Toilets and cold showers available.

Onsite water must be boiled so it is recommended you bring your own drinking water.

There is no rubbish disposal or dump station at the campsite, so you must take all waste away with you.

Dogs must be under control and on a leash at all times.

There is plenty of room to camp.

Look for the All Points flag when you arrive.

Note that the gates to the Catchpool Valley close at 8pm and open again at 6am.

There are a variety of short and longer bush walks adjacent to the campsite..

You can also explore the local area including tracks up to the historic Baring Head Lighthouse.

You can either fill in a registration form and pay when you arrive or book and pay for your site in advance online at https://www.doc.govt.nz/parks-and-recreation/places-to-go/wellington-kapiti/places/remutaka-forest-park/things-to-do/campsites/catchpool-valley-campsite/

If you book online you will see for 4 options. Choose Catchpool Valley Campsite which is on the righthand side of the booking screen. This is the general camping area.

events.name: Lost Wax in Three - Ring-making on Friday Nights!
events.venue: Workspace Studios Ōtaki, 2 Arthur Street, Ōtaki, Ōtaki
events.long_description:
Over three sessions, create your own unique ring using the age-old lost wax technique. This is a great opportunity to spend a Friday night getting creative and making something you can wear!

In weeks one and two, you will learn how to work with jeweller’s hard wax to design and shape your own ring. Experiment with texture, form and detail to create a one-of-a-kind piece. Your finished wax ring will then be sent away for casting in the metal of your choice.

There will be a week’s break before the third session to allow time for everyone’s waxes to be cast. In the final session, you’ll learn how to trim, clean and finish your cast, transforming your wax design into an original ring ready to wear.

More advanced students can use the sessions to develop their own ring designs in a supportive class setting.

Included in the class fee are all your different types of waxes, sandpaper and courier costs.

Casting and metal costs are not included and will vary depending on the size of your ring and the metal you choose. Small castings can cost around $6.65–$12, with metal costing approximately $7–$30 depending on whether you choose red bronze, white bronze or silver.

This class is suitable for teens and children aged 12 and over. Anyone under 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

events.name: Timeline - 300 Years of Music for Saxophone
events.venue: St Michael's Anglican Church, 81 Upland Rd, Kelburn, Wellington
events.long_description:
Join us as we explore the history of the saxophone through 300 years of music performed by an exciting yet subtle chamber duo.

This concert explores a broad range of music, from pieces by J.S Bach which predate the saxophone by over 100 years, to modern compositions which push the limits of the instrument. Between these moments you will hear some of the greatest works for saxophone, from the popular showcase Pequeña Czarda to the elegant staple Tableaux de Provence.

Hear the many moods and timbres of the saxophone, from delicately soaring melodies, to dark, enchanting arias and joyful, raucous moments.

Programme:
J.S. Bach - Partita No. 2 for Solo Violin: IV. Gigue
Robert Schumann - 3 Romances
J. B Singelée - Concertino Op. 78
Eugène Bozza - Aria
Pierre Lantier - Sicilienne
Pedro Itturalde - Pequeña Czarda
Paul Bonneau - Caprice en Forme de Valse
Paule Maurice - Tableaux de Provence
Steven Banks - Surrender

$25 pre-sale
$35 door sales
$10 student/concession

About the performers:
Alex Trask is a saxophonist based in Pōneke. He has a keen interest in the classical saxophone and has studied with some of New Zealand's leading player such as Simon Brew and Reuben Chin. He is a member of the Royal New Zealand Air Force Band and has performed with many other significant organizations such as Gallery Orchestra, Saxcess, Wellington Youth Orchestra, and Wellington City Symphonic Band.

Alex is also an accomplished jazz player, and has performed all over the country. In 2026 he appeared with the Aotearoa Jazz Orchestra, as well as playing lead alto for the RNZAF Jazz Orchestra. Alex helf the lead alto chair in the Rodger Fox Big Band from 2024-2025 and has performed as a guest with that band since 2022. In 2026 he recorded his first studio album, which will be released in 2027.

Gabriela Glapska is a Polish-born, Wellington-based pianist celebrated for her expressive artistry, versatility, and collaborative spirit. An accomplished soloist, chamber musician, and sought-after accompanist, she brings clarity, depth, and nuance to a wide range of musical settings.
 
Gabriela holds a Master’s degree with Distinction from the Feliks Nowowiejski Academy of Music in Bydgoszcz, where she studied under renowned pianist Ewa Pobłocka, and a PhD in Music Performance from Victoria University of Wellington. She currently works as a collaborative pianist at Te Kōkī – New Zealand School of Music.

Whether performing in concert halls, schools, or contemporary music spaces, Gabriela Glapska is known for her refined musicianship, intuitive ensemble playing, and passionate advocacy for music in all its forms.

Photo by Hayden Hockly

events.name: Yoga Nidra
events.venue: Awhi Yoga and Wellbeing Centre, 15 Johnston St., Wellington
events.long_description:
Unwind from the stresses of the week and start your weekend in a state of relaxation. Yoga Nidra, often referred to as "yogic sleep," is a deeply restorative practice that promotes physical relaxation, mental clarity, and emotional balance. It's the perfect way to rejuvenate your mind, body, and soul: your hinengaro, tinana and wairua.

Yoga nidra is a powerful technique that directly works to heal your mind by removing samskaras - untying knots and mental impressions. This practice of learning to relax consciously is well regarded as an antidote for stress, anxiety, poor sleep amongst other health benefits.

Everyone is welcome to experience the profound benefits of Yoga Nidra, and no prior experience is required. For some people, however, Yoga Nidra’s prolonged stillness or internal focus can bring up strong emotions, memories, and/or sensations. You are encouraged to listen and respond in a way that feels safe for you — adjusting your position, keeping your eyes open, grounding yourself, or stepping out of the room at any time.

Yoga Nidra may not be suitable for everyone. If you are experiencing acute mental health challenges, unprocessed trauma, or conditions that make stillness or internal focus difficult, we recommend seeking guidance from a qualified healthcare provider or speaking with the teacher before participating.

events.long_description:
Summer Tour - Kāpiti
Don't miss some Baroque French and Italian delights with NZSO Concertmaster Vesa-Matti Leppänen and Aotearoa New Zealand soprano Anna Leese.

It is astonishing to consider the musical impact Giovanni Pergolesi made, considering he died of tuberculosis at the age of 26. Like Mozart, his early demise quickly became the stuff of legend — hundreds of works were (often falsely) ascribed to this Italian late-Baroque genius, while rumours swirled that his death was the result of murderous jealousy from musical rivals.

Led by NZSO Concertmaster Vesa-Matti Leppänen, we survey some of Pergolesi’s most brilliant opera — La serva padrona, Adriano in Siria, L’Olimpiade and Il prigionier superbo. We are delighted to have Aotearoa New Zealand soprano Anna Leese join us as we delve into music that glories in resplendent Italian Baroque colours and textures.

We complete this magnificent concert with a detour into the French-Baroque, with a suite from Jean-Philippe Rameau's Platée. C’est magnifique!

Generously supported by Ainsley Walter

events.long_description:
Get your festival crew together – COME TOGETHER is rounding out 2026 with a massive end-of-year celebration, FESTIVAL ANTHEMS, bringing some of New Zealand’s most celebrated musicians together to recreate the songs and performances that have defined the world’s greatest music festivals.

From Bob Dylan going electric at Newport and the mud-soaked magic of Woodstock, to the monumental performances of Led Zeppelin and Pink Floyd at Knebworth and the modern-day spectacles of Glastonbury and Coachella, FESTIVAL ANTHEMS is a journey through the music and moments that made festival history.

Pre-sales for the Auckland and Wellington events open at 9am today, with all remaining tickets on sale to the general public from 9am tomorrow via Ticketmaster. Come Together’s end-of-year bashes are always hugely popular, so fans are encouraged to get in quickly – these tickets won’t last.
Taking to the stage for this huge celebration is an all-star line-up featuring Jon Toogood, Milan Borich, Jennie Skulander and Seamus Johnson, backed by the powerhouse Come Together band – Jol Mulholland, Brett Adams, Mike Hall, Matthias Jordan and Alistair Deverick.
Together they’ll tackle an incredible catalogue of festival-defining music from artists including Jimi Hendrix, The Who, Pink Floyd, Led Zeppelin, R.E.M., The Killers, Pulp, Radiohead, Queen, U2 and Arcade Fire, and more.

These are the artists and songs responsible for those unforgettable festival moments – performances that transcended the stage and became part of music history.

From the counterculture revolution of the ’60s and ’70s, through the defining alternative anthems of the ’90s and into the stadium-sized festival performances of today, FESTIVAL ANTHEMS will celebrate the music that has united generations of fans.

Since its inception, Come Together has earned a reputation for bringing classic music spectacularly to life on stage, assembling extraordinary line-ups of New Zealand musicians to perform some of the greatest songs and albums in rock history.

Now, Come Together is taking that spirit out to the festival fields.

Expect huge songs, exceptional musicianship and plenty of moments guaranteed to have audiences out of their seats and singing at the top of their lungs.

And best of all? It’s the ultimate festival experience without the mud, the rain or the portaloo queues.

Gather your festival crew, relive the moments that defined generations and celebrate the end of 2026 with an unforgettable night of live music.

events.long_description:
Overview

Experience traditional Māori healing practices grounded in cultural knowledge in this 2-day Foundational workshop with Manawa Ora

Nau mai, haere mai ki Manawa Ora – The Foundations of Māori Healing and Bodywork.

We invite you to reconnect with the wisdom of our tūpuna and explore the foundations of traditional Māori healing through a holistic, hands-on approach to wellbeing. Grounded in mātauranga Māori, this workshop provides an introduction to the principles, values and practices that underpin Māori healing.

Throughout this workshop, participants will be introduced to mirimiri and romiromi (Māori bodywork), exploring intention and connection in the healing process. We will consider cultural aspects such as whakapapa, tikanga, manaakitanga and wairuatanga.

The workshop offers a supportive space to learn, reflect and develop an awareness of how Māori healing traditions can inform our approach to wellbeing, both for ourselves and for those we care for. Participants will be encouraged to pay attention to their own bodies, deepen their connection with others and appreciate the responsibility that comes with engaging in the healing process.

Over the last 10 years, these workshops have welcomed people from all races and backgrounds. Wānanga/workshops are safe spaces for people to come together for the pupose of learning and healing, guided by tikanga.

At Manawa Ora, we believe that healing begins with connection – connection to ourselves, to one another, to our whakapapa and to the ancient knowledge of Rongoā Māori passed down through generations.

Whether you are beginning your journey into Māori healing or seeking to strengthen your existing understanding, this workshop provides a foundation from which to grow with respect, aroha and intention.

PLEASE NOTE THIS WORKSHOP IS NOT A QUALIFICATION TO PRACTICE.

The 2-day workshop includes:

Cultural philosophies
Whatumanawa (intuitive diagnosis)
Self-awareness and insight
Waiata, karakia and takutaku
Spiritual hygiene
Introduction to mirimiri and romiromi
Group interaction & hands-on practice
Selfcare and tools to maintain wellness

Facilitator Jolie Davis has over 30 years experience in Rongoā Māori; mirimiri and romiromi. Educator, advocate, founder and lead practitioner at Manawa Ora, the largest provider of Rongoā Māori in the Wellington region and one of the largest in Aotearoa (NZ).

WHO THIS WĀNANGA IS FOR:

This wānanga welcomes all with an open heart and an open mind

Individuals on a personal healing journey, ready to discover their inner potential
Māori and Kiwis living overseas seeking reconnection with whakapapa, culture and self-identity.
Those drawn to indigenous healing modalities and philosophy.
Bodyworkers, healers and mainstream practitioners seeking to expand their knowledge and practice

Register at: https://form.jotform.com/joliedavis/Manawaora-Dec2026

Or email joliedavis@manawaora.org for payment options.

Read less

events.long_description:
Frame your favourite work of art for a holiday gift. Bring along a painting and a suitable frame, either a cheapo from Briscoes or a good second hand frame. We will provide all the tools, process and materials to frame your piece of art.

It’s a practical course where you will learn to prepare the frame, cut with a knife, measure and cut a matt with the matt cutter.
You will walk away with your painting framed, ready to hang and some useful knowledge about framing ready for sale, exhibition standards, D rings, swing tags, acid free archival materials, tape, and how to hang a painting on the wall.

What’s included in this workshop:

Demonstration steps to framing your work
assembling the tools you need
choosing and cleaning frames
how to size and cut an acid free mat
what sort of tapes to use for each task
various fixings for hanging and D-rings
replacing acid leaching materials with foam board
cutting techniques
making and attaching labels and swing tags
how to photograph your art

This is a hands-on session where you will learn to cut card, cut a window in the matt board, present, secure, tape, screw in D-ring, tie knots etc. All materials will be provided including: knives, metal ruler, cutting board, crescent board for the mat, mat cutter, tape, d-ring, string.

What to bring along:

your artwork to frame
a suitable frame for the artwork A4 or smaller
enthusiasm

Thirty-minute lunch - bring a packed lunch to have in our historic home or explore the local cafes in Te Aro.

events.long_description:
Christmas is coming, and what better way to celebrate than with beautiful, colourful glass creations? Come into Workspace Ōtaki and make your own unique wine glass charms in a festive palette, creating tiny decorations that will add a personal touch to your celebrations.

In this fun introduction to lampworking, you’ll work with Sarah Brock, the magician of colour palettes, to explore the art of shaping molten glass into miniature creations. Think warm golds, deep greens and rich reds, alongside the classic combination of red, green and white. You’ll learn the basic techniques for working with glass, then let your creativity take over!

There’s no need to make your charms match – embrace the colours, experiment with different combinations and create a collection that’s uniquely yours. Your finished glass pieces will be turned into wine glass charms, with charm holders provided. They’re perfect for adding a playful, handmade touch to your festive table, summer drinks or seasonal gatherings, and make lovely gifts for friends and family.

No previous experience is needed, although some existing skills will help with more intricate projects. Everyone is welcome – just bring your imagination and get ready to play with glass!

Teens aged 12+ are welcome; however, participants under 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

Celebrate Pacific culture in Porirua City!
The festival will begin in style with a parade around the lagoon from 10am, led by the Tongan Brass Band and Tautua Dance.

Head to the stage at the south end of Aotea Lagoon from midday for performances from different cultural groups, and don’t miss out on free miniature train rides between 11am and 3pm.

Each of the 12 Pacific villages celebrated in the Pacific Language Weeks will have stalls selling food and crafts throughout the day.

Free water and sunblock will be available.

Free buses will be provided to and from Aotea Lagoon from Porirua Station and Waitangirua Mall throughout the day. The first bus will depart from Porirua Station at 9.15am, and will run every 30 minutes, with the last collection from Aotea Lagoon at 4.30pm.

Note – if the weather is not looking good, the event will be moved to the Porirua Cook Islands Hall, 14 Mentor Lane, Cannons Creek.

events.name: Pinhole Photography
events.venue: Inverlochy Art School, 3 Inverlochy Place, Wellington
events.long_description:
Did you know that any object that can be made light tight can be turned into a camera? Come along to this Saturday workshop and work with one of our existing pinhole cameras (made from boxes, jars, teapots…) to create evocative photographs.

We’ll work in the darkroom and explore the process of loading your camera with silver gelatin paper, before making exposures in the garden around the historic Inverlochy house & garden, testing different angles and perspectives. We’ll then return to the darkroom to develop your photographic negative, and print it as a positive. You’ll leave the course with some atmospheric pinhole photographs and knowledge of how to build your own pinhole camera.

Bring a packed lunch to have in the historic Inverlochy house or explore the local cafes in Te Aro.

Come along to this Saturday workshop and work with one of our existing pinhole cameras (made from boxes, jars, teapots…) to create evocative photographs.
We’ll work in the darkroom and explore the process of loading your camera with silver gelatin paper, before making exposures in the garden around the historic Inverlochy house & garden, testing different angles and perspectives.
We’ll then return to the darkroom to develop your photographic negative, and print it as a positive.
You’ll leave the course with some atmospheric pinhole photographs and knowledge of how to build your own pinhole camera.

events.long_description:
How to get people to your comedy shows using organic social media

A workshop for Wellington comics!

Most of us got into comedy to be funny on stage, not to run a social media account. But these days, getting people along to see you in person usually involves doing a bit of both.

Samantha Hannah (2026 Billy T nominee) is a stand-up comedian at night and a social media specialist by day. She's keen to share what she's learned about using organic social media to sell out shows, and to swap ideas with other comics in Wellington who are doing the same.

This is a relaxed, practical session where we'll chat about:

Ideas of what to post
Leaning into community when posting online
Turning your existing material into clips
Finding a posting rhythm that fits around your busy life and schedule
How to avoid social media burnout
Nurturing and building an audience long before telling them you have a show you want them to come watch!

All levels welcome! Advanced questions can be submitted by sending a DM via fb or Instagram (@samanthahannahcomedy). You’ll also get lots of opportunities to ask questions on the day.

All proceeds go to the Humorous Arts Trust, supporting the 2027 Wellington Raw Comedy Quest.

events.venue: 15 Dufferin Street, Mount Victoria, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Greccio: The Song
A sacred musical inspired by the life of Saint Francis of Assisi and the first Nativity at Greccio.
Saturday, 5 December 2026
Matinee: 2:00 PM
Evening Performance: 7:30 PM
Venue: Allan Gibbs Centre, Wellington College, 15 Dufferin StreetMount Victoria, Wellington.

Step into the story of Saint Francis of Assisi, whose longing to contemplate the humility and wonder of Christ’s birth led to the first living Nativity at Greccio in 1223. Greccio: The Song is a community faith-and-arts production bringing together live music, choir, drama, movement, and sacred storytelling in a celebration of faith, family, peace, and renewal. At the heart of the musical is Francis’ desire to make the mystery of Christmas visible and tangible: “We wish to see the Child as He was in Bethlehem.” — St Francis of Assisi.

Through music and dramatic scenes, the production follows Francis’ journey of conversion, simplicity, service, and love of Christ, culminating in the Christmas night at Greccio. The musical features music by Douglas Mews, Dr Robert Loretz, and Franciscan friars from the Philippines, with Artistic/Creative Direction by Dave Cecilio and Musical Direction by Cesar Capistrano.

Presented by Vineyard House — A Cultural Ministry of the Centre for Marriage and Family, Greccio: The Song is also part of a special year of commemoration, marking the Jubilee Year of Saint Francis of Assisi (1226–2026) and recognising 60 years of diplomatic relations between New Zealand and the Philippines.

About the production

Greccio: The Song has been created as a community faith and arts initiative, bringing together volunteer actors, musicians, singers, dancers and supporters from across Wellington. It is an invitation to encounter Christmas through the eyes of Saint Francis — not simply as a familiar story, but as a living mystery of humility, joy, peace and love.

Come and let your hearts be renewed.

Presented by: Vineyard House, A Cultural Ministry of the Centre for Marriage and Family

Website: www.marriageandfamily.org.nz⁠

Enquiries: vineyardhouse.nz@gmail.com

events.id: Mozart Requiem (Duncan Druce Completion)-Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki St, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Mozart Requiem (Duncan Druce Completion)
events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki St, Wellington
events.long_description:
Mozart Requiem (Duncan Druce Completion)

Kāpiti Chorale and Capital Choir join forces with orchestra and soloists for a powerful performance of Mozart's final masterpiece.

When Mozart died in 1791 at the age of 35, he left the Requiem unfinished. Within months, his student Franz Xaver Süssmayr completed the work on behalf of Mozart's widow Constanze. His version became one of the most famous and beloved works in the choral repertoire and remains the version most often performed today.

Yet Mozart's surviving sketches continued to raise questions. For more than 200 years, composers and scholars have revisited them, searching for clues to how Mozart himself intended to complete the work.

This concert presents one of the most fascinating answers to that question: the Duncan Druce completion. Created in 1984 by the English composer, performer and musicologist Duncan Druce, it draws on Mozart's surviving manuscript while revisiting parts of the traditional completion. The result offers a fresh perspective on one of the defining works of the classical repertoire.

This special collaboration brings together the combined forces of Kāpiti Chorale and Capital Choir, four outstanding soloists and orchestra for two performances: Saturday 28 November at Te Raukura Performing Arts Centre, Paraparaumu, and Saturday 5 December at the Riley Centre, Wellington High School.

The programme opens with a diverse selection of choral music, including works by Mozart, Salieri, Haydn, Princess Te Rangi Pai and William Dawson, before culminating in Mozart's Requiem.

Soloists

Barbara Paterson, soprano
Ruth Armishaw, alto
Richard Taylor, tenor
Joseph Haddow, bass

This collaboration will be presented in both Kāpiti and Wellington.

Duration: Approximately 2 hours including interval.

events.long_description:
Christmas Fantasia

Saturday 5 December, 7pm

Wellington Cathedral of St Paul, 2 Hill Street, Thorndon


General admission $35 (early bird price $30 until midnight 29 Nov)

Concession $30 (early bird concession price $27 until midnight 29 Nov)

School-aged children free


Nota Bene presents: Christmas Fantasia

From centuries-old texts to traditional carols given new musical life, this concert explores the many ways composers across different eras and cultures have interpreted the Christmas story.

Our programme brings together music from England to Appalachia, with works by Vaughan Williams, Warlock, Dalglish and Ešenvalds. The music ranges from reflective settings and rich harmonies to folk-inspired carols and familiar Christmas melodies.

Vaughan Williams’ Fantasia on Christmas Carols weaves together traditional English carol melodies, some emerging in the choir and others in the accompaniment. In contrast, Malcolm Dalglish’s Star in the East sets three Appalachian Christmas songs for choir and harp, drawing on a different folk tradition.

Joined by baritone Joe Haddow, harpist Michelle Velvin and organist Rachel Malcolm-Swindells, Nota Bene presents a programme that moves between familiar carols and less familiar musical settings.

And what better way to finish than by singing some favourite Christmas carols together? As is our tradition, we hope you’ll stay and join us for refreshments after the concert.

Rachel Malcolm-Swindells - Organ

Michelle Velvin - Harp

Joe Haddow - Baritone

For the first time in 10 years - Mark Moroney & David Shanhun are reuniting for a series of intimate shows across New Zealand in 2026. MARK MORONEY

“A mix of huskiness and honey, Peregian singer, songwriter and acoustic guitarist Mark Moroney’s voice acts like a balm.” Frances Frangenheim, Salt Magazine.

Singer song writer and guitarist Mark Moroney radiates emotion, authenticity and soul.  His style and sound are distilled from a musical melting pot of folk, blues, roots, soul, jazz and pop. 

A favourite at festivals including Woodford Folk Festival (AU), The Mosaic Music Festival (Singapore), & The Bay Of Islands Jazz & Blues Festival (NZ), experiencing Mark live is an unmissable highlight of any show.

DAVID SHANHUN

events.name: Kristin Hersh
events.venue: MEOW, 9 Edward St, Wellington
events.long_description:
Celebrated songwriter Kristin Hersh will return to New Zealand this November / December for a run of four main centre intimate headline shows in support of her forthcoming new album Sugar On Blackstone, out 18 September via Fire Records.

Renowned for her fiercely emotional performances and uncompromising songwriting, Hersh’s New Zealand dates will see her bring songs from Sugar On Blackstone to audiences across the country alongside highlights from her extensive catalogue.

Following on from 2023’s Clear Pond Road, Sugar On Blackstone is a darker yet delicately rendered collection exploring life and death, memory, survival and human connection. Deeply personal and emotionally expansive, the album reflects on the lasting bonds between musicians, family and friends, and the way certain sounds and places can suddenly bring someone vividly back into focus.

New single ‘Dark-Eyed Junco’ offers another striking glimpse into the album, pairing lucid melodies with deeply autobiographical storytelling. Recorded at Stable Sound Studios, the album features longtime collaborators Rob Ahlers (50FOOTWAVE) on drums and Pete Harvey (Throwing Muses) on cello.

Long celebrated as one of alternative music’s most singular voices, Hersh continues to deliver performances that are both intensely intimate and disarmingly powerful - a rare opportunity to experience one of modern music’s most influential songwriters up close.

KRISTIN HERSH Sugar on Blackstone New Zealand 2026 TOUR

South Island /Te Waipounamu shows with ‘On The Door Dunedin’
Sat 28 Nov – Ravensbourne Hall Dunedin 8pm
Sun 29 Nov – A Rolling Stone Christchurch 5 pm

North Island / Te Ika-a-Māui Shows with Plus1:
Fri 4 Dec – Kāhui, St David’s (70 Khyber Pass) 8 pm
Sat Dec 5 - Meow, Wellington 8 pm

Tickets on sale via onthedoor.nz & www.plus1.co.nz

Ministry of House is back in Session at Superfina!

Saturday December 5th from 9pm - 2am.

Join us for the last time in 2026 as we celebrate Crooked Mind’s birthday.

Banging margaritas from the team at Superfina will be on as per usual!

Ben-Jammin is kicking things off with his signature funky jams, while Crooked Mind will be taking you for a ride with his exclusive UKG takeover set to celebrate another lap around the sun.

Joining Ministry of House for the evening is their friend Joe, better known as PocketLipps.

PocketLipps, a Welly-based selector with over two decades behind the decks, is driven by a lifelong obsession with sound. From his early days in Nelson's river-valley raves to serving up a slew of original edits and productions to peak-time slots at Taniwha’s Denfestival, a sold-out sweat pit at Morning People, & jams with the S-Ence, Breakaway, & High Functioning crews, he’s a master of crafting fluid, unexpected journeys. Expect a seamless blend of funky, gritty, & bumpy house, groovy, jacking techno, lush deep house, & the raw, rhythmic power of UK bass & breaks. Currently delving into production, remixing Welly talent, & crafting his own releases, PocketLipps is a DJ who lives for the shared boogie, always found flailing wildly alongside the crowd.

events.long_description:
Tui Brewery Express: The Ultimate Christmas Party!
Climb aboard The Tui Express for the ultimate end of year office Christmas party! This is the perfect workplace celebration that beats the standard corporate dinner, making it an unforgettable scenic journey aboard our premium carriages. It’s the ultimate way to reward your hardworking team, swap out the boring boardroom, thank your favorite clients, and celebrate the year's wins with a spectacular Sunday on the rails.

The undisputed crown jewel of this journey is our passage through the spectacular Manawatū Gorge. With the old highway permanently closed, the rail line offers an exclusive, front row seat to this rugged natural wonder. Watch the dramatic river below and feel the history as we steam through the gorge's tunnels. There is no better place to capture an epic, casual end of year team photo than from our open air viewing platform, the ultimate vantage point for ditching the laptops, hearing the thunderous echo of the steam locomotive, and catching the crisp air of the Manawatū Gorge.

The festive celebrations start the second you step on board! Throughout the trip, our onboard licensed café carriage will be open. Your crew can sit back, relax, and purchase a range of alcoholic and non alcoholic refreshments to toast to your Q4 wins, along with hot espresso coffees and plenty of food, sweet treats, and snacks right from the rails as the stunning scenery rolls by.

Our tracks lead straight to Mangatainoka Station. Upon arrival, step off the platform and stretch your legs with a flat, leisurely 15 minute walk to the world famous Tui Brewery, or hop directly onto one of our dedicated transfer buses waiting for your group. Once at the brewery, relax and toast to your team's successes in the iconic historic grounds. Forget the awkward office Secret Santa and the sad boardroom sausage rolls, your ticket includes a delicious, hearty BBQ buffet lunch and a complimentary Tui beverage (or non alcoholic alternative) to celebrate a successful year together!

Your ticket covers your return journey from your chosen departure station in beautifully appointed premium carriages alongside exclusive rail only views of the Manawatū Gorge, rugged cliffs, and historic tunnels. You will have unrestricted access to the open air viewing platform for unbeatable team bonding, sightseeing, and staff photography, plus full access to the onboard licensed café carriage selling drinks, coffees, and snacks. At the destination, you get a freshly prepared festive BBQ buffet lunch inside the iconic Tui Brewery grounds, one complimentary Tui beer, cider, or non alcoholic beverage, and free transfer buses between Mangatainoka Station and the brewery.

events.name: Sea Glass Jewellery Workshop
events.venue: Inverlochy Art School, 3 Inverlochy Place, Wellington
events.long_description:
Design and create a unique ring with foraged sea glass ‘gems’ while learning and developing core jewellery fabrication techniques. An opportunity to engage in creative recycling by turning seaside flotsam into precious wearable treasures. Experiment with ring textures and forms in silver, brass and/or copper, then set your unique glass ‘gemstone’. Finish up with your choice of polish, including high lustre gloss, steel brushed satin, or darkened antique finishes.

If you can, please beachcomb and bring along some sea glass options - ideally around 1cm wide, and with a flat back. Glass provided if you are in need.

Techniques:

Create a ring with one bezel set foraged sea glass ‘gem’
Use jeweller’s callipers to measure and prepare metal
Use jeweller’s saws or snips to cut and shape metal
Use files and sanding to refine and smooth metal edges and surfaces
Use jeweller’s flame torches to solder join metal pieces
Use Dremel & bench polishers to refine & finish metal casts into wearable jewellery

Materials: Sea Glass, Copper, Brass, Sterling Silver

Project : 1 Ring with sea glass

Includes Silver, Brass and Copper options

events.venue: Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington
events.long_description:
Create gorgeous simple leadlight suncatchers with Lisa Sinclair!

A super fun day-class, ideal as a stand-alone experience, or as a day to get stuck into projects with your tutor at hand.

Beginners choose from a range of achievable patterns and choose their colour palette. They will learn to cut the glass, and prepare it before foiling and soldering each piece, creating a simple elegant colourful glass project.

The aim of this one day class is to leave with a completed small leadlight glass item.

More experienced students may bring existing projects to work on in class - though emphasis will be placed on focusing on the same techniques of flat, nicely soldered simple designs.

This is a warm and friendly class with excellent support and learning for complete beginners and more advanced students. All tools are supplied, though you are welcome to bring your own tools and glass if you have them.

Your materials for your beginner project are supplied as part of your course fee.
Additional materials and tools are available to purchase.

Not suitable for children. Older teenagers (16+) are welcome.

events.name: Standing Strong Handstand Workshop
events.venue: 52/70 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Handstands and getting upside down are good for our upper body, core strength, confidence, resilience and overall body knowledge. 

This workshop is an opportunity to learn the steps towards stable handstands within a safe environment.  This workshop is designed for folks who have interest in and maybe some experience with handstands who are keen to learn the alignment and ways to practice building up to holding them. What a better way to welcome summer than with a new trick to practice on the lawn! 


Workshop will cover:
- falling safely

- exercises to warm up and build upper body, forearm, hand strength

- the biomechanics and alignment of hand balancing

- safe ways to practice handstands at your level

- hands-on assistance

- personal feedback and tips


Your facilitators:JJ Simmons

JJ started standing on her hands about the same time as on her feet. In the past 15 yrs since training in Gymnastics and Physical Education in Denmark and Yoga teacher training, JJ has seen many adults of all abilities (hand)STAND STRONG. She's known for her experience, dynamism and care, and would love to have you join. 

Porou Wise

Porou has been involved in the health and fitness industry for over a decade. Porou’s specialty is in strength and hypertrophy condition training, body composition, general mobility work and boxing. In his spare time, Porou can be found working on his own physique in the gym, out walking with his two British bulldogs, Awhi and Uno.

PARTICIPANTS NEED

basic upperbody stregnth (can hold a plank/prone position)

readiness to try being upside down

events.venue: Lotus Yoga Centre, 91 Ruapehu Street, Paraparaumu, Paraparaumu
events.long_description:
Finish the year feeling grounded, energised, and ready to shine your light through Kundalini Yoga, breathwork, meditation and sound.

Celebrate the completion of our Journey Through the Chakras with a special afternoon dedicated to the Aura (the Eighth Chakra) through the transformative practices of Kundalini Yoga and the deeply restorative sounds of a Gong Bath.

The Aura is your energetic field—the subtle electromagnetic energy that surrounds your body. A strong, balanced aura helps you feel grounded, confident, resilient, and protected, allowing you to move through life with greater vitality and ease. Through movement, breathwork, meditation, and sound, we'll strengthen this energetic field, leaving you feeling centred, uplifted, and radiant.

Whether you've joined us throughout the chakra series or this is your first workshop, you're warmly welcome. Come and finish the year feeling grounded, energised, and ready to shine your light into the world.

Kundalini Yoga | 1:30pm – 3:00pm | Experience a 90-minute Kundalini Yoga class designed to strengthen and balance your aura through breathwork (Pranayama), dynamic movement and postures, meditation, and deep relaxation.
Herbal Tea Break | 3:00pm – 3:30pm | Take time to relax, enjoy a cup of herbal tea, oracle cards and connect with others in a welcoming and supportive environment.
Gong Bath | 3:30pm – 4:30pm | Lie back, get comfortable, and allow the soothing sounds and vibrations of the gong to guide you into a deeply restorative state of relaxation. A gong bath can help calm the nervous system, release stress, and leave you feeling refreshed and centred.

Choose the experience that suits you—you are welcome to attend either the yoga or the gong bath sessions or enjoy the full afternoon.

Suitable for beginners and experienced practitioners alike - no experience with yoga or sound healing needed. Modifications are offered throughout the yoga class.
Bring an open heart, a yoga mat, blanket, water bottle and anything you need to feel cozy + supported.
Whether you're joining the entire afternoon or just one session, you'll leave feeling calmer, clearer, and more deeply connected to yourself.

Spaces are limited, so bookings are recommended.

Investment:

$35 Yoga | $30 Gong Bath | $55 Both

Special discounted ticket option: $100 two person special - bring a friend with you to attend the yoga and the gong session. Must select this ticket option for the discount to apply (i.e. both people must book together)

If you want to pay by cash on the day or by bank transfer, please send an email to mel@prosperityyoga.co.nz to book your place.

A Deep Listening Soundbath inside the sublime acoustics of Erskine Chapel

$45

Limited door sales for $50

Please bring a yoga mat, pillow, eye mask and blanket - or whatever it is you need to feel most warm and comfortable. Dress comfortably.

Discover the transformative effects of sound therapy with this 1.5hr-hour sound bath experience.

During this session, participants will be surrounded by the resonant vibrations of gongs and taonga pūoro, carefully designed to induce deep states of relaxation and calm. As you settle into the experience, allow the soothing tones to wash over you, releasing tension and promoting a sense of inner peace.

Scientific studies have highlighted the benefits of sound therapy in reducing stress and promoting overall well-being. The rhythmic patterns and overtones of the gongs and other instruments can help entrain brainwaves, leading to a meditative state and improved mental clarity.

Beyond the immediate effects, many participants report experiencing lasting benefits such as improved sleep, reduced anxiety, and enhanced mood following a gong bath session. By immersing yourself in the healing vibrations of the sounds, you can tap into a deeper sense of relaxation and rejuvenation.

Whether you're looking to unwind after a long day or explore new avenues of self-care, this 1.5hr-hour soundbath offers a unique opportunity to reconnect with yourself and find balance amidst the hustle and bustle of daily life. There will be cups of tea available afterwards to help us integrate and ground.

Sound baths are safe and supportive for most people. However, please consult your doctor or mental health professional before attending if you:-have a pacemaker or other implanted medical device
-live with epilepsy or a sound-sensitive condition
-are in the first trimester of pregnancy
-are experiencing severe or unmanaged mental health challenges (such as psychosis, schizophrenia, or PTSD)If you have recent injuries, surgeries, or other health concerns, let me know so we can make sure you’re comfortable.

Everyone responds differently to sound. If at any point during the session you feel overwhelmed or uncomfortable, you are welcome to sit up, move gently, or step outside. Your wellbeing always comes first

About Us

Briar Prastiti

Greek–New Zealand composer and vocalist Briar Prastiti is known for her diverse musical practice, spanning contemporary orchestral and chamber music, film, theatre, songwriting, and electronic production. Her most recent compositional project was an epic work for massed choir, solo voice, and taonga pūoro, commissioned for the opening ceremony of Te Matapihi ki te Ao Nui, Wellington Central Library. In this work, Briar performed as solo vocalist alongside Alistair Fraser on taonga pūoro. 

Alistair Fraser

Alistair is a practitioner of ngā taonga pūoro. He has performed, composed, and collaborated with many of Aotearoa's finest artists, across genres of music and alongside various artistic disciplines since 1999. He worked as a maker, researcher and performer of ngā taonga pūoro nationally and internationally for the past 26 years. He has toured as a soloist with the New Zealand Symphony Orchestra, worked recently with Good Company Arts, Shayne Carter with the Zealand Dance Company for their work Home, Land and Sea, and also for David Long and Stephen Gallagher's score for the Emmy Award winning TV series Secrets at Red Rocks.

Erika Grant

Erika is a musician and astrologer based in Te Whanganui-a-Tara. She has 35+ years musical experience, in bands, orchestras and various ensembles. She has created music for film, parades and overnight soundbaths. Erika has an interest in the healing properties of sound for mental and physical wellbeing, which she currently explores through her gong bathing practice

events.name: Arahina Mai Tour - Hine + Jullekke + Casual Healing
events.venue: St Peters Village Hall, Cnr Beach Rd and Ames St, Paekākāriki
events.long_description:
Nau mai to this special triple line up collaboration between soulful songstresses Julia Cooper (Jullekke & Dr Reknaw) and Gigi Crayford (Hine) alongside Nikau Te Huki (Casual Healing) in a stripped back, intimate and spellbinding solo setting. Sit back, take a breath and ground into a night of medicine music.

Julia Cooper is an Aotearoa singer, songwriter and multi-instrumentalist. Best known as the front woman and co-founder of Aotearoa’s well loved band ‘Dr Reknaw’. Julia has recently birthed her solo project ‘Jullekke’. She is recognised for her smooth, velvety & sultry vocal tones, catchy trance bass and guitar riff. Her lyricism features an ethereal quality mixed with messages of empowerment, consciousness and healing. With flavours of roots, soul, world tastes and funk. Julia describes her music as “vibrational food for the soul of listeners. Melodies to gift and uplift”.

CASUAL HEALING - Nikau Te Huki is a unique composer, producer and multi-instrumentalist based in Pōneke, Aotearoa - and his soulful solo project goes by the name of Casual Healing. As a true sonic missionary, Nikau is creating a soothing “golden-era sound” as part of his mission to heal with his music. The songs of Casual Healing emphasise life lessons of aroha, peace and unity through powerful lyrical scribe woven into smooth reggae, soul rhythm. This infusion creates a unique nostalgic vibe, creating a captivating and comforting essence that evokes recollections of moments shared with friends and whānau. Casual Healing's goal is to create songs that “make people feel like they want to be better people”, drawing inspiration from Bob Marley, who showed us the power of compassion and simplicity.

Nau Mai ki te Ao o HINE - A Māori witch folk noir weaving of Taonga Pūoro, sonic storytelling & poetry. This enchanting songstress radiates strength through vulnerability & the connections awakened from returning to our roots. A blend of Te Reo Māori & English, this powerful set will echo through your bones & reverberate your soul. HINE recently released her debut EP 'KA MUA KA MURI' with a national tour, leading the EP to place #1 on the Aotearoa Official Top Charts. This will be HINE’s last tour of the North Island before a move to Ōtautahi and then travel internationally.

Arahina Mai meaning ‘Guide Me” speaks to the artist's devotion to spirit through their craft and devotional practice of music & art as ritual & medicine. This show will be a deeply intimate, intentional & community centric setting of heart & healing.

Shows include:

5th Dec - Pōneke Wellington at a secret location
6th Dec - Paekākāriki at St Peters Village Hall
8th Dec - Whanganui at Private Residence
10th Dec - Raglan Arts Centre
11th Dec - Thames - Buddhist Church
13th Dec - Tāmaki - Auckland Unitarian Church
17th Dec - Oakura - Dawn
18th Dec - Napier (Gigi & Aslan) Paisley Stage (No Julia)
19th Dec - Opunake Playhouse Theatre

Overview

Step away from the day-to-day and build a clear, practical plan for the next quarter.

2027: Make It Your Best Business Year Yet!


The Launch Plan – Plan for Growth, Profit & Freedom

Are you busy running your business but not necessarily getting where you want to go?

It's easy to get caught up in the day-to-day. You're working hard, making decisions and keeping everything moving, but when was the last time you stopped to look at whether your business is actually taking you where you want to be?

The Launch Plan is a practical, interactive business planning workshop designed to help you step away from the daily demands of running your business and get clear on what needs to change.

We'll start by looking back at 2026, then build a picture of what you want your business and life to look like by December 2027.

From there, we'll identify the gaps between where you are now and where you want to be, so you can focus on the things that will make the biggest difference.

What we'll work through
Review 2026: What's worked, what hasn't and what have you learned?
Create your 2027 vision: What do you want your business and life to look like by the end of next year?
Identify your business gaps: What's currently stopping you from getting there?
Decide what needs attention: Which gaps are having the biggest impact on your profit, growth or freedom?
Choose your priorities: What are the three most important things to focus on?
Build your 90-day plan: Turn those priorities into practical actions for January–March 2027.
What you'll walk away with

A clearer picture of where your business is today, a vision for where you want to take it and a practical 90-day action plan to help you get there.

This isn't a day of sitting and listening. You'll be working on your own business, sharing ideas and making decisions about what really matters.

events.venue: San Fran, Wellington
events.long_description:
UK music’s biggest underdogs, indie rock juggernauts The Reytons, keep charging forward on their unstoppable rise. Having flirted with overseas territories successfully over the past 5 years, the band are now heading out on their very first World Tour, and have announced their return to Australia and New Zealand this November and December

Renowned for their raucous live shows, and touted by many as the best live act of their generation, the British 4-piece pride themselves on their honesty and pure energy. Having taken their native UK by storm, with number one albums, sold out park shows and major festival headlines, the lads from Rotherham are taking on the world with their upcoming world tour.

In 2025 alone, they toured the UK, headlined Tramlines Festival and the iconic Wembley Arena. The upcoming world tour is a huge statement for a band who have hurdled every obstacle with nothing other than blue-collar grit and determination. It cements them as a band at the top of British music. The Reytons also recently announced their fourth studio album A Love Letter To A Broken Town - due for release in July.

Rooted in the rough around the edges humour and honesty of everyday life, The Reytons continue to channel their origins into everything they do, and A Love Letter To A Broken Town sees them staying true to those roots while pushing their sound forward with confidence and intent.

“I honestly feel like this album is the best we’ve ever done!” explains frontman Jonny Yerrell. "A lot of bands and artists like to change direction later in their careers, but that’s just not us. We absolutely love the style of music we make, the social commentary aspects and the people who turn up to jump around with us. Why would we change? Expect more, just bigger and better with a few surprises on the side! "

San Fran holds a Supervised License, meaning minors are welcome to attend events at San Fran so long as they are accompanied by a legal guardian at all times whilst at the venue. Minors are of course not allowed to purchase alcohol under any circumstance.

About the Liner Shipping Game

The Liner Shipping Game is a cutting-edge, simulation-based training solution that provides hands-on insights into the intricacies of liner shipping operations. It simplifies real-world processes, making it suitable for both industry newcomers and seasoned professionals.

Participants navigate realistic, customisable scenarios reflecting operational disruptions, key decision points, and challenges.

Key features include:

Booking Uptake: Manage dynamic booking requests while balancing capacity constraints and customer expectations.

Vessel Stowage: Plan and optimise vessel space, considering cargo types, weight distribution, and voyage schedules.

Terminal Operations: Coordinate port activities, manage container flows, and ensure efficient cargo handling.

The game's interactive nature provides practical experience and enhances skills in teamwork, revenue management, and process optimisation

.

For a closer look at the LinerGame experience, watch our official highlight video on YouTube.

Why Attend?

The Liner Shipping Game offers a rare opportunity to learn from top-tier industry experts while collaborating with peers from across the logistics sector. By attending, you will:

Understand Complex Operations: Experience the decision-making process of running a liner shipping service, covering end-to-end operations.

Enhance Your Skills: Improve your teamwork, strategic thinking, and revenue management capabilities in a fast-paced, risk-free environment.

Navigate Real-World Scenarios: Encounter challenges like port strikes, equipment shortages, weather disruptions, and overlapping booking regions, gaining critical insights into effective problem-solving.

Network with Industry Peers: Connect with like-minded professionals in a collaborative setting, exchange ideas, and explore new opportunities within the shipping and logistics sector.

Who Should Attend?

This workshop is ideal for:

Logistics & Supply Chain Professionals: Individuals involved in operations, planning, and management.

Importers & Exporters: Professionals managing supply chain activities and interested in gaining a broader understanding of liner shipping dynamics.

Freight Forwarders & Shippers: Those seeking to enhance their service offerings by understanding carrier operations better.

Port & Terminal Operators: Professionals responsible for terminal management and coordination.

From the platinum-selling Bizarre Ride II the Pharcyde to the genre-defining Labcabincalifornia, classics like "Passin' Me By," "Runnin'," "Drop," "Otha Fish" and "Ya Mama" continue to inspire generations of artists and remain essential listening more than 30 years later.
The Pharcyde's legacy extends far beyond their own catalogue. They helped open the door for a more playful, soulful and inventive style of hip hop, collaborated with a then- emerging J Dilla, worked with visionary director Spike Jonze, and proved that creativity could be just as powerful as bravado. Their influence can still be heard across modern hip hop, while their timeless live show continues to win over audiences around the world.
Featuring Imani, Slimkid3, Fatlip and DJ Cee Brown, this is your chance to experience one of hip hop's defining groups live.
Secure your tickets early and don't miss the opportunity to see true pioneers of alternative hip hop when they return this December.

events.name: An Evening with Guenther Steiner
events.venue: The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Former Haas F1 boss Guenther Steiner brings his new live show, ‘No Team Orders’, to The Opera House in Wellington. The 2026 season gave Formula 1 new cars, new rules, and new teams on the grid. Days after the final race, Guenther unpacks it all. He shares his take on which teams cracked the rule changes first and which young drivers stood out. Expect blunt opinions and stories from inside the paddock. 

Guenther has spent more than 30 years in motorsport. He started in rallying, working with drivers such as Colin McRae, a three-time Rally New Zealand winner. He later ran Jaguar Racing in Formula 1. Then he built the Haas team from scratch and led it for a decade. You might have seen him on the Netflix series ‘Formula 1: Drive to Survive’, where his colourful honesty made him a fan favourite. He famously claims he has never watched it. He has also written two books, ‘Surviving to Drive’ and ‘Unfiltered’. Today, he is CEO of the Red Bull KTM Tech3 MotoGP team. 

The evening is a live conversation on stage, followed by an audience Q&A. Bring a question of your own and put it to Guenther directly. Join whether you’ve just discovered him or you’ve followed Formula 1 since you were a wee one. Book your seats, and leave with enough insider secrets to impress at the work Christmas party.

To celebrate the tenth anniversary of their critically-praised and fan-adored debut album 'Asleep In The Machine', Yugambeh/Gold Coast-based duo Bootleg Rascal have just announced a five-date New Zealand tour, taking place in December off the back of their Australian tour.

Stopping off in Wellington, Auckland, Christchurch and Queenstown, the band will perform tracks from 'Asleep In The Machine', plus their most recent and fourth self-titled studio album, and all the classics from their extended discography.

Pub Sing - where the audience turns into the choir at the pub, with a live rock band,

No sheet music, no experience needed, and absolutely no solos.

Katy reveals three songs on the night (usually a crowd-pleaser, a ballad, and a banger), and even if you don’t know them, you’ll pick them up fast with colour-coded lyrics on screen.

From his beginnings in New York’s late-80s underground to legendary Ibiza residencies and dancefloors around the world, the Grammy-winning DJ, producer and label boss has built an extraordinary career on his instinct for the dancefloor. Support from Ügly Disco, rooted in the UK’s mid-90s warehouse rave scene and drawing from Chicago house, UK northern deep house and 90s tech house, twisted through gritty disco edits and half-forgotten underground anthems. Raw, rhythm-driven and built to move a room.

events.long_description:
Seasons for Growth Adult Retreat Weekend
Grief touches every life, yet each person's journey through loss is unique, and Christmas can be a time when we feel loss most acutely. Whether you have experienced a bereavement, the end of a relationship, or a significant shift in your life, this gentle weekend retreat offers a sacred space to pause, reflect, and find companionship on the path of healing.

Drawing on the Exploring Seasons of Grief programme, participants will explore grief as a natural and evolving process, much like the changing seasons of the year.

Through reflection, guided conversation, quiet time, and the peaceful surroundings of the Home of Compassion, we will consider the many ways grief can affect our hearts, relationships, faith, and sense of identity. Whether your loss is recent or long ago, this retreat invites you to acknowledge your experience with compassion, deepen your understanding of living with loss, and discover sources of hope and renewal.

events.long_description:
UK psychedelic heavyweights Uncle Acid & The Deadbeats return to Australia and New Zealand this December, bringing their dark, hypnotic live show to stages across the country.
The brainchild of Kevin Starrs, Uncle Acid & The Deadbeats have spent over a decade carving out a singular space within the global heavy music landscape. Since emerging in 2009 from the depths of the British underground, the band have built a reputation for their unmistakable fusion of warped psychedelic pop, downer blues and doom-metal intensity.
Too bold and idiosyncratic to be easily defined, Uncle Acid’s sound is steeped in haunting melodies, layered vocal harmonies and eerie, cinematic arrangements, offset by crushing riffs and a persistent sense of unease. It’s a sonic world that feels both deeply nostalgic and completely otherworldly, cementing Uncle Acid & The Deadbeats as one of the most compelling live acts in contemporary rock.
With their last visit to our shores in 2020, Australian audiences can expect a set that traverses the band’s cult catalogue, delivered with the immersive intensity that has made them a must-see worldwide.

events.long_description:
The Undercurrent presents The Bon Temps Bros!

Acoustic Cajun blues and Louisiana music. Three musicians with a shared love of syncopation, improvisation and the spaces between.

It started with a few tunes around a Kāpiti kitchen table. Those sessions grew into a repertoire that wanders between Cajun rhythms, blues and country roots traditions. Music that sounds a lot like musicians having fun.

Richard Klein is a fiddler and vocalist from Orange, New Jersey, whose musical journey took him through the UK and into France, where he discovered Cajun music. Wellington-based since 1997, he founded the city's much-loved Americana jam sessions and has played with the Le Blanc Brothers Cajun Band and Kiwi outfit T-Bone (playing Womad this year).

Pip Payne wears a few musical hats: blues club founder, bandleader, vocalist, swing music lover, roots gospel devotee and slide guitarist. His playing draws on a lifetime spent exploring the backroads of American roots music.

Al Norman brings accordion, snare and the unmistakable clang of the Cajun triangle. A fixture on the Wellington music scene, he's played with bands as varied as Smokeshop and the Laura Collins Band, and is currently a member of bands including The Waratahs and The Rag Poets.

Friday Dec 11

Doors 7pm

Music 7:30pm

$20

Tickets available online and at the door!

Snacks, a range of refreshing drinks, tea & coffee, and of course...books available for purchase!

Build Your Own Bánh Mì: Creative Vietnamese Fillings

What makes a great Bánh Mì? Is it the crispy baguette, the fresh herbs, the tangy pickles, or the delicious fillings?

In this hands-on workshop, you'll discover the endless possibilities of Vietnam's most famous sandwich by learning how to prepare a variety of popular Bánh Mì fillings, including:

✔ Hands-on cooking experience

✔ Insights into Vietnamese food culture

Supporting Community Through Food

events.long_description:
Whitireia Park Community Snorkel - FREE
Dive in with us this summer! 🌊

Discover the underwater world of Whitireia Park at our free community snorkelling event! Explore beautiful seagrass beds, rocky reefs and the marine life that calls them home — you might even spot a seahorse!

🐠 Everyone welcome, including beginners!

We provide all the snorkelling gear and experienced guides to help you enjoy a safe and memorable experience in the water.

A few things to know:

Participants must be aged 8+ and confident swimmers.

Anyone under 16 must be accompanied by an adult who also takes part in the snorkel.

Bring your togs, towel, refreshments and anything else you need to enjoy a day by the coast.

🤿 How to take part

Registrations open at 9.45am on the day. Come along to book your snorkel time — spots may fill up quickly!

Each tour takes approximately 1 hour and 30 minutes, including getting ready, snorkelling and returning your gear afterwards. The last tour departs at 1.45pm.

Make a day of it and enjoy exploring the coast and taking part in other activities!

This free event is brought to you in partnership with Greater Wellington Regional Council.

📍 Getting there

By bike: Why not enjoy the beautiful coastal track? It's approximately 5km from Titahi Bay Boat Club to the snorkel site.

By car: The road to the snorkel site is narrow and can be challenging when traffic is busy. Where possible, please carpool and drive carefully. Clearly signposted parking will be available throughout the day.


🌦️ Weather and event updates

Snorkelling is weather-dependent, and events may be cancelled, postponed or moved to another location. Please check this Mountains to Sea Wellington Facebook event listing for updates before heading out.

................................................................................................................................

This snorkelling event is delivered under the national Mountains to Sea Conservation Trust's Experiencing Marine Reserves programme.

The programme is Adventure Activity Certified (AA0534).

Photo Credit: Red Beanie Photography

events.name: Natural Textured Rings for Christmas - Taster Class
events.venue: Workspace Studios Ōtaki, 2 Arthur Street, Ōtaki, Ōtaki
events.long_description:
Craft a beautiful, personalised ring - a perfect treat for yourself or a thoughtful gift for someone special! This three-hour taster class is designed for absolute beginners, though all skill levels are welcome to join the fun.

You will be guided step-by-step through the core techniques of silversmithing. You'll start by practicing basic texturing, cutting, and shaping with traditional jewellery tools using copper or brass. Once you’re comfortable, you'll move on to crafting your final piece in sterling silver.

In this hands-on workshop, you will learn to:
Measure your finger and cut the metal strip to the perfect length.
Create unique surface textures using a rolling mill, hammers, punches, and even natural elements like feathers or leaves. You can stamp names, dates, whatever you like.
Work safely with a jeweler's torch for heating and soldering the metal.
Finish your ring with sanding and polishing techniques.
By the end of the class, your beautiful, custom-made sterling silver ring will be ready to wear.

This is an ideal activity for individuals, groups of friends, or visitors to Ōtaki looking for a creative experience.

What's Included:
All practice materials (copper or brass).
A strip of sterling silver for your final ring.
All necessary consumables (sandpaper, solder, chemicals).
Use of all tools and equipment.

Important Note for Young Makers: Kids aged 12 and over are welcome to attend, but anyone under the age of 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver. Extra metals are available for purchase in the studio.

events.long_description:
Christmas in Wellington has its own character. Long evenings, pōhutukawa in bloom, the end of the working year in sight, and the anticipation of a well-earned summer break with whānau and friends.

The Bach Choir of Wellington invites you to mark the season with an afternoon of festive Christmas music. You can expect the brilliance of voices and exciting programme that reflects quiet moments of wonder and all the energy and colour of Christmas.

The concert begins with Daniel Pinkham’s Christmas Cantata, drawing on medieval and Renaissance musical motifs full of rhythmic vitality. The music moves from sparkling excitement, through moments of mystery, before culminating in an exuberant “Gloria in excelsis Deo”!

Bring your singing voice! Alongside the choir and the brass band, you will be invited to join in a selection of our favourite carols, filling the church with Christmas cheer.

Join us for an afternoon of uplifting music, glad tidings, and our special guests, Aotearoa’s leading, brass ensemble, the Wellington Brass Band!

events.name: Silver Clay for Christmas - Taster class
events.venue: Workspace Studios Ōtaki, 2 Arthur Street, Ōtaki, Ōtaki
events.long_description:
Join us to try out this amazing technique and make a gift for yourself or your loved ones :-)

Metal Clay is an incredible product made from metal particles mixed with an organic binder. When your pieces are shaped - just like a modelling clay - they are then dried and fused in the kiln. That process takes only a few minutes so there is plenty of time in this 3-hour class to complete your projects.

Beginners start with simple pendants/earrings. It is much easier to start with flat projects so we leave the rings for the advanced class!

Jewellery pieces can be textured and shaped however you like, and if you don't like your piece simply squish it and start again - Art Clay Silver is the ultimate recyclable material!

Included in the course fee is 5 grams of fine silver clay, enough to make a pendant or earrings, or a collection of small charms.

Extra findings such as earring hooks and chains will be available to purchase (you can also make your earring hooks if you are feeling adventurous).

This class is great for kids also but an enrolled parent or caregiver must accompany any person under the age of 16.

events.id: Bach, Bells & Christmas — Concert by Cantoris and Festival Singers of Wellington-71 Woburn Road, Hutt Central, Lower Hutt 5010, New Zealand-Humanitix
events.name: Bach, Bells & Christmas — Concert by Cantoris and Festival Singers of Wellington
events.venue: 71 Woburn Road, Hutt Central, Lower Hutt 5010, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Celebrate the richness and wonder of Christmas with Cantoris and Festival Singers of Wellington, as they join forces for an evening of music that spans centuries, crosses continents and brings together joyful celebration and quiet reflection.

Conducted by Ingrid Schoenfeld, who directs both, the two choirs will be accompanied by well-known organists Jonathan Berkahn and Heather Easting. Together, they bring a wealth of musical experience to a programme filled with colour, contrast and seasonal spirit.

At the heart of the concert is Cantata V of J.S. Bach’s Christmas Oratorio, opening with the chorus Ehre sei dir, Gott, gesungen. This part of Bach’s great Christmas work follows the journey of the Magi, exploring their search for the newborn Jesus and the image of light shining through darkness. Its combination of exuberant choral writing, storytelling and reflection offers a vivid encounter with the Christmas narrative.

Felix Mendelssohn’s Die deutsche Liturgie brings another dimension to the evening. Its Kyrie, Gloria and Sanctus move from prayerful appeal to praise and adoration, revealing the composer’s gift for expressive melody and beautifully shaped choral textures. These three movements offer moments of warmth, grandeur and stillness.

Music from Aotearoa New Zealand has a special place in this concert. Jonathan Berkahn’s Four Christmas Songs brings together Unto us a Son is given, Meditation – rorate coeli desuper, And art thou come with us to dwell? and How sweet the angels song. The sequence invites listeners to consider Christmas through proclamation, contemplation and a sense of wonder. With Berkahn also appearing as one of the evening’s organists, the concert offers a particularly personal connection between the music and its composer.

Jenny McLeod’s Vulcan and Indigo II, from her Sun Festival Carols, add further New Zealand colour.

Philip Stopford’s Lully, Lulla, Lullay provides a tender, haunting contrast. Drawing on the Coventry Carol text, it captures both the intimacy of a lullaby and the poignancy beneath the Christmas story. John Gardner’s Tomorrow shall be my dancing day brings buoyant rhythm and infectious vitality, while Mykola Leontovich’s Carol of the Bells sparkles with its familiar repeating motif and gathering excitement.

From Bach’s joyful praise to the delicacy of a lullaby, this programme offers much to discover and enjoy.

St James’ Anglican Church in Lower Hutt provides a welcoming setting, with comfortable seating and a crisp acoustic in which to savour the combined voices and accompaniment.

Make time in the busy December season for an evening of shared listening, musical discovery and festive warmth. Join Festival Singers of Wellington, Cantoris, Ingrid Schoenfeld, Jonathan Berkahn and Heather Easting for Bach, Bells and Christmas: a celebration of the season through the expressive power of choral music.

[Children 18 years and under enter free when accompanied by a paying adult.]

YURT PARTY - Street Party Music | Wellington
Street party music!

Born in Otautahi, Yurt Party have spent the past few years riling up dancefloors around Aotearoa, playing backyards, clubs and festivals including Electric Avenue, CubaDupa, Twisted Frequency, Shipwrecked and Woodford Folk Festival (Aus).

Their high-energy instrumental music takes inspiration from Balkan, Latin and Dub. The tunes are made for dancing, leaving you with a smile on your face and sore legs in the morning!

2026 kicked off with their Australian debut at Woodford Folk Festival, where they were tagged as one of the festival's surprise favourites. They also won Best Band with a Fiddler at the Golden Fiddle Awards in Tamworth. Now they're back home with new music recorded at The Surgery in Wellington, and taking the new tunes around the motu.

Joined by DJ Everybody co-founder of festival circuit regulars 'Tempo Schmempo' collective with dynamic sets of house, techno, disco, and funk.

Come have a dance!

Brisbane - Black Bear Lodge - 23 Oct with JR Dynamite (DJ) & Jam and Scones

Wellington - San Fran - 12 Dec with Everybody (DJ)

events.venue: Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington
events.long_description:
Create gorgeous simple leadlight suncatchers with Lisa Sinclair!

A super fun day-class, ideal as a stand-alone experience, or as a day to get stuck into projects with your tutor at hand.

Beginners choose from a range of achievable patterns and choose their colour palette. They will learn to cut the glass, and prepare it before foiling and soldering each piece, creating a simple elegant colourful glass project.

The aim of this one day class is to leave with a completed small leadlight glass item.

More experienced students may bring existing projects to work on in class - though emphasis will be placed on focusing on the same techniques of flat, nicely soldered simple designs.

This is a warm and friendly class with excellent support and learning for complete beginners and more advanced students. All tools are supplied, though you are welcome to bring your own tools and glass if you have them.

Your materials for your beginner project are supplied as part of your course fee.
Additional materials and tools are available to purchase.

Not suitable for children. Older teenagers (16+) are welcome.

events.venue: 10 Kent Terrace, Mount Victoria, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
events.long_description:
G

To celebrate the end of the year and the festive season Wellington Film Society is putting on a screening of The Muppet Christmas Carol. We'd love for families to come along to enjoy this film together. Tickets are free. Seats are unallocated, just enter the cinema on the day and find a seat. We start films on time and do not play trailers.

BOOKING DETAILS


First phase - Monday 9 November to Friday 20 November: Wellington Film Society member only booking (members can book up to 5 seats and can bring non-members guests).

Second phase from 20 November: public booking - anyone including non-members can book up to 5 seats directly.

We will make all seats bookable because we’re enabling members to bring guests and non-members to attend.

The point of opening this screening up to the public is to enable children to have a fun film experience so please act in this spirit. You can book up to five seats, but please don’t book more seats than you need is as many people can come as possible.

FILM DETAILS

There have been countless adaptations of Charles Dickens’ A Christmas Carol, but no other stars Kermit the Frog, Miss Piggy, Gonzo, and Rizzo the Rat! The Muppets put a hilarious and chaotic spin on the most iconic Christmas story in literature. The film is elevated by the central performance of the only human cast member, Michael Caine as miserly Ebenezer Scrooge, who delivers on the promise he made when he took on the role, "I'm going to play this movie like I'm working with the Royal Shakespeare Company. I will never wink, I will never do anything Muppety. I am going to play Scrooge as if it is an utterly dramatic role and there are no puppets around me.”

Directed by Brian Henson, son of Muppet creator Jim Henson, The Muppet Christmas Carol follows the miserly Ebenezer Scrooge (Michael Caine) as he is visited by three ghosts on Christmas Eve, forcing him to confront the ghosts of Christmas past, present and future – and perhaps discover a little festive spirit along the way. Featuring a superb collection of songs by Paul Williams (Phantom of the Paradise) the film manages to balance genuine emotional heft with the anarchic silliness that makes the Muppets so enduringly wonderful.

More than thirty years on, The Muppet Christmas Carol has become regarded as one of the best and most beloved Christmas films. A film for children, adults, Muppet enthusiasts, and anyone who could do with a little boost towards the end of the year.

✨Explore a daily spiritual practice for more joy, wisdom, peace✨

HU is an active meditation mantra that can help quiet the mind, open the heart, and awaken a deeper sense of love, wisdom, and inner awareness.

HU (pronounced like hue) is known as the sound behind all sounds—a carrier of divine love between the Creator and you. It’s not limited to any religion or belief system and can enhance any path you’re already on.

you are welcome to stay for relaxed spiritual conversation and refreshments afterwards.

No previous experience is needed. Everyone is welcome to join, listen, and take part in whatever way feels comfortable.
