events.name: Tony Martin: From Seedling to Sensation – How New Zealand Creates the Apples and Pears of the Future
events.venue: Hawkes Bay,Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Tony Martin: From Seedling to Sensation – How New Zealand Creates the Apples and Pears of the Future
Have you ever bitten into an apple and wondered where it came from?

Not the orchard.

Not the supermarket.

But the very first idea that eventually became the fruit in your hand.

Creating a new apple or pear variety isn't something that happens overnight. It can take years of research, testing, patience and innovation before a single piece of fruit reaches consumers.

Join Tony Martin, Chief Executive of Prevar, for a fascinating behind-the-scenes Learning Lunch exploring how New Zealand is helping shape the future of fruit.

From understanding changing consumer tastes to developing entirely new varieties, Tony will reveal the remarkable journey from seedling to supermarket shelf and the science, strategy and creativity that make it possible.

You'll discover how some of New Zealand's most successful apple and pear varieties were developed, what makes a fruit variety stand out in global markets, and why innovation in horticulture requires both long-term thinking and bold decision-making.

Best of all, this isn't just a conversation.

Guests will enjoy a guided tasting of different apple and pear varieties, offering a rare opportunity to experience firsthand the flavours, textures and characteristics that breeders spend years developing.

This is a wonderful opportunity to look at something familiar in a completely new way.

Meet Tony 🎤

Tony Martin is Chief Executive of Prevar, the innovation and commercialisation company behind many of New Zealand and Australia's leading apple and pear varieties. With more than two decades of leadership experience across agribusiness, innovation and international markets, Tony works at the intersection of science, consumer insight and global horticulture, helping bring world-class fruit varieties from concept to consumers around the world.

What We'll Explore
• How new apple and pear varieties are created
• The science and strategy behind fruit innovation
• What consumers really want from future fruit varieties
• The journey from research programme to supermarket shelf
• Why innovation often requires patience, persistence and long-term thinking


📍 Location: FoodEast-Haumako, Hawke's Bay
📅 Date: Wednesday 10 March 2027
🕙 Time: 11:00am – 1:30pm
☕ Refreshments: Lunch and fruit tasting included
🎟️ Tickets: $95 per person

👥 Hosted by Love Heart
Warm, welcoming learning experiences designed for people who enjoy discovering new ideas and meeting interesting people.

events.name: BLOODBATH (SWE) + NERVOCHAOS (BRA) - WELLINGTON
events.venue: Valhalla, Wellington
events.long_description:
Two of the world's most respected names in extreme metal are joining forces for an unmissable New Zealand invasion. Swedish death metal icons Bloodbath are coming to New Zealand in 2027, bringing Brazilian extreme metal veterans NervoChaos as their main support.

BLOODBATH
SWEDISH DEATH METAL
Founded in 1998, Bloodbath has become one of the defining names in modern death metal. Originally formed by members of Opeth, Katatonia and Paradise Lost, the band has built a formidable reputation through landmark releases including Resurrection Through Carnage, Nightmares Made Flesh, The Fathomless Mastery, Grand Morbid Funeral and Survival of the Sickest. Renowned for their uncompromising sound, crushing HM-2 guitar tone and devastating live performances, Bloodbath remain one of Sweden's most celebrated exports in extreme music.

NERVOCHAOS
BRAZILIAN EXTREME METAL DESTRUCTION
Formed in São Paulo in 1996, NervoChaos have spent more than three decades forging a reputation as one of South America's most relentless extreme metal forces. With an extensive catalogue of acclaimed releases and countless tours across Europe, Asia, North and South America, the Brazilians have earned worldwide respect for their ferocious live performances and unwavering dedication to the underground. Fusing old-school death metal with blackened aggression and thrash intensity, NervoChaos have continued to evolve while maintaining the raw, uncompromising attitude that has defined the band since its formation.

With Bloodbath and NervoChaos teaming up for a double headline tour this is a rare opportunity to witness two international extreme metal forces on the same bill.

events.name: National Dog Database
events.venue:
Willeston Conference Centre
Wellington, Wellington Region
events.long_description:
Overview

Using the NDD to its full potential. Get hands-on and use realistic scenarios to explore and learn the functionality of the NDD website.

Description

The National Dog Database went live 1 May 2006 and provides a countrywide overview of dog control in New Zealand.

It brings great benefits to the animal control industry including the ability to;

track classified owners and dogs
monitor the national infringement count of owners
look up out of district dog and owner details
locate dogs when only limited information is available;
and contribute accurate data to ongoing policy analysis.




Outline

Using the NDD training environment (it looks just like the live NDD system but contains fictional data), the NDD training workshop will explore the following areas:

Background – the history of the NDD project – from 2003 to present
TA Extracts – how information gets from your local system to the NDD and the feedback the NDD will give you as well as the different types of files you can send
Searching – how to get the best out of the search screen and how to interpret the results of your search
The ToDo List – what are errors, warnings, information and system notifications? Detailed discussion about what you need to do with them.
Automated and Manual Linking – National Duplicates – comparing dogs and owners that look similar but are in different districts, and how to manually search for other duplicates.
Security – passwords, adding new users or expiring old accounts, as well as the owner protected status.
Reports – what reports you can run and how to use them in your TA. Did you know there are 18 different kinds of reports that you can generate from the NDD and that you can use some of them to compare your TA’s data to a national summary?




Learning outcomes

With a focus on maintaining data quality, participants in the workshop will learn to use the NDD as a tool for animal control and further understand the importance of administrative roles at the local level. Following the completion of the NDD training workshop, NDD users will have the confidence to use the database to its full potential.




Audience

This course is suitable for managers, team leaders and users with animal control administrator responsibilities.




Prerequisites

To participate in the NDD training workshop you must be a registered user of the National Dog Database (employee or contractor). You are required to bring your own laptop.

Two of the world's most respected names in extreme metal are joining forces for an unmissable New Zealand invasion. Swedish death metal icons Bloodbath are coming to New Zealand in 2027, bringing Brazilian extreme metal veterans NervoChaos as their main support.

BLOODBATH
SWEDISH DEATH METAL
Founded in 1998, Bloodbath has become one of the defining names in modern death metal. Originally formed by members of Opeth, Katatonia and Paradise Lost, the band has built a formidable reputation through landmark releases including Resurrection Through Carnage, Nightmares Made Flesh, The Fathomless Mastery, Grand Morbid Funeral and Survival of the Sickest. Renowned for their uncompromising sound, crushing HM-2 guitar tone and devastating live performances, Bloodbath remain one of Sweden's most celebrated exports in extreme music.

NERVOCHAOS
BRAZILIAN EXTREME METAL DESTRUCTION
Formed in São Paulo in 1996, NervoChaos have spent more than three decades forging a reputation as one of South America's most relentless extreme metal forces. With an extensive catalogue of acclaimed releases and countless tours across Europe, Asia, North and South America, the Brazilians have earned worldwide respect for their ferocious live performances and unwavering dedication to the underground. Fusing old-school death metal with blackened aggression and thrash intensity, NervoChaos have continued to evolve while maintaining the raw, uncompromising attitude that has defined the band since its formation.

With Bloodbath and NervoChaos teaming up for a double headline tour this is a rare opportunity to witness two international extreme metal forces on the same bill.

events.long_description:
English singer-songwriter Beth Orton is one of the best-known practitioners of folktronica. This is a subgenre where folk songs are set to electronic beats. This unique sound, popularised in the late ‘90s and early ‘00s, can be heard when Beth travels to Wellington in March. Her tour takes her to Whakarauika Wellington Town Hall where audiences will get to hear intimate and adventurous song writing. 

Beth has released nine studio albums including the most recent ‘The Ground Above’ (2026). Thirty years into her career she is still evolving as an artist. Music blog Pitchfork proclaimed, “Orton is one of the UK singer-songwriters of her generation working at the highest level right now.” Collaborations with the likes of Andrew Weatherall, William Orbit, and The Chemical Brothers indicates he is not just your average singer-songwriter.

events.id: Miss Saigon-Michael Fowler Centre, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
events.name: Miss Saigon
events.venue: Michael Fowler Centre, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Tragic pop-musical Miss Saigon hasn’t played Wellington in over 15 years. Fabulous soloists, a 40-strong local choir, and a live orchestra are rectifying that in 2027. G&T Productions brings a semi-staged concert to the Michael Fowler Centre. This format puts the performers and music front and centre. Set during the final days of the Vietnam War in 1975, Miss Saigon is a heartbreaking, bold, and gripping musical theatre piece. 

From the songwriting team behind ‘Les Misérables’, Miss Saigon is a tragic love story of a young Vietnamese woman (Kim) who falls in love with an American soldier (Chris). Saigon falls, and their story unfolds alongside the Engineer, a ruthless survivor chasing his own ‘American Dream’. 

Wellingtonian Maya Handa Naff plays Kim. She has previously sung the role in the United States. Maya is an actor, director, and teacher whose Wellington performance credits include ‘Wicked’ (Glinda) and ‘Les Misérables’ (Eponine). Director and actor Kyle Chuen plays Chris. Laurence Mossman returns as Thuy after performing the part on Australian and international tours. Expect to hear songs like I’d Give My Life for You, Why God Why, and Bui Doi.

Together, Julia and Anthony’s personal messages leave audiences feeling comforted and inspired.

The spectacular venue played an important role in the orchestra's story since its earliest days so WIUO is thrilled to present the concert there. The performance will feature beloved classics, new material and, inevitably, a few trademark surprises.

Fans already know that WIUO’s gloriously eclectic repertoire moves effortlessly between pop hits, rock classics, country ballads, waiata Māori, Pacific music, indie favourites and unexpected deep cuts. Attendees at the March 2027 gig can also expect spontaneous comedy and plenty of audience participation.

The Wellington International Ukulele Orchestra was founded in 2005 by friends Age Pryor and Bret McKenzie, what began as an informal gathering of ukulele enthusiasts at Wellington's Deluxe Café quickly evolved into one of New Zealand's most celebrated live acts. Over the following decade WIUO captivated audiences across Aotearoa, Australia, the United States, China and Japan. It released four bestselling EPs and an album, collaborating with internationally renowned artists, and inspiring thousands of people to discover the joy of making music.

The Weave - Sheol
The first weekend game for The Weave LARP campaign, a futuristic fantasy game in Wellington.

About this Event



*********

Don’t look down. The sky is clear and blue. When you breathe in for the first time after your months-long voyage, the fresh air tastes impossibly sweet.

Don’t look down. A single star rests in the heavens, yellow and warm. Shoals of silvery fish dart through picturesque waves.

Don’t look down. The islands quake and churn beneath your feet. Alerts appear hourly on your screens about impossibilities, measurements beyond rational explanation.

You look down. What lies beneath? What might be unearthed from the strata of the past? What has been forgotten? And what should have remained buried?




What's going on?

A week ago, three ships landed on the planet called Etsen. The Highmit Research Mission has journeyed to this planet, across the vast dangers of space, to help the planet’s scientists understand the impossibility of measuring a second star in a 100 kilometre diameter patch of their sky.

You landed at Scion. It’s small, compared to the average communities on your home planets. Not even 5000 people. But it’s the largest settlement in Etsen’s affected zone. And it’s a strange new environment for many of you, perched on an island in a temperate archipelago.

The research mission’s primary team has already set up their main base of operations in Scion. Alongside the limited number of specialised Etsenite scientists, they are beginning initial research into the planet’s anomaly.

A few days ago, a small settlement in the affected zone, Axis, reported abnormal technological errors. Yesterday, a different settlement, closer to Scion, reported similar malfunctions.

You are members of the secondary research team dispatched to Axis. Your task sounds simple enough.

Identify the cause of the errors.
Prevent them from spreading further.

But, just like the impossible second star, you suspect nothing is as simple as it seems.




*********




OOC information

Sheol is the first weekend game of The Weave LARP.

The game is running on 20-21 March 2027 in Wellington at Khandallah Scout Hall (11A Station Road, Khandallah, Wellington 6035).
The game runs for 2 full days. There is no overnight accommodation. You will have the opportunity to leave a small amount of gear on-site overnight.
Players are self-catered. We are currently working with a generous volunteer to see if we can cater our crew. The crew will get confirmation closer to the start of the game if we can cater them.
The game is open to new player-characters, pending available tickets.

This game is 18+.




Tickets

Tickets go on sale Tuesday 29 September at 7pm through Eventbrite. Participants who attended the July 2026 day game will have early bird access. You must buy a ticket to secure your place. Ticket costs do not include Eventbrite fees.

Players: $110 ($100 with NZLARPs member discount)
Crew: $60 ($50 with NZLARPs member discount)


Find the NZLARPs discount code by logging into your NZLARPs account and looking at the event page ( https://nzlarps.org/events/detail/356). If your NZLARP membership details are still pending or you can't figure out how to log into the website, ask us for the code in an email at .

events.long_description:
WELLINGTON INTERNATIONAL UKULELE ORCHESTRA 2027
After ten years in ‘deep hibernation’, the much-loved Wellington International Ukulele Orchestra (WIUO) will reassemble for a spectacular show at the newly restored Te Whare Whakarauika Wellington Town Hall on Saturday 20 March 2027.

This special event reunites two treasured Wellington icons, both relishing being back in action, with stronger foundations, sexier décor and refreshed acoustics.

Founded a bit by accident in 2005 by friends Age Pryor (The Woolshed Sessions, Congress of Animals, Fly My Pretties) and Bret McKenzie (Flight of the Conchords, The Black Seeds), what began as a joyful experiment quickly evolved into one of New Zealand's most celebrated live acts.

Over the following decade, the Orchestra captivated audiences throughout Aotearoa and around the world, releasing four bestselling EPs and an album, collaborating with internationally renowned artists, and inspiring thousands of people to discover the joy of making music.

Following an extensive touring schedule that included New Zealand, Australia, UK, the United States, China and Japan, the band put their ukes on ice to explore other instruments and new creative pursuits.

But the call of the ukulele is strong - asked if they’d regroup for one special all-ages show to celebrate Te Whare Whakarauika Wellington Town Hall’s triumphant reopening, the Orchestra’s answer was an instant “holy hecking ukeballs YES”.

The band said: "That's what it's always been about for us: getting everyone together, lifting the roof and finding magic in the moment through amazing music."

The reunion feels especially fitting for a group that sprang from the creative milieu of mid-2000s Te Whanganui-a-Tara. The Town Hall, City Gallery, Central Library and Michael Fowler Centre all formed part of the Orchestra's journey as it grew from local curiosity to international phenomenon.

Heidi Morton, GM Events & Experiences at WellingtonNZ, says: "The Wellington International Ukulele Orchestra holds a special place in Wellington's cultural story, and we're delighted to welcome them back as part of the celebrations marking the reopening of Te Whare Whakarauika Wellington Town Hall. We know many people will be eager to join in for this one – so be sure to get your tickets quickly as we definitely expect a sell-out.”

Audiences can expect everything they remember and love about the WIUO: soaring harmonies, dazzling musicianship, inventive arrangements, spontaneous comedy and plenty of audience participation. The performance will feature beloved classics, new material and, inevitably, a few trademark surprises.

The band’s repertoire takes a gloriously democratic approach to the global songbook, moving seamlessly between pop hits, rock classics, country ballads, waiata Māori and Pacific, indie treasures and unexpected deep cuts. Proud champions of the unique instrument and its surprising range, the WIUO proves that a room full of ukuleles can be moving, virtuosic, funny and unexpectedly powerful, often all in the same song.

The first rule of the Wellington International Ukulele Orchestra remains unchanged: “If you know the words, sing along.” And the second: “If you don’t know the words, sing along.”

The Wellington International Ukulele Orchestra also features Andy Morley-Hall, Bek Coogan, Carmel Russell, Daniel Yeabsley, Deanne Krieg, Francis Salole, Gemma Gracewood, Megan Salole, Nigel Collins, Samuel Auger and Stephen Jessup.

Presented by Venues Wellington’s Live in WLG, this special reunion celebrates not only the return of the Wellington International Ukulele Orchestra, but also the reopening of a venue that has long been at the heart of the capital's cultural life.

For one night only, Wellingtonians and visitors will once again have the chance to gather and celebrate together in one of the city's most treasured communal spaces.

THE WELLINGTON INTERNATIONAL UKULELE ORCHESTRA
7:30PM SATURDAY 20 MARCH, 2027, WELLINGTON TOWN HALL. ALL AGES.

events.id: NZSQ — Strings in the Earth & Air-Te Whare Whakarauika Wellington Town Hall-Wellington NZ
events.name: NZSQ — Strings in the Earth & Air
events.venue: Te Whare Whakarauika Wellington Town Hall
events.long_description:
A concert of traditional Irish airs and folk melodies will be presented at a concert at the newly opened Wellington Town Hall in April 2027. Join Tom Delany and Dave Flynn for traditional and contemporary works in NZSQ — Strings in the Earth & Air. Tom Delany will play the uilleann pipes, while Dave Flynn will be on the guitar. ‘Uilleann’ means ‘elbow’ in Irish. The uilleann pipes are powered by the elbow, pumping air instead of the Scottish bagpipes that use the lungs. 

The concert takes its name from James Joyce’s poetry collection ‘Chamber Music’. Most of the poems in the collection revolve around the twin themes of love and music. ‘Strings in the earth and air’ is the poem that opens the collection. The concert forms part of New Zealand String Quartet’s In Collaboration series. With roughly one in six Kiwis being of Irish heritage, there are enduring connections between Ireland and Aotearoa. This concert brings those ties to life through poetry, song, and strings.

Tom Delany plays uilleann pipes, guitar, and bouzouki, and sings. As a founding member of Irish ensemble FOURWINDS, he has toured the world. He is known for playing traditional Irish music in a daring, free-flowing style. Dave Flynn is a composer and guitarist who offers a unique blend of Irish trad, minimalism, and jazz. His work has been performed by leading ensembles in venues across the globe.

events.long_description:
There’s never been a group, let alone a supergroup, in rock history quite like it. Now you get to see a tribute to their huge success. In 1988, a group of five rock legends joined together to form The Traveling Wilburys. They were Bob Dylan, George Harrison, Jeff Lynne, Roy Orbison, and Tom Petty. 
Across four years, they produced two mega albums, a slew of hits and won a Grammy. They never toured. Now, a tribute band, The Travelling Wilburys Collective, is on tour and it’s visiting the St James Theatre in Wellington. 
You’ll get to hear some of their biggest and most celebrated hits like Handle with Care, End of the Line, Tweeter and the Monkey Man, and She's My Baby. Along with these original hits, you’ll get served classics from each individual artist and the groups they were in. That includes The Beatles, The Heartbreakers, and ELO. 
The Traveling Wilburys Collection bring together the collective talents, excitement, and magic that the original quintet had to offer. Join them for a night of fun and nostalgia.

Rabbit Island, Tasman
events.long_description:
Overview

Join me on this luxury retreat to reset and re-energise. Workshops, yoga, meditation and plenty of free time with nourishing kai awaits.

You've built a successful life. But somewhere along the way, you lost yourself in it.

You're capable, accomplished, and by most measures, thriving. And yet you're exhausted in a way that a good night's sleep doesn't fix. Rest feels like something you have to earn. Slowing down feels risky. And the idea of a whole weekend just for you might feel almost indulgent. That's exactly why you need this.

A weekend to stop, breathe, and come back to yourself.

Retreat to the stunning Waimea Plains, just 20 minutes from Nelson. This isn't a hustle-harder weekend. It's not a productivity programme with a prettier view. It's two and a half days of genuine restoration, honest conversation, and the kind of clarity that only comes when you finally stop long enough to hear yourself think.

Through facilitated workshops, daily yoga and meditation, nourishing plant-based food, and plenty of unstructured time in one of New Zealand's most beautiful settings, you'll reconnect with who you are beyond what you achieve, and leave with the tools to sustain that beyond the weekend.

Book this unique weekend retreat if:

You've achieved a lot, but you're quietly exhausted and wondering if this is really it
You can't remember the last time you did something just for you, without guilt
Rest feels like something you have to earn, and you haven't quite earned it yet
You're functioning well on the outside but running on empty on the inside
You know the pace is unsustainable but you don't know how to slow down without losing ground
Your identity is so tied to what you do that you're not sure who you are without it
You're successful by every measure, and yet something important feels missing
You need more than a holiday, you need space to think, breathe and reconnect with yourself

What you'll come away with:

A clearer sense of who you are beyond your roles and achievements
Tools to navigate burnout, build resilience, and sustain your energy
A calmer, quieter mind — and practical ways to keep it that way
Permission to rest, and the ability to actually do it without guilt
A personal plan to carry the weekend's insights into your everyday life
Access to my online learning suite to support you across the year ahead

Where and when

Friday 2 April 2027 (from midday) – Sunday 4 April 2027
Appleby House & Rabbit Island Huts, Waimea Plains, 20 minutes from Nelson.

Set on 25 acres of open plains with 360-degree views of the Richmond Ranges, Mt Arthur, and the Waimea Estuary, this is one of those places that slows you down the moment you arrive. Walking and swimming at Rabbit Island, the galleries and cafés of Mapua, and the conveniences of Richmond are all minutes away, but you won't feel the need to rush anywhere.

Accommodation ranges from ensuite luxury rooms to beautiful, private huts with outdoor baths. All rooms have queen beds, a fridge, and tea and coffee making facilities. Shared and private spaces throughout the property give you room to be social or solitary, whichever you need most.

Your package includes:

2 nights' accommodation in your own room
Airport transfers
Facilitated workshops and coaching with Jess
Daily yoga and meditation
Use of the onsite sauna
Healthy, delicious plant-based meals throughout the weekend
Walking and free time to explore the surrounding environment
Goody bag with books and online resources to take home
Access to Jess's online learning suite to sustain you across the year
Massage and additional activities available to pre-book (additional cost)

Accommodation Options

VIP rooms and luxury ensuite huts: $2,495 per person.

Private standard double hut and glamping tent: $1,945 per person. (Three luxury huts all with double beds share two external luxury bathrooms and an outdoor bath.)

20% discount available for early birds using the code EARLYBIRD; limited time only.




Your host: Jess Stuart

I'm an author, keynote speaker, national newspaper columnist, and work-life balance expert with a background in corporate HR spanning 15 years. I've written eight books, including Burnout to Brilliance and Calmony, and I've spent the better part of my career helping high-achieving women build success that's actually sustainable.

I'm also a retreat fanatic. Getting away from daily life has always been where I've had my biggest breakthroughs, which is why, after years of being asked, I finally started running my own. I believe that tapping into your potential doesn't mean doing more or changing who you are. It means uncovering what's already there, and learning to trust it.

I'd love to have you join me.

events.long_description:
The New Zealand professional premiere of one of Andrew Lloyd Webber’s most celebrated musicals is coming to Wellington. Sunset Boulevard takes centre stage at the newly restored Wellington Town Hall in April. Local company WITCH Music Theatre is presenting an epic site-specific production as part of the venue’s grand reopening programme. 

In a major coup for the production, acclaimed Tony Award-nominated performer Keala Settle will be playing the main role, Norma Desmond. Keala has strong iwi links to New Zealand so she sees this opportunity as a homecoming. She is best known for her role as Lettie Lutz in ‘The Greatest Showman’ and for her powerhouse performance of the Golden Globe-winning song “This Is Me” from the film. 

Sunset Boulevard has earned major acclaim across Broadway and the West End, including seven awards from 11 Tony Award nominations for its original 1994 Broadway production. It’s 2023 revival won seven Olivier Awards from 11 nominations. The production, designed specifically for the Town Hall’s refurbished auditorium, marks the New Zealand professional premiere of the musical.

events.venue: The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Described as the ultimate ladies’ night out, Menopause the Musical has been delivering laughs across the globe for years. Now the fun-filled musical about ‘the change’ returns to Wellington for one night.
Set in a department store, four women meet by chance while shopping for a black lace bra. Though they couldn’t be more different, they quickly discover a shared bond over memory loss, hot flushes, night sweats, and mood swings. What follows is a hilarious, heart-warming musical told with love, laughter and the greatest hits of the 60s, 70s and 80s. The laughter-filled 90-minute production gets audiences out of their seats dancing and singing along to clever parodies of beloved pop classics.
Winner of over 40 Tony Awards, Menopause the Musical has entertained more than 17 million fans worldwide. It’s been translated into nine languages and performed in more than 500 cities. The show’s enduring appeal lies in its honesty, hilarity and heart. It celebrates women everywhere and turns shared experiences into shared joy.

events.long_description:
The last in a trilogy of cycling-themed plays skids into The Wellington Opera House in May.  Writer-director Gregory Cooper and seasoned Kiwi actor Mark Hadlow collaborate once more to bring their cycling trilogy to a close. The one-man play 'WOBIL: Wise Old Bugger in Lycra' follows previous installments ‘MAMIL: Middle Aged Man In Lycra’ and ‘GOMIL: Grumpy Old Man In Lycra’. Expect familiar faces, trademark physical comedy, plenty of laughs, and a fair bit of heart too.
Mark is one of New Zealand’s best-known actors. You might have seen him on screen in ‘King Kong’ or ‘The Hobbit’, or a host of live professional theatre shows on stages around the motu.  Gregory's past work includes ‘That Bloody Woman’. This latest chapter sends Wayne on his hardest hill climb yet. With help, and hindrance, from a few old friends and enemies, he’s determined to go out in a blaze of lycra glory. Get ready for one last spin through friendship, ageing, and resilience.

events.long_description:
Presented by: Destroy All Lines
British legends Squeeze are returning to New Zealand in April 2027 with their Tried, Tested and Trixies Tour, celebrating 53 years of classic songwriting and standout music hits from one of the UK’s pioneers of Brit-pop music.
Founded in 1974 by Chris Difford and Glenn Tilbrook, Squeeze are one of pop’s best-loved bands with a catalogue of sky-high classics such as ‘Up the Junction’, ‘Tempted’, ‘Cool for Cats’, ‘Another Nail in My Heart’ and ‘Labelled with Love’, whose live shows are legendary and, as The Guardian wrote, “pop perfection”.
Squeeze remain one of the most revered and distinctive music outfits in UK pop history. Led by the unparalleled songwriting duo Glenn Tilbrook and Chris Difford, their legacy spans over five decades of masterful songwriting, stellar live performance, and cultural impact; between 1978 and 1996 they had no fewer than 11 singles in the UK Top 40, with six in the Top 20. Many more of their songs have been woven into the very fabric of the British songwriting tradition – alongside those of The Beatles and The Kinks – influencing everyone from Lily Allen to The Killers.
Coming to New Zealand to mark 50+ years of Squeeze and celebrate the release of their new album, Trixies, will be Glenn Tilbrook, bassist Owen Biddle, percussionist Steve Smith, keyboardist Stephen Large, drummer Simon Hanson, guitarist Leon Tilbrook and backing vocalist Danica Dora.

Following his first New Zealand shows in 2025, Craigie returns with his latest album, I Swam Here, out now on Zabriskie Point Records. Written and produced by Craigie, the album was recorded between New Orleans and Astoria, Oregon, bringing together the musical spirit of the Gulf Coast with the quieter sounds of the Pacific Northwest.
 
For more than a decade, Craigie has built a devoted following through his warm, sharply observed songwriting and live shows that pair music with humour and storytelling. His touring has taken him across the U.S., Europe and Australia, with appearances at Newport Folk, Pickathon, Edmonton Folk Festival and High Sierra, and performances alongside artists including Gregory Alan Isakov, Sierra Hull, Brett Dennen and Jack Johnson.
 

I Swam Here follows 2024’s Pagan Church, Craigie’s collaboration with TK & The Holy Know-Nothings, which spent six weeks at #1 on the Americana Albums chart. Expansive yet intimate, the new record marks another chapter for Craigie while retaining the sincerity and conversational songwriting that have become central to his work.
 

Craigie returns to San Fran, Wellington on Thursday 15 April and The Tuning Fork, Auckland on Friday 16 April 2027, returning to the same venues that hosted his first New Zealand tour in 2025.

events.long_description:
The iconic bluesman and one of Australia’s most revered live performers, Lloyd Spiegel, brings his world-famous guitar work, soulful voice, and deeply human storytelling to New Zealand in April 2027!

This is a rare chance to experience world-class artistry up close, in an intimate listening-room setting designed for focus, connection, and a true love of live music.

“A guitarist almost without peer, Spiegel deconstructs how the blues guitar is supposed to operate… makes sweet love to it, then kicks it out the back door.” — Australian Guitar Player

“Spiegel is ALL presence, authority, rhythm and drive. He epitomizes control, soul and passion with white-hot ferocity and blazing instrumental mastery.” — The Age (Melbourne)

📍 Friday 17 April 2027 @ Old St Paul's - Wellington

Seated concert

Doors 7 PM | Show 7:30 PM

Family friendly, with discounted tickets for under 18s

DON'T miss your chance to experience live music at its finest!

ABOUT LLOYD SPIEGEL

Lloyd Spiegel is a travelling bluesman at heart — a guitarist by trade and a storyteller by nature. The 14-time Australian Blues Award winner has spent a lifetime refining a signature style that honours the deep traditions of blues while pushing the music forward in his own unmistakable voice.

His performances move effortlessly between jaw-dropping guitar work, powerful vocals, humour, and deeply human moments, creating shows that feel personal, generous, and completely alive in the room.

With ten albums to his name and an international touring career spanning North America, Europe, Japan, and beyond, Lloyd is equally respected on world-class festival stages and in intimate listening rooms. At home in Australia, he is recognised as a trailblazer for blues music and has been named among the 50 greatest Australian guitarists of all time.

Whether playing to thousands or a quiet, attentive audience, Lloyd Spiegel has a rare gift for connection — making every performance feel like a shared experience, and every listener feel part of the story.

ABOUT THE VENUE

Located in the heart of Wellington, the magnificent Old St Paul’s is one of New Zealand’s most beautiful historic churches, renowned for its stunning timber architecture, soaring vaulted ceilings and warm, intimate atmosphere.

For one special night, Nightingale Concerts transforms this breathtaking heritage landmark into a listening room, bringing audiences together to experience the extraordinary musicianship, stories, and energy of Lloyd Spiegel up close.

Expect an evening of remarkable guitar playing, powerful blues, laughter, and the kind of connection that makes live music so special.

🎟️ Tickets are ON SALE NOW! These intimate concerts have been selling out in venues around the world. With limited seating available, don't miss your chance to experience Lloyd Spiegel live in Wellington!

events.name: The Curious Case of Benjamin Button The Musical
events.venue: St James Theatre, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Every second counts. That’s the theme of The Curious Case of Benjamin Button. Having taken London and New York by storm, the hit musical is now making its way to Wellington, New Zealand. 

Described by WhatsOnStage as “The best British musical in decades” the show is an enchantingly beautiful and truly unordinary story. It follows Benjamin Button who is born old and bound to the fate of growing younger each day, Benjamin wants nothing more than to live a little life. But will he ever find a place to belong?   

The Olivier Award-winning musical is based on the 1922 short story by F Scott Fitzgerald. The story also inspired a 2008 movie. Now for the first time out of Broadway and the West End it travels to Australasia and Wellington has scored the premier. It brings a big heart, a foot-stomping score, and 15 remarkable actor-musicians who, among them, play 30 instruments. Get ready for a sweeping live score and a show epic in scale but intimate in feeling.

events.venue: Meow Nui, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Presented by: Destroy All Lines

St. Paul & The Broken Bones are a powerhouse soul ensemble from Alabama known for their electrifying live shows and impassioned vocals. Formed in Birmingham in 2011, the band features Paul Janeway (vocals), Jesse Phillips (bass), Browan Lollar (guitar), Kevin Leon (drums), Al Gamble (keyboards), Allen Branstetter (trumpet), Chad Fisher (trombone), and Amari Ansari (saxophone).

Their new self-titled sixth album marks a creative renewal—melding the band’s adventurous spirit with a return to soulful, song-focused roots. Recorded at the legendary FAME Studios and produced by Eg White (Adele, Celine Dion), the record blends psych-funk grooves, gospel-tinged ballads, and cinematic rock flourishes. Tracks like “Sushi and Coca-Cola” and “Going Back” reflect both personal introspection and the band’s deepened identity after a decade of evolution.

St. Paul & The Broken Bones have shared stages with The Rolling Stones, Lizzo, and Black Pumas, and performed at major festivals like Coachella, Glastonbury, Lollapalooza, and Bonnaroo. Even Sir Elton John took notice, inviting them to perform at his Oscar party. Blending rock & roll, soul, R&B, and more, the band continues to captivate audiences around the world.

events.name: Kia Mau
events.long_description:
Kia Mau is an arts festival that showcases innovative Indigenous performances. Held every two years, the festival lights up Wellington's winter. See contemporary performances by leading Tāngata Whenua , Tāngata Moana, and global Indigenous artists. The two-week festival includes dance, theatre, music, and visual art. Audiences can expect to be challenged and thrilled by new work from Aotearoa and beyond.
Kia Mau was first held in 2015, founded by two leading Aotearoa creatives. Hone Kouka (Ngāti Porou, Ngāti Kahungunu, Ngāti Raukawa, Kai Tahu) is the Artistic Director and Chief Executive. Mīria George (Ngāti Kearoa, Ngāti Tuara, Ngāti Awa, Ngāti Kūki ‘Āirani) is the Executive Director.
Hone and Mīria describe themselves as innovators. They push boundaries, redefine forms, and forge new paths. They say the festival is not just a platform for presentations, it’s a hub for kōrero and whanaungatanga . The festival has a strong influence on many artists and plays an important role in shaping New Zealand’s contemporary arts scene. “Kia Mau has continued to thrive because of the imagination and commitment of our artists. And of us to them,” says Mīria.

We are excited to announce that the NZSLTA conference will take place at Victoria University of Wellington.

2027 is a big anniversary year!

We invite you to join us to celebrate three milestones in NZSL teaching history:

👐35 years since the first formation of NZSLTA (1992)

📖 30 years since the launch of the Dictionary of NZSL (1997)

🎓30 years of the Certificate in Deaf Studies: Teaching NZSL at VUW (1997)

Over this time, the NZSL teaching profession has grown and had a huge impact on breaking down communication and attitude barriers for the Deaf community. Growth of this field has also supported many new professional opportunities and services.

This conference is an opportunity for NZSL teachers to celebrate our progress, reflect on current challenges and think together about future directions. The conference theme is:

“Energising NZSL Teachers”

We aim to make an exciting conference programme that will show the depth and diversity of knowledge, skills and creativity in our teaching community.

We look forward seeing you here in Wellington!

events.name: Bat Out of Hell — The Musical
events.venue: Michael Fowler Centre, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
The explosive stage show, Bat Out of Hell — The Musical, swoops onto the stage of Wellington’s Michael Fowler Centre in August 2027. The musical is based around songs from Meat Loaf’s 1977 album ‘Bat Out of Hell’. It marks the 50th anniversary of its release.  Featuring an all-Kiwi cast and a live band, it covers a uniquely theatrical song list from the 50-year-old album. Expect a fun, chaotic musical that defies traditional theatre rules.   

A wild, post-apocalyptic world offers a backdrop for the show. The story follows Strat, an 18-year-old rebel leader of a gang called The Lost, who falls in love with Raven, the sheltered daughter of the city's tyrannical boss, Falco. Packed with massive tunes, you will hear hits like ‘I’d Do Anything for Love (But I Won’t Do That)’, ‘Paradise by the Dashboard Light’, ‘Two Out of Three Ain't Bad’, ‘Dead Ringer for Love’, ‘It’s All Coming Back to Me Now’, and the title track.   

The Bat Out of Hell album evolved from writer and composer Jim Steinman’s early university workshops. Despite initially being rejected by mainstream radio, it became one of the biggest-selling albums in history. It’s an album that takes up space: big, brash, and loud, like the musical itself.   

Ben McDonald, the producer of the musicals Chicago and Menopause the Musical, teams up with Stewart and Tricia Macpherson (The Best Exotic Marigold Hotel and Green Day’s American Idiot musical) to produce the New Zealand tour.

Celebrate the creative genius and musical talent of one of the greatest pop singers. The Michael Jackson HIStory Show promises to be a riveting live performance. The full-scale production at the Opera House pays tribute to one of the most significant cultural figures of the 20th century. Expect a stellar live band, choreographed dancers, and authentic costumes. 

Garth Field is at the centre of this performance. He’s often described as electrifying in his role as Michael. Garth is a triple-threat performer with impeccable vocals, dancing, and acting. 

The show tracks Michael’s journey from his early days as a member of the Jackson 5 to his groundbreaking theatrics in the 80s. It goes on to acknowledge his continued domination of pop culture into the 21st century. Hear all the hits like Thriller, Billie Jean, Bad, Beat It, Don’t Stop Til You Get Enough, They Don’t Really Care About Us, and many more.

events.id: Fashion Thrift Society | Wellington November 27th-TSB Arena, Wellington -Ticket Master
events.name: Fashion Thrift Society | Wellington November 27th
events.venue: TSB Arena, Wellington
events.long_description:
FASHION THRIFT SOCIETY – AUSTRALIA’S BIGGEST CURATED FASHION MARKET

FASHION THRIFT SOCIETY IS COMING TO WELLINGTON

Wellington, Fashion Thrift Society is taking over TSB Arena on Saturday 27th of November from 10AM–4PM.

Australia’s biggest curated fashion market brings together vintage, preloved and independent fashion, local creatives, food, music, beauty, experiences and more - all under one roof.

WHAT’S ON

75+ curated stalls featuring vintage, preloved, designer and independent brands

Thousands of unique pieces to shop

Second-hand treasures alongside products from independent small businesses

Local food vendors

Music and DJs at select events

Beauty, fashion and creative activations that vary from city to city

SHOPPING AT FTS

Every stall at Fashion Thrift Society is run by an individual business or independent stall-holder. Purchases are made and paid for directly at each stall, with no central FTS checkout.

Most stallholders accept card and/or cash, however payment methods vary between vendors, so we recommend having both available.

Bring along a reusable shopping bag or tote to carry your finds throughout the day. FTS tote bags will also be available to purchase at the merch desk at selected events.

BEAUTY, SERVICES & ACTIVATIONS

Alongside shopping, FTS events feature a rotating line-up of free and paid beauty, fashion and creative experiences.

Depending on the city, these may include nails, hair styling, barbering, tattoos, henna, permanent jewellery, piercings, tooth gems, grillz, tarot, brows and lashes, colour analysis, fashion illustration, records, kilo sales, clothes swaps and more.

Activations vary between events, with confirmed experiences announced via our social media and event updates.

Free services have limited availability and operate on a first-come, first-served basis, with sign-ups on the day. Paid services are operated independently, with pricing set by each provider.

TICKETS & SESSION TIMES

General Admission - $15

Entry is staggered across capped sessions and popular sessions may sell out, so we recommend booking your preferred entry time in advance.

Student Tickets - $12
Available to students aged 12+ with valid student ID.

Kids 12 & under - FREE
Free entry all day.

Companion Card holders - FREE
Free entry with a valid Companion Card.

Pension & Government Concession Card holders - $5
Valid card required.

Seniors 65+ - $5

FREE AFTERNOON ENTRY

2pm - 4pm 

The final two hours of the event are free to attend, however a free ticket must still be secured through Moshtix in advance to guarantee your spot. Free-session tickets are capped and subject to availability.

MORE INFO

Follow @fashionthriftsociety on Instagram, TikTok and Facebook for event announcements, confirmed activations, vendor previews and updates.

Visit fashionthriftsociety.com.au for more information, upcoming tour dates and everything FTS.

Celebrating your birthday on the day of the event? You can enter free all day - just purchase the free birthday ticket type and show valid ID at the door.

Please note: Photography and filming take place at FTS events and may be used by Fashion Thrift Society and its partners for promotional, social media and advertising purposes. If you do not wish to be photographed or filmed, please let an FTS team member know on arrival.
